End.text: I will make sure your donation is shared fairly.

EndAlt1.text: My church seems so empty all of a sudden. Whatever did you tell them, Mercenaries?

EndAlt2.text:
Ah, no matter.
Now I can get back to my prayers without worrying that those devotees will starve to death.
Please take as my thanks.

BanditEnd.text: By Saint Jeru! What did you bring me, Mercenaries?

line0.text: Prevent the faithful from starving to death.

Start.text: We must do penance, Mercenaries.

Next1.text: This past Festival of Light, we sold our sheep for more than they were worth. Taking advantage of gullible people is a terrible sin!

line0.props.tipText: Suggest the farmers make amends.

Convinced.text:
You're right. Donating a sheep as penance should be enough.
Let’s go, son. Without us, Drombach will starve to death.

Start.text:
Oh God of Light!
Oh heavenly Eye!
Hear our prayers and forgive us for straying from the righteous path.
Turn your wrath away from those who repent.

Next1.text:
If you spare us,
we will free our slaves from their chains.
We will shore up our mines securely.
We will pay our workers an honest wage.

line0.props.tipText: Convince the mine owners to make good on their promises right away.

Convinced.text:
Well... so be it!
We'll prove to the God of Light how strong our faith is. With intentions so pure, we should be safe from His wrath.

Start.text: The God of Light is after us! I feel like His gaze is constantly upon us since we performed The Green Night of the Tules!

line0.props.tipText: Convince the jugglers to dedicate their art to the God of Light.

Convinced.text:
Really? You think the God of Light would forgive us if we performed holy plays?
I guess it could work... Yes. It has to work!

Start.text:
Oh joy!
Oh happiness!
We did it! I can feel the Eye’s forgiveness blessing my soul.

Next1.text:
Thank you, Mercenaries! Here’s something my former comrades and I obtained through nefarious means.
I don’t want it anymore!

End.text: I'll talk to the priestess! I bet she’ll be happy to see me!

Note.text: <narrator>For increased efficiency, place four traps in a tight square.</narrator>
<narrator>The upper row must have two keys.</narrator>
<narrator>Warning: Do not place any note around the treasure.</narrator>
<narrator>An Eye key must be placed next to the treasure.</narrator>
<narrator>Fill a whole row with traps to greatly increase the chance that would-be thieves will be injured.</narrator>
<narrator>Place a first booby-trapped sword chest over an Eye key and a second one over another Eye key.</narrator>

<narrator>Do not write instructions yourselves.
These notes were successfully tested on the best thieves of Grinmeer's jail and can be used to find your treasure while resisting looters.
</narrator>
<narrator>Place 2 booby-trapped sword chests around the treasure's key.</narrator>

Start.text:
You would steal Saint Serene's treasure?
Have you no honour, Mercenaries?

Bribe1.text: That's a lot of Krowns you're offering, Mercenaries. It's worth considering...

Bribe2.text:
Fine! We're taking the gold.
Now get lost!

Start.text: Without a trade route, the only things I can sell are local products. Goods that come from afar tend to rot along the way.

Next1.text:
Are you looking for exotic wares? Then you won't be disappointed, Mercenaries!
Thanks to the Trade Routes you opened, I can now sell you everything you might need.

Start.text: The result is quite satisfying, don’t you think, Mercenaries?

Next1.text:
Everything is ready for your convenience: a chest to store unneeded items, and stools for Companions who are... also unneeded.
As for me, I will arrange journeys from one Travel Post to another.

Next2.text: Is there somewhere you would like to go?

line0.props.disableReason: Build Travel Posts in other villages to get there quickly.

line0.text: Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your first Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your second Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your third Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fourth Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fifth Trade Route.

Start.text: A small ramshackle house stood here before it fell to the Eye’s Reckoning.

Next1.text:
It would be a shame to leave this land unused. Would you like to invest, Mercenaries?
Wouldn’t it be great to have a Travel Post to journey quickly from one place to another?

line0.props.tipText: Build the Drombach Travel Post.

Build.text: Stay here, I'll let the craftsmen know!

Start.text:
Make sure to close the door behind you.
Those nosy Inquisitors are everywhere.

Alt.text: The Inquisitors may be gone, but that doesn't mean you can leave the blasted door wide open!

Repair.text: Your equipment should still last a while.

Start.text:
You’re Mercenaries?
Then follow me, I need to talk to you away from prying ears.

End1.text: So? Any news about our innkeeper?

End2.text: By Saint Eleor, not here! Meet me outside, quickly.

InquisitionEnd.text: I regret asking Mercenaries for help.

MissionDesc.text: Investigate Valiant Tower to find the New-Asthel innkeeper.

line0.text: Take on Lady Mayoress Gerslind’s mission.

line1.text: Find out what happened to the New-Asthel innkeeper.

Start.text: My customers are so scared of being questioned by the Inquisition that they fled the market!

Next1.text:
Thieves have came back since the Inquisitors left.
By the Eye, we just can't catch a break!

Start.text: I was drinking in the tavern when the Eye’s Reckoning struck. Sobered me up real quick.

Next1.text:
The God of Light is gone?
This calls for a celebration at the tavern!

Start.text: I'll head south as soon as I sell my wares, away from those heretics and this cursed county!
We’re tasked with finding the heathens who angered the God of Light and drew His Reckoning onto the county.

Next1.text: While we’re at it, we’re also checking this market’s morality.

Start.text: People are talking about you in... less respectable circles, you know? You've got a certain reputation with our kind... Want to see “the lair”? But if you want to get in, you've got to be known to the authorities, if you catch my drift...

GoOk.text: We criminals need to stick together. Put these bags over your heads and follow me – I'll take you to the lair.

GoNo.text: Sorry, lads, but you're too squeaky clean to get in. We're all in the same boat here, right? So if you haven't got a bounty on you, you've no need for us.

RewardQuest.text: You've finished one of the jobs? We won't bother going all the way over there – here's your reward.

Start.text: Drombach County is in turmoil because of the Eye’s Reckoning. There are plenty of missions to be found, if you know who to ask.

Done.text: I would have made the same choice.

line0.props.tipText: The Iron Hoof Stables were destroyed by the Eye’s Reckoning. There might still be survivors inside.

line1.props.tipText: Apparently, the Lady Mayoress of New-Asthel approached several mercenary groups discreetly.

line2.props.tipText: The Scholars at the Sophy Adr Alazar Laboratory want to further their research, but it appears that they would rather avoid the Inquisition’s scrutiny.

line3.props.tipText: Prince Aerald Adr Alazar is looking for a Troop of experienced and reliable mercenaries for an important mission in the mountains of Alazar.

Stables.text: The Iron Hoof Stables were destroyed by the Eye’s Reckoning. There might still be survivors inside.

Taverner.text: Apparently, the Lady Mayoress of New-Asthel approached several mercenary groups discreetly.

Laboratory.text: The Scholars at the Sophy Adr Alazar Laboratory want to further their research, but it appears that they would rather avoid the Inquisition’s scrutiny.

Prince.text: Prince Aerald Adr Alazar is looking for a Troop of experienced and reliable mercenaries for an important mission in the mountains of Alazar.

DeliverMission1.text:
<narrator>The informant doesn't look happy.</narrator>
I thought it would take longer. Thanks anyway.

End.text: Apologies, but I have nothing for you.

PathCrime1.text: Seeing how easily you dealt with a certain security system, the Informants deemed it inefficient. Still, it appears to have piqued the Scholars' interest in spite of its flaws.

PathCrime2.text: A group of savants decided to buy the system from its inventor in order to perfect it using their Knowledge. I hope you are up to the challenge.

PathCrime3.text: There are precious few Scholars who are competent enough to tackle such a complex matter. You should have no trouble finding them.

PathCrimeEnd1.text:
The shamed inventor left for Belerion. As for the Scholars, they were expelled from their University for losing the dean's treasure.
The mission was a success, Mercenaries.

PathCrimeEnd2.text:
The Informants have always held you in high regard, but I have to say that you really went above and beyond.
On behalf of my colleagues, I thank you.

line0.text: Buy the Scholar's Key from the Informant.

line1.text: Find and thwart the security system matching the Scholar's Key.

Start.text: Honestly, I liked it better when my master was hiding in the mountain.

I don’t know if I'm allowed to rent rooms or sell my master’s recipe.
I'm just watching the Tern’s Nest while he’s away.

I got my freedom back after my former master was branded a heretic by the Inquisition.
Lucky break for me...
People are giving me dirty looks, the Lady Mayoress piled a bunch of new instructions on me... I wonder what’s going on.

Next1.text: I'm the new owner of this tavern! Lady Mayoress Gerslind told me so herself!

Start.text: It’s good to see things return to normal.
I can heal any injury, but frostbite is my speciality!

Done.text: Don’t forget to make regular stops on your trip. Frostbite is always a risk when it gets this cold.

Start.text: I'm warning you: if you’re with the Inquisition, I won't even repair your boots.

Repair.text: Sorry for the cold welcome. I'm nervous with those zealots around.

Alt.text: They say the Inquisition is gone... Is it true?

Start.text: My horse froze to death last week. I’ll leave with the next caravan travelling through the village.
No one can make me serve Inquisitors. Not even the Prince.

Alt.text: We haven’t seen the Inquisition around here for a while. Do you know why?

Start.text: A shop's prestige is defined not by how many customers it has, but by their quality. Our merchandise is exclusively for fighters skilled enough to defeat our champion.

Alt.text:
Step right up! Don't be shy!
You'll love our selection!

Start.text:
I hope you weren't expecting to fight in front of a roaring crowd.
The Weald alone was already enough to keep a fair number of spectators from getting here alive, so now with the lycanthropes…

NoBeginArena.text: In any case, we don't have a lot of folks in the stands today.

OnLeaveArena.text:
Are you sure?
Too bad, the crowd was just getting warmed up.

Completed.text:
By Saint Jeru! What a victory!
Anyone who was too scared to come will be kicking themselves!
You've more than earned the right to wield our champion's weapon!

ArenaLost.text:
Don't be ashamed for having lost.
I've never seen the place this empty. No one will remember what happened.

ArenaDiff.text:
Fight again?
Well, of course, you can!
By Saint Jeru, if I'd known you'd be back, I'd have sent for a town crier from Hosberg!

line0.props.tipText: Replay the Arena in Hard Mode.

CompletedDiff1.text:
That was incredible, Mercenaries!
When we tell the villagers about your fight tonight, they'll turn up in droves next time!

CompletedDiff2.text: I hope you like your reward! We had to dig into the funds we normally donate to charity in order to give you these Krowns.

CompletedDiff3.text: We won't be able to fork out next time – it might hurt the arena's reputation.

ArenaAgain.text:
How wonderful of you to come! The crowds love to see warriors facing off for a good cause.
Today, all of our profits will be donated to Sommer's Refuge and the victims of the Weald.

line0.props.tipText: Replay the Arena in Hard Mode.

CompletedAgain.text:
Our previous champion won't believe her eyes!
The show you put on for the folks here has made them especially generous!

Start.text: The imprisoned soldiers all have the same dead-eyed stare.

Next1.text: The corpses are starting to rot.

Start.text:
The others have gone prowling around the prison to see if they can find Raffi.
I hope they don't try to go in themselves.

Next1.text: Where have they taken Raffi? What have they done with him?

Start.text:
The interrogation isn't making much progress.
Had any more luck with that key?

Next1.text:
I strangled the Guards you captured.
It wasn't revenge, it was punishment.
How could they do nothing while the Count tortured my men?

Start.text: After all that, Therius said I could stay. To replace Raffi, he said.

Next1.text: Not to sound ungrateful, but it wasn't a good idea. I can tell I don't measure up to their old comrade.

Next2.text: So if there's room in your company, I wouldn't mind changing careers. If you know what I mean...

Start.text: Did the Guards tell you about the monsters? It seems they come out of the Weald at night and attack anyone who's unlucky enough to cross their path.

Next1.text: Some of them are even venturing onto farms and devouring entire families!

Next2.text: I want to turn back!

Start.text:
What are we going to do if we can't go to Rigel?
The Eye's Reckoning has destroyed our farm!
I was the best patrolman in the Guard! All the Bandits in Rigel shuddered at the sound of my name!

Next1.text:
Those cowards in the capital sent me out here to freeze to death! They keep all the best posts for themselves!
Cursed be the Knights!

Start.text:
This gate must remain closed! Any peasant caught crossing the border without authorisation will be hung on the spot.
Count Karl Adr Hosberg won't let those monsters expand their reach outside of Rigel!
Don't listen to the rumours about Rigel. The situation is much worse than they're saying.

Next1.text: With all those monsters about, neither the Guards nor the Knights have time to worry about lost travellers in the Weald. Once you're in the forest, you'll only have your Lantern to rely on.

Start.text:
Your Companions retch and gag at the sight of a severed leg... all that remains of the occupants of this camp.
Paw prints lead off to the west.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the camp for clues about the lycanthropes.

MissionDesc2.text: Follow the lycanthropes' trail.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: The people of Munden are distrustful of woodcutters. They say that the Weald is turning people into lycanthropes because we cut too much wood!

Next1.text:
Bah! What should I do instead?
I've got my own family to feed!

Start.text: You? Assistants to the Head Surgeon of Alazar? Ha! He really got you, Mercenaries. I don't suppose he even bothered to explain what a graft is, did he?

Next1.text: The lycanthropes' organs have certain anomalies. Things you'd expect to find in the Weald rather than inside an animal. Revolting stuff, but the Head Surgeon claims they're the key to understanding this scourge.

Next2.text: So sample away, my dear assistants! As soon as you find a lycanthrope!

Accept.text: These creatures are anything but stupid. The disease doesn't seem to affect their intellect. The clues they leave behind are few and far between. See for yourself.

Track.text:
You've got a keen eye. I almost regret turning you over to the Head Surgeon. Perhaps I would have done better to keep you with me.
Lead the way, Mercenaries, and we will follow.

Start.text: How did they manage to kill this man?! We were right over there!

The Count claims that the Weald has a will of its own, and that it's the forest itself that has cursed Rigel.
A belief that's both heretical and irrational.

MissionDesc1.text: Question the Count and bring him along with you.

MissionDesc2.text: Find Captain Osweld and the King's Knights.

MissionDesc2Bis.text: Bring ::vars.amount::Lycanthrope Bile to the Head Surgeon.

MissionDesc3.text: Use the Head Surgeon's Field Laboratory.

MissionEnd.text: Unmask the original lycanthrope, who is hiding somewhere in Rigel.

line0.text: Take on Head Surgeon Magnus's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line0.text: Take on Captain Osweld's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: There's an impressive number of stills and test tubes here.

What's going on, Mercenaries?
Why on earth is the Count travelling with you?

Next1.text:
What did you say?
He created… what?!

End1.text: All right. I've heard enough.

End2.text:
If all we have to do to stop the scourge of lycanthropy and win back the capital honourably is to flush out this original monster, I can commit a few of my men to the effort.
Can I count you among our number, Mercenaries?

End3.text: Whoever unmasks the lycanthrope first will alert the others. We can't run the risk of letting it escape. So we'll attack it together.

End4.text:
In my boundless generosity, and also because he annoys me nearly as much as the Head Surgeon, I'll let you take the Count along with you.
I'll look over his notes on how to flush the creature out, and let you have the pleasure of questioning him.

Start.text: My dear assistants! Ah! I knew you'd unearth something interesting!

Next1.text: Although I wouldn't have guessed you'd find the Count to be a traitor.

Start.text:
…so even though, yes, I am the one behind this scourge, I can also be the one to heal it!
In fact, that's exactly what I was doing when your Mercenaries interrupted me…

Next1.text:
The Count is lying! He must take us for fools!
I've just read his notes, Captain! And his remedy is anything but complete! He's missing a key ingredient!

Next2.text:
I'm growing weary of your secrets and lies, Hosberg.
I order you, explain yourself! What's the Head Surgeon talking about?

Next3.text: It… That ingredient's not easy to obtain! But I had every intention of asking you for help, Captain. It's true! Really I did!

Next4.text: It's the heart of the original lycanthrope. My test subject… The one who ran away and spread this disease. With the graft it contains, I can create a concoction that will reverse the process of lycanthropic transformation.

Next5.text: But I don't know where he's hiding! My loyal Igor tried his best to find him, and I even sent soldiers out on his trail, but all in vain!

Next6.text: He must be in Rigel! The Mercenaries can tell you themselves! The lycanthropes are obeying a leader! He must be close by!

Start.text:
What?
Do you suppose that my distaste for you would prevent me from meeting my responsibilities?
If that's what you think, then you don't know me at all. I intend to tell you everything.

Next1.text: The reason my soldiers were unable to get their hands on him is simple: he's hiding among the rabble in his human form.

Next2.text: When Igor first brought him to me, he was a bandit. But our monster is a clever one: he must have switched to a profession less likely to draw attention.

Next2Bis.text:
Lastly, there's his scent.
The elixir I used on him oozed from every pore on his body. If you have a bloodhound, you'll have no problem finding him.

Next3.text: Once your suspicions have settled on one of Rigel's residents, simply point him out to me. I'll observe him discreetly and let you know if he's my test subject.

Next4.text:
Yes, that should work…
In the meantime, it's better I keep my distance to make sure he doesn't recognise me before I've identified him. I'll be in your camp if you need me.

Start.text:
Your connection with the Head Surgeon is really touching.
I've never seen him be this friendly with anyone. Even His Majesty can't stand him.
I can't wait to see what sort of sentence the Knights mete out for the Count! I hope it will be just punishment for his crimes!

End1.text:
What? Why is he still alive?
Mercenaries! You told me I could trust you, and you're just taking him on a tour of the County?

End2.text:
The man created lycanthropy! He's sullied Tules' Rock with the blood of innocent creatures!
We can make the remedy without him! He must die!

Start.text: The Count had better tell us everything he knows! His life and my honour depend on that remedy! So for his sake, it had better be real!

End1.text: Captain Osweld has personally congratulated me for convincing you to spare the Count. I hope the Trackers' accidental death won't be mentioned in his report to His Majesty.

Start.text:
Listen, at any other time, I'd love to sit and talk. I love hearing Mercenaries' tales.
But we've just lost another patrol! And that means we've also lost a Lantern!

Next1.text: Captain Osweld has asked me to make a Lantern for you. Apparently you're part of our auxiliary forces? Congratulations!

Next2.text: I'll do my best, but don't expect any miracles. This type of item is difficult to forge. I'll need a bit of time before you can go off and explore the Weald.

Call.text: Mercenaries! Don't leave without your Lantern!

End1.text: I thought you were about to leave without your Lantern! After all the time I spent making it, there's no way I'd let you go into the Weald without it!

End2.text: I took the liberty of adding a few doses of Lantern Oil. I heard you'd learned to make it yourselves, so this is my little way of wishing you good luck!

Wait.text: Every time a patrol disappears in the Weald, that's one less Lantern for the Knights. I'm constantly making more, but they're disappearing faster than I can forge them!

Start.text: What have you got there? Are those from Captain Osweld? Well, don't just stand there, give them to me, by Saint Jeru! These grafts must be intact if I'm going to get anything out of them!

Next1.text:
Is that all?
What do you expect me to learn from a punctured eyeball and half a spleen?
Does Captain Osweld think I'm Sophy Adr Alazar?

Next2.text: This County is driving me mad, Mercenaries. I can feel myself sinking into despair! I can't even figure out the connection between this Eye-forsaken Weald and the lycanthropes! Everyone in Rigel will turn or be devoured, and this scourge will spread all the way to the capital!

Next3.text: I don't care that you never went to university, I'm officially appointing you as my surgical assistants! Go back to that idiot captain and tell him not to go anywhere near the lycanthrope carcasses. No, you will be collecting their grafts instead!

Next4.text: Off with you, then! My research can't wait! Until I figure out where lycanthropy comes from, this disease will continue to spread – no matter how thoroughly the King's Knights tear up the County.

Wait.text: Have you brought back the grafts I asked for? Oh, come on! They're not that hard to find! Cut into the lycanthropes' organs and take whatever looks abnormal! The County of Rigel is dying! Hurry!

Final2.text: Hmph. Even a Harag barber would have done a better job. Was the lycanthrope still squirming when you pulled out its gall bladder?

Final3.text:
Bah! No matter, Captain Osweld was even worse than you.
Have your Apothecary set up a workstation in my lab. I'll show them what a real Scholar can extract from these grafts, despite his assistants' incompetence.

Study1.text: Yes, this certainly confirms that there's a link between the Weald and lycanthropy. It's very clear, but… Is that all? Really everything?

Study2.text:
Oh, the Beast take me! Let it take this whole blasted County and its monstrous inhabitants!
We should have burned down that forest and executed all the villagers…

Study3.text:
…No. I mustn't give up. His Majesty has put his trust in me.
We can only keep moving forward… And besides, you can kill lycanthropes and extract the grafts yourselves. If I gave you the plans for my laboratory, you could even do your own research…

Study5.text:
Well then, I'm counting on you, dear assistants!
Scour the entire County and study everything you can find. By combining our efforts, we'll find the source of this disease and put an end to it. Our success will be every bit as important as Sophy Adr Alazar's!

Study6.text:
Have you learnt anything useful?
Slaughtering lycanthropes won't be enough to eradicate this scourge. We must study them!

NoIntro.text:
Do I look like I want to talk to a bunch of lowly Mercenaries?
Let me work, or I'll kick you out myself!

SettingLog2.text: You gave the Head Surgeon the grafts he needs for his experiments.

SettingLog3.text: You agreed to help the Head Surgeon in his research efforts.

Start.text:
The Head Surgeon is the King of Alazar's personal physician.
Even so, it's hard to say if he was sent here for his skill, or because His Majesty wanted to get rid of him.

Bah! Everyone at court knows that Count Adr Hosberg is incompetent.
If he'd called on His Majesty the King a little earlier, Rigel wouldn't be in such a state!
It'd be easier if you would let me out of this cage!

Next1.text: I'd rather die, my Lord.

Start.text: The efforts of the Head Surgeon and the Count are starting to pay off. Unfortunately, preparing remedies for everyone in Rigel will be long work indeed.

Next1.text: You can't imagine how eager I am to return to the capital and get away from those idiots.

Start.text:
<narrator>The books in this library are almost all covered in mildew.
A yellowed letter is shoved in beneath one of them.</narrator>

Next1.text: Dear Cousin, I am sorry to hear that the treatment provided was not more successful. I understand your indignation, and regret that I cannot do more to bring you relief.

Next2.text: Alas, my research on the Plague is still faltering. I'm afraid that the effects of this remedy may not be permanent. I beg you to believe that they are still better than the madness that would have befallen you.

Next3.text: I hope you find some consolation in knowing that your failed experiment was of great help to me in developing a more effective remedy. With all my affection, Sophy Adr Alazar.

Start.text: I wouldn't touch that if I were you.

Next0.text:
Please excuse my sentimental side, Mercenaries.
That spear belonged to me when I was still fighting for the Northern Kingdom. It's very dear to me, and I have no intention of letting it go.

Next1.text: So now that this little misunderstanding has been cleared up, may I please ask you to leave and never come back to disturb my peace and quiet?

Next2.text: Your insistence on picking up that weapon borders on rudeness. Please leave my home.

line0.text: Cut back the brambles to free the door.

line1.text: Open the castle door with an Ornate Key

line0.text: Acquire Adelbarth Adr Alazar's weapon.

Start.text:
A cart with muddy wheels.
There are jars in the back, filled with some sort of black blood.
Parts of this man's innards have been replaced with animal organs…

Welcome to Sommer's Refuge.
If you have a Companion to leave with us, know that we will welcome them without asking for anything in return.
All those who have lost their minds in the Weald are part of my family.

Next1.text:
That said, with the arena profits that normally provide our funding at an all-time low, we'd be very happy to receive any donation you'd like to make, no matter how modest.
Unless...

Next2.text: You're fighters, aren't you? Could you fight in the arena for us? It would be an excellent way to remind our patrons that we need their generosity, now more than ever.

Next3.text: In exchange, I could teach you my old techniques... the ones I used when I was a champion myself.

End1.text:
I've been told we have you to thank for the arena rising from the ashes.
Is that true? Was it your feats that brought the crowds back?

End1Bis.text:
It's wonderful – the spectators' donations will start flowing in again!
Our refuge will finally be able to pay off its debts.

End2.text: Words cannot express how grateful I am. Ever since I retired from my career as a champion, caring for the sick has been my sole purpose in life.

End3.text: The doors to this refuge will always be open to you. I won't leave any of your Companions behind.

Start.text:
No one can heal after losing their mind in the Weald.
Just look at poor Sommer: Alix found her in the middle of the forest five years ago, and the poor wretch still thinks she's there.
These poor people are nothing more than empty shells. I cannot bear look at them.
The Brotherhood doesn't normally give credit, but this is different.

Next1.text: Anyone can get lost in the Weald... and we fear we may need this refuge ourselves one day. So the bosses are a bit more lenient.

Start.text: As long as I stay close to the light, I'm real...
The sick seem to be sleeping fitfully.

line0.title: Green Hell
line0.props.helpTip: Provide Scholar Jürgen with ::vars.amount:: Lantern Oil.

Start.text: I don't understand why people living at the edge of a haunted forest are so afraid of lycanthropes. There's a lot worse in the Weald!
Yes, it's all my fault. As always.

Next1.text:
Am I the one who put that blasted root there, too?
You think maybe I tripped over it on purpose?

Next2.text: Or maybe they shouldn't have made me carry the whole supply of fuel! This fiasco is their responsibility.

Start.text: AAAAAAAAAAAH!

Next1.text: Oh! By all the saints! You scared the life out of me! I thought you were a monster from the Weald, or a lycanthrope!

Next2.text: We've been stuck on this farm for two days. As soon as we set foot outside, the Madness comes rushing down on us. And the worst part is, I think the Weald is starting to creep in under the door...

Next3.text: Would you be willing to share a bit of your fuel with us in exchange for this map? It was meant to lead our expedition to the treasure of Adelbarth Adr Alazar, the reclusive prince. But given the choice, I'd honestly just rather get home alive.

Start.text:
Oh! Blessed be the Eye! Thank you!
Saint Eleor's blessings be upon you!
We'll finally be able to get out of this hell.

Next1.text: I hope you find that treasure, Mercenaries. As for me, I'm heading back to the capital!

MissionDesc1.text: Bring 10 Hemp, 10 Wood or 10 Sandstone to Gertrud.

MissionDesc2.text: Rest at the farm and wait for the lycanthropes to arrive.

MissionDesc3.text: Claim your reward from Gertrud.

line0.text: Take on Gertrud's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Rest while waiting for the fight?

I refuse to leave! This Sawmill is my home!
My great-grandparents built it with their own hands! My parents taught me the profession here! And how will my sons make a living if they run off somewhere else?

Next1.text: The Guards won't protect us! They claim it's all our fault! They say the lycanthropes are attacking Rigel because of the harm we do to the Weald! We're so utterly alone!

Next2.text:
Oh! By Saint Jeru, I'd rather die than leave! These monsters can attack my house all they want, I'll still keep fighting! They'll tire before I do!
All I need is a little help!

Start.text:
You… You'll do it? I can't believe it!
Praised be Saint Eleor for sending you!

Next1.text:
I don't know where to begin…
Maybe you could give my sons a hand? They're building barricades where the lycanthropes have already struck.

Next2.text:
Their attacks are becoming more and more aggressive, and we're even starting to run short on wood to protect ourselves!
Any material will do the job, we're not picky!

Next3.text:
It's better than nothing, believe me.
Besides, my boys are quite resourceful. They'll find a use for it.

Next4.text:
I… I've prepared some beds for you. In case you decide to stay when the lycanthropes attack.
If the Count is right, and the Weald really is angry with us…

Next6.text: Oh, please, I'm begging you! Stay a little longer. Just to be sure the lycanthropes don't enter the Sawmill!

SettingLog1.text: You helped Gertrud to barricade the Sawmill.

Attack1.text: They're here! The lycanthropes are just on the other side of the window!

End1.text: Oh! By Saint Jeru! Oh! By Saint Eleor! We should have left!

End2.text:
All those creatures… They were so close to us! So hungry…!
If you hadn't been there…
The next time…

End3.text: I've made my decision. We're leaving! It's too dangerous! The Weald wants us dead! The Weald itself, do you understand?!

End4.text:
I'll never cut another twig as long as I live! I swear it!
I'll take my sons with me and head to Hosberg. Even if we have to become beggars, at least we'll be living beggars!

SettingLog2.text: The lycanthropes' attack has convinced Gertrud and her sons to seek refuge in the city.

Start.text: I've tried everything to get Gertrud and her sons to leave, but that old hag's head is harder than the wood she cuts!

Next1.text:
Count Adr Hosberg has forbidden us to protect the Sawmills and the Woodcutters' camps. His scholars believe that they're the ones causing the Weald's wrath and the lycanthropes.
The best I can do is convince them to leave!

End.text:
Why are you encouraging them?
Are you all going to die for this stupid Sawmill?

Start.text:
Do you think we'll be welcomed in Hosberg?
They think it's our fault that the lycanthropes are eating people!
I won't… give up… my… home!
I… I nearly died!
Stay back! I'm sure I saw you get bitten!

MissionDesc1.text: Inspect the area.

MissionDesc2.text: Kill Roselind's murderers.

MissionDesc3.text: Talk to Sisbert to claim your reward.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text:
It looks like our meal has arrived!
Perfect timing, this prey was a bit scrawny…

Next1.text: Sisbert?

Start.text: This mutilated corpse is all that's left of the most beautiful woman in Hosberg.
How did you find us? We crossed the river twice. You should have lost our trail ages ago!

Next1.text: Did you really think one puny river would stop me? I didn't lose my brain when I turned!

Next1Bis.text:
My prey and my territory belong to me! I forbade you to hunt here!
Kidnapping that woman was a declaration of war!

Next2.text: Damn it, Sisbert! What will it take for you to understand the rules of the pack? The prey belongs to everyone, we have to share it! Chief's orders!

Next3.text:
I'm not part of the pack.
I don't follow your rules.
And I don't recognise the putrid creature you call your chief. If he needs to be taught a lesson, I'm more than willing to do it!

Next4.text:
Mercenaries!
You can't let this poor woman's murder go unpunished! Those creatures know no limits! They're dangerous to every living creature in Rigel!

Start.text: Well, then! I suppose I can stop playing the tearful fiancé now.

Next1.text: Thank you for helping me avenge Roselind's death. Not being able to devour her myself enraged me so, that I nearly transformed in front of witnesses a number of times. Weeks of effort were nearly ruined because of those animals!

Next2.text: You can't imagine how difficult it is for me to mimic my old human habits. Ever since I was bitten, even one mouthful of bread is enough to make me sick. Although I'd still rather eat a whole bakery than join that pack of degenerates...

Next3.text: Anyway! Now that that's taken care of, I can go back to Hosberg and go about my business. Thank you for your help, and please be so kind as to avoid mentioning my true nature to the villagers.

Recruit1.text: I suppose I knew you wouldn't let me leave that easily.

Recruit2.text: Why should we fight? Haven't I proven that I'm a civilised lycanthrope?

Refuse.text: Well, if you're so worried about Hosberg's safety, maybe we could team up? I refuse to be part of their pack, but yours is a different matter entirely. If I join you, the humans will see me as just another Mercenary, and I'll be happy to eat the corpses of your enemies as my meagre pay.

SettingLog.text: You helped a lone lycanthrope to defend his territory.

MissionDesc1.text: Place your trust in the Trackers or in the King's Knights.

MissionDescTrackers1.text: Talk to Tracker Morrigan to receive your reward.

MissionDescRoyal1.text: Talk to the sergeant of the King's Knights to receive your reward.

MissionDesc2.text: Search the area for clues.

MissionDescTrackers2.text: Report your findings to Tracker Morrigan.

MissionDescRoyal2.text: Report your findings to the sergeant of the King's Knights.

MissionDescRoyal3.text: Take on the mission from the sergeant of the King's Knights.

MissionDesc3.text: Follow the cart tracks.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: The rotting carcass of a pig. This poor animal has been dead much longer than the others.
There's not a single drop of blood left in this animal's carcass.
Whoever killed this wolf wasn't after its pelt or its meat.
The animal's throat has been cut, but your Companions don't see any sign of blood nearby.
It's a sacrilege! This place has been sullied with blood!

Next0.text:
It's even worse than I thought! Rigel has dared insult the Tules in their own territory!
An appeasement ritual won't do any good as long as those behind this massacre still live!

Next1.text: You want to save the people of this godless County? Then help us track down these blasphemers!

Wait.text: Let's inspect the corpses! We need to understand what happened here!

Next2Bis.text:
Oh! Damn it!
Those cursed Knights!…
I thought for sure you'd turn on us, Mercenaries.

Next3.text: I swear to you, our intentions were sincere! We never meant to trap you! You were meant to bear witness to the magic of the Tules…

Next3Bis.text: And you will! Once we've found whoever did this, you'll see how we appease the little gods' anger.

Next4.text: Those heathens must have left some traces. Let's find them, Mercenaries!

Chariot.text:
Cart tracks!
They're sure to lead us to the blasphemers! Let's hurry!

Start.text: These beasts aren't just dead; they've been bled dry.
How could anyone do such a thing? Right here at Tules' Rock! This is madness!

End.text:
By the Tules!
I'm not used to fighting humans any more!

Start.text: So those Trackers weren't lycanthropes bent on turning you. But they did perform a demonic ritual!

Next0.text:
We're in one of their so-called sacred places, surrounded by sacrificed animals!
So they're still guilty of summoning lycanthropy! … Or something along those lines.

Next1.text: Let's gather some evidence. If a war's to be declared, it must be based on strong foundations.

Next2.text: Be quick about it, I feel I'm being watched by hundreds of little eyes.

Chariot.text:
Cart tracks? By Saint Eleor! Since when do those Harag savages use carts?
And why would they need them…

End2.text:
Well!
It looks like this was all an unfortunate misunderstanding. Apparently, we're dealing with a simple case of poaching.
The ruffians who did this are responsible for this mistake.
Find them – Captain Osweld will need a scapegoat for our actions.

Accept.text:
Be smart about it. Killing Trackers without a valid reason could draw the ire of Harag's clans.
I'll present this to the captain in the proper light whilst you go out looking for them.

Start.text: I'm glad it's you handling the carcasses. These gloves cost me a fortune!

By Saint Eleor!
These savages are tough!

How dare you accuse us of being lycanthropes?
It was your people who did that!

Next1.text: Our people? Was it our people who lured the Mercenaries out to the middle of nowhere, with no witnesses for miles? What were you planning to do next? Turn them into monsters too?

Next2.text:
I… What?
No!

Next3.text:
Admit it! You wanted to get rid of the Head Surgeon's assistants before they discovered the truth!
Lucky for them, Captain Osweld ordered us to keep an eye on their Troop!

Next4.text:
In the name of His Majesty, King Wilburt Adr Alazar, I order you to lay down your weapons.
Surrender quietly and we'll grant you a painless death.

Next4bis.text:
Mercenaries, this is ridiculous!
We wanted to lift the curse…

Next5.text:
I invite you to fight by our side, Mercenaries!
You must be dying to get revenge on the men who tried to trap you!

Start.text:
Get back, Mercenaries!
Step away from those lycanthropes!

line0.text: Deliver ::vars.amount:: Rubies to Edua the Witch.

Start.text: The Weald speaks to those who listen – and it's got plenty to say! Open your ears, Mercenaries, and listen to Nature's song! Let the true voice of Rigel guide you, and you'll never get lost among the trees again!

Next1.text:
Oh! My cats tell me you fear the forest. Could they be right?
No! No! You must have turned a deaf ear to its call. You've insulted it!

Next2.text:
You poor souls!
You must reconcile! I shall help you. I know the forest well, and you'll be back on good terms in no time.

Next3.text: Seek forgiveness by offering it a gift. Something lovely, precious and beautiful. Yes, a present that will please the forest, to adorn its branches and roots.

Give1.text:
What a beautiful offering! How kind!
I'll place it on one of its beloved trees. My cats have told me which one.
It'll only take me a few minutes. Prepare to receive its gifts.

Start.text:
The Weald loves you, and has given me some gifts for you.
Which ones will you choose?
As the intercessor, I ask for only modest compensation.

Intro.text:
Yes, the leaves are quite clear: the Weald loves you. It has asked me to share its gifts with you.
I'll take any form of currency!

MissionDesc1.text: Take the Merchant back to the Rigel border crossing.

MissionDesc2.text: Talk to the Captain of the King's Knights.

line0.text: Take on the Merchant's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line0.text: Take on Captain Osweld's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text:
They're dead! Dead! Eaten alive!
Oh! Saint Jeru… those monsters…

Get me out of here! I want to return to Gosenberg!
No goods are worth such a horrid death.
My stock is all yours, if only you'll bring me to the border!
How did this creature pass itself off as a mere Merchant?

The more time passes, the bolder the lycanthropes get!
At first, they were only attacking isolated travellers, but now they've slaughtered a whole inn full of people!
Speak to us with the deference we deserve. The King's Knights are the elite of the Alazarian army, not some lowly commoners in armour like the Count's soldiers.
You can keep your thanks, and the reward that creature promised you. My Knights were simply doing their duty by defending our good people from those monsters.

Next0.text: Our Scholars call them lycanthropes. Their ability to return to human form makes them extremely difficult to track down. They can hide themselves among the common people, to devour or contaminate them, and no one suspects a thing.

Next1.text:
When His Majesty tasked our Order with exterminating those creatures, my Knights had to learn to be suspicious of everyone and everything. I urge you to do the same.
If you get bitten, you could become a lycanthrope yourself.

Next2.text: I'm giving you this advice because your men look experienced and brave. We'd welcome some support from a company like yours. The Count and his Guard have so thoroughly neglected their duties that this new scourge is now threatening Rigel's stability.

Accept.text:
Excellent!
In that case, I'll assign you a mission that we don't feel li… that we don't have the time to complete.

Accept2.text: Deliver this to the Head Surgeon waiting in our camp. But be quick about it – patience isn't one of his virtues. If he has any virtues at all.

Wait.text:
You should be praising Saint Eleor for your good fortune.
Not only have we saved your lives, we're entrusting you with a mission. What more could a Mercenary hope for?

MissionDesc2.text: Deliver the Mysterious Cargo to the Head Surgeon.

SettingLog.text: Your company survived its first encounter with a lycanthrope.

MissionDescRoyal.text: Talk to the sergeant of the King's Knights.

MissionDesc1.text: Open the door inside the Mausoleum.

MissionDesc2.text: Enter the secret passage.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Written on the sarcophagus in old-fashioned lettering is the name Adelbarth Adr Alazar.

What are we doing here, Mercenaries?
I thought the people of Alazar used this kind of place to store their dead. Why bring a cart here?

Next0Bis.text: … Where is it, anyway? I can't see it anywhere!

Next0.text:
By all the Tules! A passage!
H… How did you get the key?

Next1.text:
I see. So you found that key on the body of a man who was kidnapping prisoners...
Was he planning to sacrifice them too?

Next2.text:
The Tules protect us, I've got a bad feeling about this.
Let's move forward carefully.

Wait.text: I'll cover the rear, Mercenaries.

Start.text:
Stop giving me that shocked look.
Captain Osweld didn't even give me the time to finish my report before sending me out right behind you.

Next0.text: An unfair punishment! Those Trackers were threatening us! They could easily have been lycanthropes! We killed them to save you!

Next1.text:
But regardless, I'm now tasked with investigating a wolf blood trafficking ring.
I hope you at least know how to open this door!

Reward.text:
You had the key all along! So you're the ones who killed those wolves! You're lycanthropes!
We should have protected the Trackers from you instead!

Reward2.text:
Igor? That key belonged to a man who was kidnapping prisoners, too?
What does that have to do with our wolves being slaughtered? Are you telling me he was doing both?

Reward3.text:
I'm warning you! If this is another trap, you'll get my dagger in your back.
Go on ahead, I've got my eye on you!

Wait.text:
I'm warning you! If this is another trap, you'll get my dagger in your back.
Go on ahead, I've got my eye on you!

MissionDesc1.text: Search the area for lycanthropes.

MissionDesc2.text: Collect ::vars.amount::Lycanthrope Bile from the corpses.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: What brings you to this mine, Mercenaries?

Next1.text: I hope the people in the valley are safe. Are the lycanthropes still prowling around Munden?

Warg1.text: What brings you to this mine, Mercenaries?

Warg2.text: Oh… we left tracks in the snow, didn't we?

Start.text:
By Saint Izella!
Can't you see I'm working?

Where did you come from?
We have no need for Mercenaries.
So we'd better hurry up and kill you before the Knights arrive!
Don't expect me to get anywhere near any corpses. You're the Head Surgeon's assistants, go collect whatever you want.

End.text: I see no difference between the way my men and yours handled this task. Let's hope the Head Surgeon doesn't agree.

End1.text: Go back and deliver these grafts to him. I'd go with you, but I try to avoid talking to him more than strictly necessary. His personality is quite detestable.

MissionDesc1.text: Calm Konrad the prisoner.

MissionDesc2.text: Buy Konrad's freedom.

MissionDesc3.text: Bring Konrad to the Bandits.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: I hope you haven't come here empty-handed, Mercenaries. The Count insists that the prison always be full of outlaws. He'll even accept lycanthropes, if you happen to catch any!

Deliver.text:
Don't forget your bounty.
If you want another one, bring us any and all scoundrels you find.

NoSlotAvailable.text: By Saint Jeru, you're back already? I haven't even had time to hang all the scoundrels you brought last time! Come back in a few days and I'm sure we'll have freed up a few chains!

Raffi.text: Raffi? I don't know anyone by that name.

Start.text:
No! Let me be! I don't want to go with you! I don't want to disappear like the others!
Oh, Saint Eleor! Please help me in my hour of need!
Raffi?... Did his accomplices send you? The Beast devour me, of course, I know what happened to him! Get me out of here and I'll tell them everything!

Give1.text:
That… that's better.
Go ahead. If you just want to talk to me, I'm listening.

Give2.text: Raffi?... Did his accomplices send you? The Beast devour me, of course, I know what happened to him! Get me out of here and I'll tell them everything!

line0.title: Alazar Students
line0.props.helpTip: Make your way to the last room of the Tomb and talk to Professor Grete.

Start.text:
Welcome to the University of Alazar admission exam!
How wonderful to see that a haunted forest and a pack of lycanthropes haven't dampened your thirst for knowledge!

Next1.text: Your task is quite simple: make your way to the Ancient One's sarcophagus, then make it back here alive. That will earn you the right to study with the greatest Scholars of our time!

Next2.text: But beware! This tomb is only a test of logic – looting will not be tolerated! Participants are strictly forbidden to steal anything at all, especially the Ancient One's Treasure.

End1.text: Did you make it to the end? In that case, please describe the fresco in the last room.

End2.text:
By Saint Jeru, so it's true! You've done it!
Congratulations! Let me enter your names in the register and welcome you to our great academic family.

Thief1.text: Wait… What's that in your bag? Is that the Ancient One's Treasure?

Thief2.text: Looters! Guards! Seize these vile thieves!

Wait.text: My dear students! Do you have any questions? How can I help you?

Thief1Bis.text: Wait… What's that in your bag? Is that the Ancient One's Treasure?

Thief2Bis.text: Looters! Guards! Seize these vile thieves!

Start.text: Aren't you a bit old to become students?
I had to fail this exam twice before accepting the harsh truth: advanced studies aren't for everyone.
The door is locked.
A Scholar Companion might be able to decipher the inscriptions on this headstone.

Next1.text: Four wise men wish to open a locked door, but only one of them has the key. He's not the shortest one, but none of those adjacent to him is the tallest. Find the right wise man.

Start.text: The door is blocked on the other side.
The door is locked.
A Scholar Companion might be able to decipher the inscriptions on this headstone.

Next1.text: Three wise men wish to join forces to open a locked door. The first is the tallest, and the second is across from the shortest. The third is equidistant from the two others. Find the right three wise men.

Start.text: Within a few steps, your Companions are sure of it: they're being followed!
The door is locked.
The key to the puzzle must be on the other side…

Next1.text: My companions still haven't returned. I'm scared to think what they might have run into in the dark…

Start.text:
Greetings, fellow students.
How's your admission test going?

Next1.text: As for me, I've already found the sarcophagus room. Quite simple, really. I studied the floor plans of all the tombs that were discovered by our explorers.

Next2.text:
I could be outside, if I wanted, but I'm after the honours. And I'll graduate summa cum laude, once I can explain to the jury why the room has no ceiling.
The answer must be somewhere in this room… or elsewhere…

Wait.text: Get away! I won't let you copy my notes!

Start.text: The giant basin has gone through the floor.
Despite the nearly illegible runes, your Companions can make out a name: Belit.
The door is locked.
One of your Companions stumbles over a soft shape huddled on the ground.
The light of your torches falls on a deformed face.
The only runes your Companions manage to decipher mention danger and fragile chains. Hard to deduce much from that.
Can your Companions really be blamed for this unfortunate turn of events?
An aspiring student who will never pass her exam now.
The creepers have put an end to this young man's ambitions.

line0.text: Find the three escaped ponies in Rigel and bring them back to the stable.

Start.text: Primrose is glad to see you again.
What a greeting! Mugwort recognised you right away!
Laurel has regained some weight since you last met, and his coat is gleaming.
What's the use?

Next1.text:
My parents are dead. My ponies have run off!
Once I've finished this bottle, I'll have nothing left at all!

Start.text:
What can I do for you, my lords?
Is there anything you need? Do you wish to buy one of our animals?
Hosberg was only a few days' walk from here... it shouldn't have taken more than a day to sell that horse!

Next1.text: But that's all the time it took for the lycanthropes to devour my parents and two of our animals.

Next2.text:
I don't know where the other ponies are! The door to their stall is smashed open, so maybe they escaped…
Oh! By Saint Jeru! I'd give anything to get them back!

line0.props.tipText: Bring back the escaped horses.
line0.props.disableReason: You haven’t captured any wandering ponies.

Poney1.text:
That... That's one of our ponies!
Blessed be the Eye of Light! Thank you, Mercenaries! Thank you!

Poney2.text:
Another one? Amazing! I can't believe they both survived.
And the third one? Have you captured it as well?

PoneyEnd.text:
You must have been sent by Saint Jeru himself!
Thank you, Mercenaries!

End.text:
I can't believe everything you've done for us.
I'll never forget you.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the place with Sisbert.

MissionDesc2.text: Search the place with Sisbert.

MissionDesc3.text: Search the place with Sisbert.

MissionDesc4.text: Follow the lead that Sisbert discovered.

line0.text: Take on Sisbert's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text:
Between the lycanthropes and the Weald itself, I'm sure that Roselind is already dead.
But you can't say no to the son of a rich Lord Mayor.
I don't care what the King's Knights say! My fiancée isn't dead! She's gone missing!

Next1.text: Nothing will stop me from searching for my beloved, whether those prigs from the capital help me or not. Even if I have to spend all of my father's gold.

Next2.text: Please join the search, Mercenaries. I need as many willing helpers as I can get. The more of us there are, the faster we can save my darling from the dangers of the Weald.

Accept.text:
The Brotherhood and the volunteers from Hosberg have gone on ahead, so you're the only ones left to accompany me.
You must help, I beg of you! I'll go mad if I stay here!

Accompany.text:
Just follow me.
Thanks to the beacon, I have kept a close eye on the Weald. I have taken note of even the tiniest noises, the slightest suspicious movement of any branch. Together, we shall find my Roselind!

MissionDesc1.text: Meet up with the Trackers.

line0.text: Take on Tracker Morrigan's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: The curse that has befallen the people of Rigel is a cruel punishment! My heart goes out to them – and hunting the Ghost Pack is my way of easing their burden.

Next1.text:
I'd be happy to count you among my Trackers, as long as you promise me you'll be careful.
Day and night no longer have any meaning. Once you enter the Weald, the Pack may strike from any direction.

Accept.text: Good luck on the hunt, Mercenaries. May the Tules protect you and your men.

Wait.text: Tell your Companions to stay prepared and alert at all times. The Pack has the advantage in a forest this vast.

End.text:
So you took care of the Ghost Pack?
Mercenaries, you're even more skilled than you look. That Pack had already taken three of my best Trackers.

End2.text:
I'll inform the villages – their residents will be relieved to know they're a bit safer now.
At least, I hope so.

line0.text: Agree to join the Hunt.

line1.text: Follow instructions from the Rigel Hunt item to find and defeat the Ghost Pack.

line2.text: Report your victory to Master Tracker Avren.

Start.text: Don't expect me to offend the little gods! War paint is sacred, and simply taking part in the Hunt doesn't make you worthy of wearing it.

Next1.text: Until you and your men have been initiated in the Tules' Glade in Ludern, I refuse to paint your faces.

Tatoo1.text:
So you've been initiated in the Tules' Glade?
In that case, there's no better way to win the little gods' favour than by wearing their war paint.

Tatoo2.text: Does anyone else among your Companions want an ornament?

Start.text:
The Master Tracker should leave the people of Rigel to their fate! They deserve to be turned into monsters!
That's what happens when you offend the Tules!
I'm the one who sent you that message! I couldn't stand to see you wasting your time collecting monster parts.

Next0.text: You want to know where lycanthropy comes from? Well, I'll tell you: it's a curse!

Next1.text: Even the Count knows it! By attacking the trees with their axes and building their farms on their roots, the people of Rigel have provoked the Weald's wrath! The Tules have cast a spell on them, and no one will be able to do anything about it until a penitence ritual has been performed!

Next2.text:
Still don't believe it?
Then come with us to the heart of the Weald! You'll serve as impartial witnesses. The Knights and even the King of Alazar himself will be forced to admit the truth!

Accept.text: Tules' Rock is the most sacred place in all of Rigel! That's obviously where the curse is coming from! You'll see how people get rid of a curse when they worship the right god!

Start.text:
Last night, I was standing guard outside and I heard strange noises coming from the shed.
When I opened the door...

Next1.text:
Jertha was devouring Clauss's entrails!
Oh! How long have we been working alongside a lycanthrope?!

Start.text: I'd rather clean latrines at the Trade Palace for the rest of my life than set foot in the Weald again.

Bah! If you think one more skill will protect you from the lycanthropes or the Weald, you're even more naive than you look.
Rigel is where Mercenaries go to die!

Respec.text: If I were you, I'd go use that new knowledge somewhere else.

A2CastleBookShelf.npc.name: Kings of the North, by Oldberth of Asthel

Start.text: <narrator>…among those who ever ascended to the throne of the Northern Kingdom were three queens, two of whom served only as regents until their eldest sons came of age.</narrator>

Next1.text: <narrator>As rare as women were, illegitimate children were rarer still. Court records mention just one, Ronfulss Adr Alazar known as Ronfulss Adr Hosberg, whose legendary intelligence and agreeable demeanour convinced the Court to prefer him over his legitimate brothers. </narrator>

Next2.text: <narrator>Though his example is often cited in times of succession disputes, it must be remembered that Ronfulss was a unique case, and that the husband of a legitimate female heir was often chosen over a son of dubious ancestry. </narrator>

CampDialog.text: I suppose you've forgotten everything I've told you about the original lycanthrope?

CampDialog2.text: My theory is that the monster is disguising itself in a human form. So you're looking for a man who used to be a Bandit, but has now taken on a completely different profession… and who gives off a specific odour. An animal should have no trouble detecting it.

Start.text: The Count is very busy. He has no time to receive mere Mercenaries.

End.text:
I haven't the time to dwell on the failures of our previous Count. The castle must be ready for his successor's arrival.
His Majesty has no shortage of options among his abundant offspring.

Start.text:
Lycanthropy is a disease that comes from the Weald, it's obvious.
The forest is taking vengeance on those who have harmed it for so many years. It was bound to happen sooner or later.

Next1.text:
I've suggested several times that we appease the Weald's wrath by hanging a few woodcutters at the forest's edge.
The Count is too soft with his people. He always rejects the idea.

End.text: Why has the Count excluded me from his research? Doesn't he trust me?

Start.text:
We've sacrificed so much to contain this scourge!
I've lost track of how many of us have fallen to the lycanthropes' claws!

Next1.text:
The King's Knights act as though we just stood there with our arms crossed, watching the farmers get eaten!
Saint Eleor curse them!

End.text:
How could the Count have done this to us?
So many of our comrades have died because of him!

Start.text: Oh! I can imagine what those idlers in the capital think of our County! They hate bastards!

Next1.text: Let them laugh at our distress. We know that our Lord has tried everything to protect his people. It's an honour to serve him.

End.text: I should have suspected something when that horrible Igor character started hanging around our Count.

Start.text:
The King's Knights have relegated our soldiers to watching over the markets.
They won't be needing my services.

Repair.text: Looks like I haven't lost my touch!

Start.text: Something with superhuman strength broke free of this operating table.

MissionDesc1.text: Inspect the area.

MissionDesc2.text: Vanquish the castle guards.

MissionDesc3.text: Question the Count about this place.

MissionDesc4.text: Return the Count to the King's Knights.

Start.text: You've found Raffi…
Someone tried to transplant a wolf's organs into this man's body.
Well, it's about time! What took you so long, Igor?

Next1.text:
I hope you have what I asked of you.
…

Start.text:
You win. I surrender.
I'll talk! I'll talk!

All this is that drunkard Igor's fault!
If it weren't for his negligence, you never would have got to me. Who would have cared about a few dead wolves and a missing gang of criminals?

Next1.text: I rid my own County of its worthless dregs, for an experiment that could have finally restored Alazar to its former glory! My father would have been the most powerful ruler in the Five Kingdoms, thanks to those enhanced soldiers!

Next2.text:
But then, my most promising test subject had to escape and sow terror throughout Rigel!
How could I have known that the spores in the transfusions could spread their properties to other subjects?

Next3.text:
Don't look at me like that, I'm not a monster!
Yes! Lycanthropy was my creation!
But ever since, I haven't stopped looking for a remedy! This is my County, and it was never my intention to do it any harm.

Next4.text:
Don't expect me to just give it to you with no guarantees! I'm well aware that once you've got it, you'll immediately kill me to claim all the credit for my discovery.
I'll only hand over my remedy to the King's Knights. So take me to my father's men. It's your only option.

Start.text:
Intruders!
Guards! Come quickly!

Where are we? Has this place been hidden here, under the Count's castle the whole time?
By Saint Jeru, what are you waiting for? Interrogate him!

End0.text:
Do as he says, Mercenaries.
I can't go back to Captain Osweld without the remedy!

End1.text: I trust you. Make sure he doesn't try to escape during the journey. What he knows could be our key to finally returning to the capital.

End2.text: I'm going to gather some evidence before leaving. We'll meet you at the camp.

Start.text:
This place is insalubrious.
Hurry up and question the Count – I refuse to stay here any longer.

End1.text: Are you going to let this man live after what he just told you? He deserves to die, Mercenaries! He created a curse!

End2.text:
Very well. I trust your judgement.
You trusted us at Tules' Rock. Now it's our turn.

End3.text: We'll wait for you at the King's Knights' camp. If that man was lying, I want to be the one who makes him pay for his betrayal.

Wait.text: We'll wait for you at the King's Knights' camp. If that man was lying, I want to be the one who makes him pay for his betrayal.

Start.text:
<narrator>Dear Nephew,
It is my duty to warn you of the quagmire you have cast yourself into.</narrator>

Next1.text: <narrator>Rigel is, in many ways, a cursed County. Your predecessors led austere lives there – and, I regret to inform you, very short ones as well. By naming you to govern it, your father hopes to see you meet the same fate. </narrator>

Next2.text: <narrator>If you had any common sense, you'd go back on your decision and return to court, or go into exile in Gosenberg like so many others before you. Let the legitimate heirs fight for my brother's attention, and lead the scholarly life you deserve! </narrator>

Start.text:
A company of Mercenaries?
I had hoped that Captain Osweld himself would come out to look for us.
I've got a score to settle with that son of a crocswine.

Next1.text: But what if I killed you? And what if I devoured all the others who came after you? Maybe then our dear captain would deign to venture out here. What do you think?

Give1.text: A remedy? For lycanthropy? Does that mean Captain Osweld has completed his mission?

Give2.text: I won't let him get all the credit after what he did to us! Give me that!

Start.text: We've been wandering in this forest for so long, Mercenaries. I can't even remember what colour the sky is...

Next1.text:
We're running low on Lantern Fuel – could you spare some?
I beg of you, we'd do anything to avoid being left in the dark again!

Give1.text:
May Saint Eleor bless you for your kindness.
Ah! If only we'd met you a little earlier…

Start.text:
Don't tell me my parents sent you!
They're the ones who abandoned me in the Weald!

Next1.text:
Those liars said they wanted to go pick mushrooms as a family!
Then my father tore the Lantern out of my hands before my own mother clubbed me from behind!
When I woke up, I was lost and alone!

Next2.text:
Oh! I'll bet they suspected me of being a lycanthrope, but they were too scared of being accused themselves to turn me in! So instead, they just abandoned me in the Weald!
They must pay for what they've done, Mercenaries. I have to get back to Hosberg!

Accompagny1.text: Just take me to the market square. I know the way from there.

Start.text: You're right! I'm much better off without them! And I've got a whole pack to watch over me now!
What a fight! May Saint Eleor bear witness to our triumph!

Next1.text:
You've completed your mission, Mercenaries. When we first met, I wasn't so sure it was possible.
And to think, you could have foolishly let yourselves be eaten by that lycanthrope!

Next2.text: Don't worry about all that nonsense with the grafts. The Head Surgeon and the Count will fine-tune the remedy for lycanthropy. Soon, my Knights will be travelling all over Rigel to hand out the remedy. And woe betide anyone who refuses to drink it…

Next3.text: In a few days, the lycanthropes will be nothing but a bad memory, while your reputation will spread all the way to the capital!

Start.text: My men are all here. They're ready to attack Alor.

Next1.text:
I hope you're not mistaken – both for the Count's sake, and for your own safety.
His Majesty would be most upset to learn that a village of innocent people was slaughtered by his own Knights.

Start.text:
Our order is most intrigued by lycanthropy. We believe that this affliction has much in common with the Plague.
We were somewhat surprised that Sophy Adr Alazar's remedy doesn't work on these monsters.
Count Karl Adr Hosberg is discreetly observing the person you pointed out.

WrongLycan.text:
Are you playing with me, Mercenaries?
Do you think I like being your prisoner?
That person looks nothing like my test subject!

RightLycan1.text: Bloody hell! It was him! I recognised him straight away!

RightLycan2.text: We must warn Captain Osweld! I'll bet all the residents of Alor are actually lycanthropes!

Wait.text:
You can't go in there!
You... you've been ordered to wait for the captain! Don't ruin everything, Mercenaries!

Start.text: Do you believe them? I don't.

Next1.text:
That drunkard preferred taking his own life rather than submitting to a bit of questioning. The secret he was hiding was too much for him… Or maybe he refused to take responsibility?
Regardless, others are involved besides him, starting with the Count.

Next2.text: I'd like to trade you for your prisoners so I can question them at my leisure. Would you be willing to hand them over to me in exchange for this key found on our dear Igor's body? It seems to be quite valuable.

End.text:
I like the way you think, Mercenaries.
The rest of the bounty is yours.
If I manage to pry the truth out of those Guards, you'll be the first to know.

SettingLog.text: Your company found a strange key on the body of the man named Igor.

Start.text: I'll ask you one last time: Where is Raffi?

Next1.text:
I'm telling you, I have no idea!
The Count just ordered us to protect him from the King's Knights!

Next2.text:
Why would I question an order from the Count?
I'm just a simple soldier! Let me go!

Start.text: Step back, rogues!

Next.text: What do you want with this man? Why are you attacking him? Did the King's Knights send you?

Next0.text:
The King's Knights…? What?
What are you talking about? We just want to ask this man a few questions!

Next1.text: But what questions precisely? Why Igor specifically? What have you discovered?

Next3.text:
Oh! By the Beast's fangs, you know! You're his accomplices! The Count's soldiers are in on this!
Where is Raffi? Where are the prisoners? Seize them, Mercenaries!

NotifyObjectiveFight.text: You must capture at least one Alazarian soldier.

Start.text:
Praised be the God of Light!
We've made it through! This accursed Weald is finally behind us!

Next1.text:
You can leave us now, Mercenaries.
The Lord Mayor is a good and pious man. He'll be happy to lend us a hand.

Next2.text:
Thanks again!
You will be forever in our prayers.

Start.text:
Oh! Mercenaries! Can I talk to you for one moment?
We're in a pretty bad spot. We could use a little help to get through the Weald.

Alt2.text: The Merchant who sold us what we thought was an authentic Rigel Lantern wasn't as trustworthy as he seemed. We'd barely lit it up when it broke.

Alt3.text:
All we have left are these few drops of fuel. It's yours, if you'll agree to guide us to Hosberg without getting lost in the darkness of the Weald…
Oh! Say yes, please say yes! Our pilgrimage cannot end here!

AltAccept.text: You'll need to get hold of a Lantern. As far as I know, the only person around here who still makes them works for the King's Knights. I assume you'll have to get in their good graces to acquire one.

AltAccept2.text: We'll wait for you here as long as it takes. We don't have much of a choice, do we?

IntroDone.text:
Oh! This is incredible! Blessings be upon you! We're finally going to leave this horrible place!
Just say the word, and we'll follow you anywhere! We're more than ready!

Trigger.text:
By Saint Jeru and all his companions, what ever possessed you to go into the Weald without a Lantern?
Hasn't anyone ever told you?

Trigger2.text: People who go in there without a light… they just never come back! The Madness consumes their minds, or keeps them there forever, or…

Next1.text:
It's not superstition, Mercenaries! It's deadly serious!
We took an enormous risk in coming to find you when our own Lantern was unusable! In the name of all that is sacred, please never do that again!

Next2.text: Our pilgrimage was supposed to bring us through Hosberg. Unfortunately, it seems the Merchant who sold us what we thought was an authentic Rigel Lantern wasn't as trustworthy as he looked. We'd barely lit it up when it broke.

Next3.text:
All we have left are these few drops of fuel. It's all yours, if you'll agree to guide us to our destination.
Oh! Say yes, please say yes! Our pilgrimage cannot end here!

Accept1.text: You'll need to get hold of a Lantern. As far as I know, the only person around here who still makes them works for the King's Knights. I assume you'll have to get in their good graces to acquire one.

Accept2.text: We'll wait for you here as long as it takes. We don't have much of a choice, do we?

Start.text: Halt! In the name of His Majesty, King Wilburt Adr Alazar, I order you to stop!

Next1.text:
The townspeople say they've heard screams coming from that inn.
Were you inside? Are there any casualties? ...

Next2.text: By Saint Jeru! That man with you! He's no Merchant!

Next3.text: Get away from him immediately! He's a lycanthrope!

Start.text: Halt! Mercenaries!

Next0.text:
Are you planning to enter the prison?
In that case, I'm sure you wouldn't mind having a look around for us!
It's just that... we're worried about one of our lads.

Next1.text: Raffi was supposed to be executed on Hosberg Square three days ago, but the hanging was mysteriously cancelled. And had that nitwit been released, he would've run straight to our camp.

Next2.text:
The jailer doesn't know you, so it'll be child's play.
You walk in, check if our lad is still there, and walk out. His old mum has the right to know what's become of her good-for-nothing son, hasn't she?

Accept.text: Try and be quick – strange rumours have been floating around the Black Market about that prison.

Wait.text:
So?
Is Raffi in there? Don't tell me we've all been worrying and he's been dead of dysentery the whole time.

Return1.text:
Who's that, then?
If he told you he's Raffi, then you've been had, Mercenaries!

Return2.text:
Oh! He knows what's happened to him?
Well, have him tell you! Let's see if you've spent your Krowns wisely.

MissionDesc1.text: Take on the Bandits' mission.

MissionDesc2.text: Inquire about the fate of someone called Raffi.

Start.text: Your Raffi didn't stay in the prison long. Not long at all! Once the man had examined him, he chose him and took him away.

Next1.text: He wasn't the first! In the three months I've been rotting in this cage, that son of a crocswine has cleared out the whole prison. Men, women, thieves, killers… Everyone! He took them all.

Next2.text: Bloody hell! I don't know what he's planning to do with them all, but I'll wager it's not a tea party. And the strangest bit was he didn't pay.

Next4.text:
He didn't pay?
Are you sure he wasn't an executioner or a Guard?
What did he look like?

Next5.text: How am I supposed to know? He wore a cape that hid his face and his clothes, and the only thing I could make out was his breath! Oof! I've known my share of drunks, but that's the worst I've ever smelled by far. Even his partners, the ones who called him Igor, stayed a good five feet away.

Start.text: What could that man be doing with his prisoners?

Next1.text:
I'm dying to ask him myself. Aren't you, Mercenaries?
Come on, then! What if I paid you a tidy sum to get your hands on him?

Accept.text: Let's start by searching the Taverns. Drunks can never stay away from them for long.

MissionDesc1.text: Inspect the Alor Tavern.

MissionDesc2.text: Inspect the Hosberg Tavern.

MissionDesc3.text: Inspect the Munden Tavern.

SettingLog.text: You've discovered that prisoners have been disappearing from Rigel prison.

Start.text: That's Roselind's! Shove over!

Next1.text: Oh, yes! I recognise her perfume. She came through here. And she wasn't alone!

Next2.text: Trust me, Mercenaries! I've got a lead here! If we follow it, we'll find my beloved!

Start.text:
Those wretches don't know how to take proper care of their animals.
Just look at this horse! We found it abandoned in the Weald.

Next1.text: Lucky for him, I've got three kids who'll be thrilled to have him as their new pet. A gift like that will help ease their minds while I'm away.

Next2.text:
Well, well! So his owners are looking for him? Too bad, my mind is made up.
No one will stop me from taking him with me!

Start.text:
This horse looks as timid as it is undernourished.
You need to find something to lure it with.
The horse starts to snort when it sees you approaching.

MissionDescInn.text: Talk to the men who saved you.

MissionDescWolves.text: Listen to what the Trackers have to say.

MissionDescEndSetting.text: Wait or rest whilst waiting for Captain Osweld to arrive.

MissionDescEndFight.text: Attack Alor with Captain Osweld's help.

MissionDescEndReward.text: Talk to Captain Osweld to claim your reward.

MissionDescMission3.text: Guide Gero back to the Market Square.

MissionDescMission2.text: Some travellers claim they were robbed of their Lantern Fuel by strange Merchants. The Lord Mayor of Hosberg insists that the Weald be rid of these thieves.

Start.text:
These villagers were participating in the search.
Whilst searching their remains, your Companions find a broken lantern.
Among the corpses is a lycanthrope wearing Brotherhood armour.
There's nothing but a ribbon caught in the brambles.

Your Companions discover the body of a Bandit half-buried in the snow.
It doesn't take long to figure out that he was trampled to death.

line0.props.tipText: Ask the Count to keep an eye on this person.

Start.text: This is where travellers say one last prayer before entering the Weald.
An altar to Saint Izella. Found only in Alazar.
All that's left of one of the King's Knights' patrols. The Weald has started to reclaim the corpses.
Caught by surprise, this Knights' patrol had no chance of surviving.
Dead lycanthropes, executed by the King's Knights.

My remedies have been approved by the University of Alazar, unlike that witch's slop!
Don't be fooled, her "potions" are a joke!

Next.text: Child's play for someone as educated as myself!

Start.text: The Mausoleum door is half-open.
Cart tracks that lead straight to a Mausoleum.
To keep lycanthropes from coming back to life, you just have to bury them face-down!

Next1.text: Really? Did the Knights tell you that?

Next2.text:
No, but just think about it!
When they wake up, they'll try to make their way to the surface, but they'll actually be digging even deeper. Then after a while, they'll fall out the other side of the world!
And just like that… We'll be rid of them forever!

Next3.text: Oh, yeah! That actually makes sense!

Start.text: With no Trade Route, I can only sell local items. Goods from further away just end up rotting on the way here.

Next1.text:
Looking for exotic items? You won't be disappointed, Mercenaries!
Thanks to the trade routes you've built, I've got all the wares you could ever need.

Start.text:
This should change our fellow citizens' minds.
Who would ever suspect that anything had happened here?

Next1.text:
I've done everything in my power to make this place warm and welcoming: stools for any unneeded Companions and a chest for your unused items.
As for organising your travel, let me handle it! I'm a professional!

Next2.text: Do you want to go somewhere?

line0.props.disableReason: Build Travel Posts in other villages to get there quickly.

line0.text: Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your first Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your second Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your third Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fourth Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fifth Trade Route.

Start.text: The family that lived here has been devoured by lycanthropes. Not a single one of them survived. A real bloodbath.

Next1.text:
Hosberg needs to move on and forget this miserable business.
A nice Travel Post should help.

line0.props.tipText: Build the Rigel Travel Post.

Build.text:
There must be some workers still alive in this village!
Give me time to go out and look for them.

Start.text:
The Count hasn't been seen in weeks. He must be hiding in his castle like the coward he is!
It's a good thing our king agreed to send his Knights, or there'd be no one left in Rigel but a bunch of lycanthropes!

Alt.text:
Adr Hosberg was behind all of this? I hope His Majesty hangs him without a trial!
A traitor to his County!

Repair.text: Well, that should give you a little protection from the lycanthropes!

Start.text:
The most beautiful girl in the village has vanished, and it seems her fiancé has gone quite mad with worry.
How romantic!

SisbertKilled.text:
It turns out that Sisbert was a lycanthrope! The Lord Mayor's son was a monster!
Do you think he killed his own fiancée?

SisbertRecruit.text:
Sisbert's become a Mercenary?
The poor man, his heart must truly be broken…
