Dialog4.text: The Skelmar army is in complete disarray. Any that didn't reach their ships in time will be hunted down and executed. Never again will the people of Ormance suffer under their cruelty!

Start.text:
You won't see me kneeling in front of the Count.
I didn't fight the Skelmar to become a law-abiding citizen.

Sigurdr promised that all converts would be pardoned by the Count.
I'm going to make sure he doesn't break his vow.

May Saint Jeru bless the day when the Montrevels kicked all the invaders out of their lands and reconquered their County.
I hope you realise what an honour it was for you to fight under my banner.

Dialog4.text:
And now, your reward.
I know this is all you care about... I'll settle my account with you promptly so you can leave my County as quickly as possible.

Accept.text: No need to thank me any further. You are dismissed. I'm sure other contracts await you.

SettingLog.text: You've liberated Forecastle Rock.

Start.text: This may be the last time we see each other: I'm returning to the capital tonight to report the details to the General.

Dialog2.text:
The battle of Forecastle Rock is a huge success: the Skelmar have been routed, and the County has regained its rightful ruler.
The General will be altogether satisfied.

Start.text: There are still a few isolated Skelmar in the region. I intend to leave a few men behind to take care of them.

Dialog3.text:
The same goes for the Hierophant.
I'll tell him how we killed the heretics and drove them all the way back to their ships. Ah! Dozens of them must already have drowned in their attempts to escape!

Start.text:
We've done it! We've done it!
I knew the Countess would lead us to victory.

You won't see me licking the Countess's boots.
The truce between the Bandits and the Guard was only temporary.
Don't worry, I'll make sure the Skelmar converts find their place in Edoranian society.
My recapture of Ormance has ended in most excellent fashion. They will sing of this battle on every street corner in the Five Kingdoms.

Dialog5.text:
In my generosity, I add to these spiritual offerings a part of the treasure that the High Jarl dared to steal from me.
Yes, you may thank me.

Accept.text: Ormance has no further need of your services. You are dismissed.

SettingLog.text: You've liberated Forecastle Rock.

Start.text:
All this gold! Bloody hell!
I didn't think there was this much in the whole world!

Dialog2.text:
After everything you did to the High Jarl, those clans won't be setting foot in the kingdom again.
Ha! The survivors must be clambering for their spot in the last few boats headed for the World's Edge!

Start.text: Of all the events we've experienced, the wedding of the Countess to that barbarian was the most surprising.

Dialog3.text:
The General will be happy to know that peace has returned to his kingdom.
I'll be sure to mention your decisive role in this victory.

Start.text: Any Skelmar who decide to stay in Ormance will have a choice to make: conversion or death.

Dialog4.text: I'll do the same with the Hierophant. You may not be saints, but what you've done for Ormance certainly deserves an altar to your glory.

Start.text: We couldn't have dreamed of a better ending.

The new Count is no better than his wife.
You won't see me licking their boots.

Sigurdr promised that all converts would be pardoned by the Count.
I'm going to make sure he doesn't break his vow.

We've done it! Mercenaries!
Forecastle Rock is ours! Ormance County is free!

Dialog5.text: We've got a lot of work ahead of us before Ormance rises from the ashes, but just know that you will always be welcomed here as heroes, Mercenaries.

Start.text: I won't leave out any details when I tell the Hierophant of your feats.

Dialog2.text:
Saint Jeru watched over our victory, and in his immense generosity, he sent you to guide us, Mercenaries.
Praised be the Eye of his Light!

Start.text:
We mustn't fool ourselves – the General will end up giving Ormance County to some noble family.
The Lord Mayor's role in this victory won't mean much against the Kingdom of Edoran's traditions.

Dialog3.text: The General is very pleased with your victory, Mercenaries. It is a great relief for the Legion to know that our kingdom is free of the Skelmar threat.

Start.text:
Don't expect me to support the Lord Mayor.
I didn't risk my life in hopes of becoming a law-abiding citizen.

Dialog4.text:
You've earned your reward, Mercenaries.
Take this. This comes from our late Countess's treasury. I'm sure she'd have no objections to your taking it.

SettingLog.text: You've liberated Forecastle Rock.

Start.text: With no lord or lady to look to, the Guard will obey the Lord Mayor of Ormance.
Don't worry, I'll make sure the Skelmar converts find their place in Edoranian society.

This is it, Mercenaries! The moment of truth!
We mustn't fail!

Next1.text:
The men are dedicated to you. You can count on them to carry out your orders.
Simply tell them when to act.

line0.props.tipText: Obtain the Guard's Strategic Skill: <skill>Volley</skill>.

Start.text:
Victory is ours! We've done it, Mercenaries!
The Skelmar have been routed! The castle has been retaken! The Barony of Belestan is free!

Next2.text: Let's hurry inside, I must see our Countess immediately.

Start.text: Give us the fugitives! The jarl said "no survivors".
The place is occupied by unknown warriors.

The Skelmar are hot on our heels! We don't know where to run to!
Help! Please! We're exhausted!
Saint Eleor bless you! We haven't stopped running since the castle fell!

Next1.text: But what are you doing here, Mercenaries? The barony is lost! It's all over for Ormance County! You should flee, like the rest of us!

Next2.text: Pallas sent you to find the Countess? So the captain hasn't given up hope. What an admirable woman!

Next3.text: I wish I had better news to report. Our battalion defended the western rampart to the very end, and we never saw Countess Montrevel come through.

Accept.text: You can count on us to join the captain's ranks. Under her orders, we will protect Two-Shores with our very lives!

SettingLog.text: You saved the Guard from their pursuers.

Start.text: The Guard is facing off against adversaries unknown to the Companions.

Next0.text:
Over here! Whoever you are!
In the name of Saint Eleor, please help us!

Start.text:
The Guard tore down this bridge. Supposedly to slow down the Skelmar.
But now we're trapped like rats!

Next1.text:
Bring me some materials and I'll show you how to patch this pile of rubble back together.
Then my animals can cross over, and you'll have learned a new skill!

Next2.text:
Just like new! Good materials make good bridges!
Try it, you'll see!

Start.text:
I'm staying in Goella. As long as this barony is in my enemies' hands, I refuse to leave this place.
I'll meet up with you when you return.

I understand that you're concerned with the fate of the other baronies, but it's my duty to watch over our abbey.
We'll meet again when you return.

The siege is broken! Praised be Saint Eleor and Saint Guilhem!
Grace be upon them!

Next1.text: Follow me inside! Your reward awaits!

Start.text: Perfect timing, Mercenaries! The assault has just begun. The Inquisition seems to have things well in hand, but it would be foolish not to take every advantage we can get.

Next1.text: Saint Guilhem abbey will be generous to its saviours. I can promise you that.

Start.text:
Well done, Mercenaries.
We gave them a show worthy of the kingdom's finest jugglers!

Next1.text:
Of course, impersonating the God of Light is a sacrilege, but ultimately, wasn't it only the better to serve him?
I'm sure our souls have nothing to fear.

Next2.text: Take your reward. I'll make sure that the Inquisitors are fully prepared to break the siege on the citadel.

Reward.text: If you wish to follow us in this holy undertaking, I promise that the abbey's coffers are full enough to pay you more than adequately for your services.

SettingLog.text: You convinced the Inquisition to help the Citadel of Saint-Guilhem.

Start.text:
The Eye has unleashed its reckoning upon you, heretics that you are!
You refused to defend a sacred place! Your souls will never join the Light!

Next1.text:
Those were the Hierophant's orders!
We were just following them!

Next2.text: Obeying a man instead of your own god? Such impiety is unworthy of the Inquisition!

Next3.text: Redeem yourselves! Redeem your souls by fighting alongside the God of Light to save His abbey!

Next4.text:
We'll obey the Light! We'll do everything in accordance with His will!
Give the command, and we will follow! I swear it!

line0.props.tipText: Obtain the Inquisition's Strategic Skill: <skill>Inferno</skill>.

Start.text: Th… the Eye's Reckoning!

What do you want, Mercenaries?
I don't see any Skelmar patrol! Why did you call us?

Next1.text: How dare you insult the Inquisition? You call us... Heretics? Ours is a sacred mission, and…

Next2.text:
... What did you say about my mother?
I'll make you eat your words!

Start.text: I'm not giving up. The Inquisition must come and help us.

Next1.text: Take me to the Gosenberg Travel Post, I'm sure I'll find some convincing arguments there!

Start.text: One of these bears is wearing a collar labelled Scruffy.

line0.props.disableReason: There must be some way to distract Scruffy and his companion.

Alt.text: One of these bears is wearing a collar labelled Scruffy.

Eat.text: The bears don't seem interested in you.

Start.text: This way, Mercenaries!

Next1.text:
Look at this little marvel!
A catapult, straight from our Sawmill! Plautaire really outdid himself – he's never made one this precise!

line0.props.tipText: Obtain the Craftsmen's Strategic Skill: <skill>Catapult</skill>.

Next2.text:
Hm? Oh, you don't know how to use this type of weapon?
Don't worry, if the Legion can do it, anyone can.
Be bold, Mercenaries! Our barony's future is in your hands!

Start.text: Please allow me one personal remark before putting my men's lives and my own at risk.

Next1.text: Countess Montrevel doesn't deserve to have you save her. The Guard thinks they can't do without her, but they're wrong. The recapture of Lycia was proof of that.

Next2.text:
Besiege the prison, liberate the entire Barony of the Isle, but don't waste your time saving that troublesome hostage.
That will be my final piece of advice.

Start.text:
Well!
Good thing you've got catapults!
What are you waiting for? Quickly! My men are already on the frontline!

Next1.text: With your help, we can liberate Lycia!

Start.text: It's the slaves you want? And you're willing to pay?

Give.text:
They're all yours.
In any case, they didn't seem too likely to survive the Crossing.

Start.text: Oh my! We're free!

Next1.text:
Please! You must save my wife! She was kidnapped, too!
I'm sure Lord Mayor Septin will pay to have us back!

Alt1.text: Oh my! We're free!

Alt2.text: ... You saved my wife, too? Praised be Saint Lenaid! Thank you!

Alt3.text: I'll lead the other villagers to the Bandits' Lair. Let's meet up there. Lord Mayor Septin will pay you handsomely when he sees we're all safe and sound!

MissionDesc.text: Claim your reward from Lord Mayor Septin.

Start.text: These slaves are ours! We captured them! Find your own!
Thank you! Thank you, Mercenaries! Thank you for coming to save us!

Next1.text:
Please! You must save my husband! He was kidnapped, too!
I'm sure Lord Mayor Septin will pay to have us back!

Alt1.text: Thank you! Thank you, Mercenaries! Thank you for coming to save us!

Alt2.text: ... You saved my husband, too? Praised be Saint Lenaid! Thank you!

Alt3.text: I'll lead the other villagers to the Bandits' Lair. Let's meet up there. Lord Mayor Septin will pay you handsomely when he sees we're all safe and sound!

MissionDesc.text: Claim your reward from the Lord Mayor.

Start.text: The Skelmar have prisoners! If you alert them, those prisoners will be killed! The Lord Mayor promised a reward for each farmer we save!

Next1.text:
Our plan is to sneak into the camp and kill the Skelmar in their sleep.
There are a lot of those bastards, so we wouldn't mind a bit of help. We'll share the reward equally.

Next2.text: Your men and mine must be perfectly coordinated. If you have an order to give, choose the right time for it.

line0.props.tipText: Obtain the Bandits' Strategic Skill: <skill>MurderByStealth</skill>.

Day1.text: Don't enter their camp! The Skelmar have taken prisoners! If you attack them head-on, they'll kill those poor wretches!

Day2.text:
The plan is to wait until nightfall. Once those savages are sound asleep, we'll strike. By the time they figure out what's going on, we'll have freed our companions.
Sound good?

Day3.text: If you want to join us, come back here at sunset. The Lord Mayor is offering a reward for each prisoner freed. In the meantime, why not go and look around at our lair? They may need you back there.

MissionDesc.text: Attack the Skelmar camp at nightfall.

Start.text: The Skelmar invasion has forced our guild to stay away from Ormance. Fortunately for the locals, we're back now.
To arms, Legionaries! This battle is yours! And on this day blessed by the Eye, we're going to take back our Academy from the Skelmar!

Next1.text:
With our blades and their blood, the Legion will wash away the affront it has suffered! We shall crush our enemies, and our names will be sung from here to the Capital!
Let us liberate our Academy! Our Barony! Our County!

Start.text: Halt, Mercenaries!

Next1.text:
If you've come to fight the Skelmar, I'll have to ask you to set your plans aside.
Those barbarians are holding our companions hostage.

Next2.text: We've sent an emissary to negotiate with their jarl. I won't let you ruin their progress…

Start.text: I… it's… By Saint Eleor! The lieutenant has failed!

Forget everything I said – you've got to help us!
Enter their camp, challenge Jarl Skeda and bring back our companions. We can't afford to lose any more men!
Please, I'm begging you!

My men told me everything! You're heroes, Mercenaries!
The Legion and the entire barony are in your debt.

End2.text: The Skelmar are a pain, but with a jarl leading them, they become a real scourge. Thanks for stepping in!

EndFightDead1.text: I thought I heard fighting… Surely you didn't…

EndFightDead2.text:
Noooo!
Our men! Why did you attack the jarl when she had hostages?! It's a disaster…

EndFightDead3.text: I'll tell you what you can do with that blasted reward!

SettingLog.text: You have defeated Jarl Skeda.

Start.text: What have you done with the rats? Why can't I hear anything now?

Next1.text:
You've killed them? By the Beast's fangs! Do you know how long it took us to capture them and release them in the Skelmar camps?
We were bitten at least eight times, and…

Next2.text:
Of course we thought of the risks of an epidemic…
Ah, well! What matters is that we're rid of Jarl Tyrra! Let's call it even, all right?

Next3.text: Take this. In exchange, don't say anything to the Colonel. All she needs to know is that there's one fewer jarl in the barony.

SettingLog.text: You got rid of Jarl Tyrra.

Start.text: Creatures are wriggling and squirming inside the camp.

line0.props.tipText: Enter the Skelmar camp.

Start.text: The camp seems to be occupied, but no one is guarding the entrance.

line0.props.tipText: Enter the Skelmar camp.

Start.text: You hear sounds of fighting from outside the Skelmar camp.

line0.props.tipText: Enter the Skelmar camp.

Start.text:
What a disgrace for the clan!
Lucky thing you were there to catch him and kill him.

Next1.text: We'll throw his body in the sea and hope the gods accept the offering.

Next2.text:
After that… well…
Naming a jarl takes a long time. Especially if the gods are angry.
It's better for the clan if we go back to more familiar lands.

SettingLog.text: You have defeated Jarl Kraven.

Start.text: Let me be! I didn't do anything to become jarl! I don't know why the gods chose me!

Next1.text: All I wanted was to pillage a few towns and go home! Not become jarl! Not fight the Legion! Oh, by Aeda, why me?

Start.text:
You want to fight us?
Perfect timing, warriors!

Next1.text: The gods have just chosen a new jarl for the clan. Nothing like a fight against the odds to prove his worth!

Next2.text: Come on! Follow us, I'll take you to him.

line0.props.tipText: Enter Majora's Farm.

Wait.text: Any news about that coward Kraven?

line0.props.tipText: Enter Majora's Farm.

Start.text: Sheathe your weapons, strangers. Our jarl bids you welcome.

line0.props.tipText: Enter Attia's Arena.

Start.text: You've rebuilt the bridge?

Next1.text:
Praised be Saint Eleor!
We've been worried for days that we'd have to find some other way to cross!

Next2.text:
We'd love to invite you for a drink in celebration, but we've got a long road ahead of us!
Give the Legion our best!

line0.props.tipText: Let the deserters go.

Start.text:
I recognise you!
You're the Mercenaries who rebuilt the bridge! How are you doing?

I'll be damned! We've done it! The camp is ours, Mercenaries!
Take a minute to soak in our victory!

Wait, Mercenaries.
I have something to tell you.

Next1.text:
The priestess taught us that true believers support one another against heretics.
Therefore I must ask you to kill Sigurdr.

Next2.text:
I've known him my whole life, and he has no intention of leaving these lands, nor of sharing the loot.
If you want to drive the heretics from Edoran, you'll have to take him out.

Next3.text: He'll be vulnerable after the battle. Your hand must not falter!

Start.text:
We're here! The camp is just ahead!
Do you all know what to do?

Next1.text: Show no mercy! This camp must fall if we're to reach the High Jarl! Its occupants supply the fortress at Forecastle Rock. Without them, Sven will be trapped on his little island. And without food, his men will rebel in turn.

Next2.text:
I'm counting on you, and on my brave Mercenaries as well. Follow their orders as though they came directly from me.
In the meantime, I'll remain on the hill. For a better view of the battle.

Start.text: Our alliance has borne fruit, Mercenaries! I knew I wouldn't regret teaming up with warriors of your skill.

Next1.text: It's just that, before I can pay you, I need my enemy's treasure. Do you see where I'm going with this?

Next2.text: We'll have to attack the Large Camp in the western part of this barony! Thanks to you, and to the members of my clan that we've deftly rallied to our cause, it should be child's play.

Start.text: Such efficiency, Mercenaries! You have a most exotic way of fighting.

Next1.text: We haven't saved the whole clan yet, but there are enough of us that my men can support you in combat.

line0.props.tipText: Obtain the Skelmar's Strategic Skill: <skill>HornOfValor</skill>.

Next2.text: Don't hesitate to call on them at any time. It's their duty to obey their jarl.

Next3.text: Let's keep going, we're nearly there.

Start.text: Are you the Mercenaries everyone's been talking about? Thorkell wants to see you. She's set up camp at the Ormance Stables.

NoSigurdr.text:
Thorkell's asked you to find Sigurdr?
Make sure you strangle him before he tries talking to you.

Sigurdr1.text:
Well, well! Is that the traitor Sigurdr by your side?
Don't tell me he actually convinced you to obey him!

line0.props.tipText: Enter the tower.

Start.text:
These men are under the protection of the God of Light! You have no rights over them!
Leave, vile Skelmar!

Next1.text:
Wha…?!
What are you talking about?

Next2.text: These men are ours! They are Skelmar! Their clan has been dishonoured, and the gods demand their deaths for their jarl's betrayal!

Next4.text:
I can't let you murder these converts to the word of the Light!
You! Mercenaries! Help us!
Those who protect true believers deserve honours… and a reward!

Start.text: Sheathe your arms, strangers. I have a proposal for you.

line0.props.tipText: Enter the occupied location

Sigurdr1.text: Ah, wonderful! You've brought the traitor Sigurdr back to us…

Sigurdr2.text: Wait! Why isn't he tied up?

Sigurdr3.text:
Idiots! You've let yourselves be taken in!
This dog will betray you like he betrayed his own people!

Start.text: This place isn't guarded, but you can hear screams from inside the dilapidated lighthouse.

line0.props.tipText: Enter the lighthouse.

Start.text: To arms! To arms, people of Edoran! Death to the heretics!

Next3.text: Death to the heretics!

Next4.text: For Ormance!

Next5.text: Glory to the Kingdom of Edoran!

Start.text:
The time has come to take what is rightfully mine!
For the horns of war to herald my glory!
Tonight, my banner shall wave over the ramparts of Forecastle Rock!

Next1.text: For Countess Montrevel!

Next2.text: Glory to Edoran! Glory to the General!

Next3.text: For the God of Light and our guide Saint Jeru!

Start.text: To arms, people of Ormance!

Next0.text:
The time has come to take what is rightfully mine!
For the trumpets of war to herald my triumph!
Tonight, my banner shall wave over the ramparts of Forecastle Rock!

Next1.text:
Attack, my brothers!
The High Jarl must pay for what he's put our clan through! Show no mercy! Die!

Next2.text:
Die! Die!
For Ormance County!

Start.text:
People of Ormance! This battle is yours!
Don't fight for a jarl! Don't fight for a Lord!
Fight for your land! For your families! For all you hold dear!

Next1.text:
Let us take vengeance on these looters and killers!
Let us drive from our lands those who have brought so much death and destruction!
The Skelmar must perish! Ormance is ours!

Start.text: We all knew it would end like this.

Next1.text: It's too bad… I rather liked you.

NotifyIntroduction.text: Disturbing rumours have reached the Companions' ears. The inhabitants of the Town of Two-Shores may know more about them.

MissionDescIntroduction.text: Question the Guards in the Happy Harvest Market to learn more about the County.

MissionDescMill.text: Eliminate the Skelmar pursuing the Guard.

NotifR4VillageReady.text: You have received a letter: you are expected at the Bandit Camp.

MissionDescR4VillageReady.text: Talk to the Lord Mayor and the Bandit Chief.

MissionDescR2TradingPost.text: Bring Priest of the Light Salvien to the Gosenberg Travel Post.

MissionDescR2InquisitionCamp.text: Meet Priest of the Light Salvien in the Inquisition Camp.

NotifyR2Siege.text: The battle for Saint Guilhem Citadel has begun.

MissionDescR2Siege.text: Join the Inquisition to break the siege on Saint Guilhem Citadel.

MissionDescR2SiegeEnd.text: Meet Priest of the Light Salvien in Saint Guilhem Abbey.

MissionDescR3Siege.text: Besiege the Skelmar bastion with the help of the craftsmen and their catapult.

MissionDescR3End.text: Talk to the workers to get your reward.

NotifR3Siege.text: The messenger for the Sawmill craftsmen has found you: your siege engines are waiting for you outside the Brotherhood Training Grounds.

MissionDescR4SiegeEnd.text: Meet the Lord Mayor and the Bandit chief in the Town Hall.

MissionDescR4PrisonEnd.text: Enter Ormance Prison to receive your reward.

MissionDesc2R5Fishery.text: Challenge Jarl Skeda or fight her.

MissionDescR5End.text: Talk to Colonel Volusia at the Border Crossing.

MissionDescR5Fight.text: Defeat the Skelmar entrenched inside the Military Academy.

MissionDescR5Reward.text: Talk to Colonel Volusia at the Military Academy.

MissionDescR6EndBodil.text: Talk to Liv to get your reward.

MissionDescR6EndSigurdr.text: Talk to Jarl Sigurdr to get your reward.

MissionDescEnd1.text: Meet up with your allies in Saint Guilhem Abbey.

MissionDescEnd2.text: Meet up with your allies in Countess Montrevel's Castle.

MissionDescEnd3.text: Meet up with your allies in the chapel of Countess Montrevel's Castle.

MissionDescEnd4.text: Meet up with your allies in the Lycia Town Hall.

MissionDescEnd.text: Enter Forecastle Rock and celebrate your victory with your allies.

Start.text:
The body is in a frightful state.
Paw prints lead away to the north.
Wait!
The bodies of a group of farmers. They fled in the wrong direction.
The legionaries' corpses are still warm.

E1NotDone.text:
The bridge has been destroyed by men wielding pickaxes.
An attempt by the Guard to slow the Skelmar's advance.

E1Done.text: There must be someone in the barony of Belestan who knows how to rebuild bridges.

Talk.text: Do you want to rebuild the bridge?

E1NotDone.text:
The bridge has been destroyed by men wielding pickaxes.
An attempt by the Guard to slow the Skelmar's advance.

E1Done.text: There must be someone in the Barony of Belestan who knows how to rebuild bridges.

Talk.text: Do you want to rebuild the bridge?
Do you want to rebuild the bridge?
Do you want to rebuild the bridge?
Do you want to rebuild the bridge?
Do you want to rebuild the bridge?
Do you want to rebuild the bridge?

Start.text: These Inquisitors had a deadly encounter.
Dead Skelmar. They were tortured with extremely refined techniques.
A massacred Skelmar patrol.
These boats probably belong to smugglers.
Some farmers tried to hide in the forest.

It's a pleasure to welcome you to my shop!
I feel like I could heal or treat just about anything!

Next.text: When I tell my wife you came through here, she'll be green with envy!

Start.text: Pedlars need lucrative Trade Routes to travel from village to village. Without them, all I can sell you is what's produced locally.

Next1.text:
Take a moment to admire my wares!
Thanks to the Trade Routes you've built, I have everything a Mercenary company could possibly want.

Start.text: This new Travel Post represents the rebirth of Lycia!

Next1.text:
Here you'll find everything you need to store both your items and your less useful Companions.
Feel free to travel from our lovely, peaceful County to more dangerous locales – I'll plan your trips for you.

Next2.text: Where would you like to go?

line0.props.disableReason: Build Travel Posts in other villages to get there quickly.

line0.text: Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your first Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your second Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your third Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fourth Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fifth Trade Route.
Liberate all of the baronies in Ormance to access this content.

line1.text: The clerk is finally willing to sell you the Lycia Travel Post.

Start.text: Now that the lovely old house that used to stand on this plot has gone up in smoke, there's enough room to turn it into a Travel Post!

Next1.text:
It's too bad the County is at war, isn't it?
All the available resources and workers have been directed to the war effort.

Start.text: Now that the lovely old house that used to stand on this plot has gone up in smoke, there's enough room to turn it into a Travel Post!

Next1.text:
The Lord Mayor will be thrilled to see Lycia come back to life.
Think of it as an act of charity!

line0.props.tipText: Build the Ormance Travel Post.

Build.text: Excellent! I'll go right out to find some workers who haven't been too badly crippled in the war. With a bit of luck, I might even run into a disciple of Saint Lenaid!

Start.text:
Just imagining those Skelmar with their dirty paws all over my tools…
Let me take care of your armour, I need to keep my mind occupied.

Repair.text: This forge is mine, and mine only.

MissionDescPrison.text: Meet up with the Bandit Chief outside Ormance Prison.

MissionEngin.text: Come back when you've found catapults in the Barony of Puy-Corbin.

MissionDescEnd4.text: Meet up with your allies at Forecastle Rock and begin the final assault.

MissionDescR4.text: Find craftsmen with the skills to make a catapult in the Barony of Puy-Corbin.

line0.text: Talk to the Bandit Chief.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line2.text: Accept the Bandit Chief's mission.

Start.text: Who would have guessed that learning to count would take me this far?

Next1.text: The Lord Mayor has appointed me treasurer! I'm in charge of providing whatever you may need to fight the Skelmar.

EndRebuilt.text:
Now that I'm treasurer, why go back to being a Bandit?
My life is much quieter between these walls!

Start.text: You've done it! Mercenaries! Lycia is free! We've got our village back!

Next1.text: By Saint Eleor's shield! We did it all by ourselves! No need for the Guard or the Legion – it's the people of the Isle who did this. With your help, of course.

Next2.text: On behalf of all the inhabitants of this humble barony, please allow me to present you with this. It's not much compared to everything you've done, but it's the best we can offer you.

Wait.text: Oh, it feels good to be home!

SettingLog.text: You have liberated the village of Lycia.

Start.text: Don't look at me like that! The Lord Mayor's the one who's got your reward.

Countess1.text:
Countess Montrevel… yes…
I may not have told you absolutely everything.

Countess2.text: It's not that I don't want to help you, especially after all you've done for Lycia, but the prison is completely impregnable. You'd need equipment that no one in this barony has.

Countess3.text: Siege engines – catapults, for example. The kind of thing we don't have on hand in a trading town like Lycia, that they only build way out at the other end of Ormance, in the Barony of Puy-Corbin.

Countess4.text: The best I can do right now is to pray that the Skelmar haven't massacred all the craftsmen with the know-how to build them. While you're gone, I truly swear to watch over the good folk of Lycia.

CountessAlt1.text:
You haven't given up on the idea of rescuing the Countess?
I don't understand you, Mercenaries. You don't need that coward!

CountessAlt2.text: Look at Lycia: the village was liberated by locals, Bandits and Mercenaries. Only the Guard wants to see her liberated!

CountessAlt3.text:
But so be it! I promised you my support, and you shall have it.
Let me know when you're ready. And don't forget your catapult. The prison is much more heavily fortified than Lycia.

Countess5.text: You've found catapults? By the Beast's fangs, I thought they'd all been destroyed.

Countess6.text: Well, that certainly changes things! The craftsmen of Puy-Corbin make the best siege engines in all the Five Kingdoms. What a shame to use these marvels to free someone like Countess Montrevel!

Countess7.text: But so be it. I promised you my support, and you shall have it. Just let me know when you're ready.

Start.text: I am glad to see you, Mercenaries. Our allies were beginning to doubt in our ability to retake Ormance County.

Dialog8.text: Tella is right. Acting in the County's interest is what allowed the Barony of the Isle to liberate itself all on its own.

Dialog9.text: As for the coordination between our armies, we could entrust you with that task, Mercenaries. All of us here have borne witness to your talent. It's just a matter of whether you'll accept this role.

Accept.text:
In that case, it's settled! Let's move!
We'll take Forecastle Rock by storm and kick the Skelmar out of our county!

Dialog6.text:
Silence!
We have no need for a jarl, a hierophant or a general!

Dialog7.text: All that matters is saving our county from the Skelmar! Stopping those savages from pillaging and slaughtering our people! That's why we must unite!

Dialog2.text: Without Countess Montrevel, there's no banner to join our forces under! Who will give the order to attack? And by what right?

End.text: If the Legion doesn't take part in this battle, and if by some miracle, the Bandits manage to win, we'll have a civil war on our hands.

Dialog3.text: I've already recommended that we fight in the name of the God of Light. Our faith is what makes us natural allies against the heretics!

End.text:
The Inquisition will fight alongside the faithful.
This County must not devolve into heresy.

Dialog4.text:
I agree with the fanatic!
My men want to prove their worth to the Eye by driving their heathen brothers from their lands!
Let the Inquisitor be our jarl!

End.text: Fight without a jarl? By Saint Jeru, that's a risky idea…

Start.text:
Since our victory at Forecastle Rock, our County is still waiting for a lord to be named.
The noble families in the capital must be busy killing each other to acquire new lands.

Next1.text: As for Tella, all I know is that she's assisting in the reconstruction of Ormance. Thanks be to Saint Jeru that it's keeping her far away from her old life.

End.text: I'd like to give you news about Tella, but all I know is that she's assisting in the reconstruction of Ormance. Thanks be to Saint Jeru, it's keeping her far away from her old life.

EndRebuilt.text:
Now that the reconstruction of Ormance is complete, I don't have any illusions about what Tella's likely up to.
The Bandits have re-established their grip on the roads of the County.

line0.text: Liberate all of the baronies in Ormance to access this content.

line1.text: The Gosenberg Merchant has finally received some inventory.

Start.text: Good to see you again, warriors!

Tatoo2.text: Say… You wouldn't want a tattoo, would you? It's just… I'm still awfully short on customers! If the people of Edoran see their heroes all inked up, they'll line up for my services in a hurry!

Tatoo3.text: With that one, even the Guard will show up!

Start.text: It's not all entirely fresh, but with all the damage the Skelmar have done to our crops, we'll have to make do.

Ormance County, and the Barony of the Isle in particular, are quite famous for their cold cuts.
The Skelmar caught on, and cleaned out my whole stock!

It's just… I haven't anything to sell you!
The Gosenberg Merchants refuse to re-establish all their Trade Routes until the County has been fully liberated.

Lycia is the last stop before the capital of Edoran.
The Gosenberg Merchants were very eager to get back there.

People are talking about you in... less respectable circles, you know? You've got a certain reputation with our kind... Want to see “the lair”? But if you want to get in, you've got to be known to the authorities, if you catch my drift...

GoOk.text: We criminals need to stick together. Put these bags over your heads and follow me – I'll take you to the lair.

GoNo.text: Sorry, lads, but you're too squeaky clean to get in. We're all in the same boat here, right? So if you haven't got a bounty on you, you've no need for us.

RewardQuest.text: You've finished one of the jobs? We won't bother going all the way over there – here's your reward.

Start.text: I have my kegs brought in from the town of Two-Shores. The Skelmar methodically drank up all of my reserves.
You've come to defend us against the Skelmar, right? Is that why the Guard is on the Market Square?

Next.text:
I've healed you up as best I could.
All of our hopes now rest on you, Mercenaries.

End1.text: They say that Mercenaries helped Captain Pallas to retake Belestan. I hope they'll do the same for the whole County!

EndNext.text: Give my best wishes to your colleagues.

Start.text:
The Skelmar don't know who they're dealing with!
I'll die fighting before I let them turn me into their slave!

Repair.text: You look ready to eviscerate some Skelmar!

End1.text:
Are you the Mercenaries everyone's talking about in Belestan?
I'd be honoured to repair your armour.

line0.text: Take on Captain Pallas' mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: We've failed! It's over! The castle has fallen! The last free barony is lost! Ormance County is in the Skelmar's hands now!

Next1.text:
It's only a matter of hours until those barbarians sweep in here to slaughter us!
Oh! May the God of Light come to our aid!

Next2.text: Huh? Who are you? I don't have any missions for you. Unless…

Next3.text: If you're in fighting condition, you could go out to look for Countess Montrevel… There may be a chance that her escort escaped in time during the siege.

Accept.text:
In that case, search all over the barony: the escort may have hidden on a farm to get away from their pursuers.
With our lady leading us, we could organise what's left of the Guard and protect Two-Shores.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the area for Countess Montrevel.

MissionDesc2.text: Search the area for Countess Montrevel.

End1.text:
Thanks to the Guards you saved, we're almost certain that Countess Montrevel and her escort never crossed the castle's ramparts.
If she's still alive, we'll have to act fast!

End2.text: There are enough of us to try and break through. The Skelmar didn't have time to repair the defences that they broke through themselves.

End3.text:
This is our only chance: we must attack the castle and take the Countess back from those barbarians.
Are you willing to help us?

EndAccept1.text:
The men are happy to have you with us.
You've brought us hope at a time when so many others have abandoned Ormance to its fate.
Thanks to you, the Guard is getting things back under control!

MissionDescEnd.text: Liberate the castle from the Skelmar.

Start.text: Captain Pallas has my full confidence. Under her command, I'll never flee!
I owe you my life, Mercenaries. If you order me to fight, I'll fight!

I… I ran as fast as I could!
Too bad about my shield. The barbarians can keep it!

End.text: You saved our companions, Mercenaries! You are heroes!

Start.text: The Skelmar have no mercy for the wounded. Those who weren't able to make it this far are dead.

It's too late for this man.
All we can do is to say a prayer to help him join the Light.

End.text: I've buried the Guards. They received the honours they deserved.

Next1.text: These men are too badly wounded to fight.

Start.text: It's not the first time I've fled before the Skelmar's advance, but this time I truly thought it would be the last.

End.text: I didn't think I'd see the lieutenant alive again! Thank you for bringing them back from the Skelmar!

Start.text: Has the castle really fallen? Who will prevent the Skelmar from pillaging the town?

End.text: The Barony of Belestan is free! All hail the Belestan Guard!

Start.text: If you think a barbarian invasion will make me lower my prices, you must not know me very well!

End.text: The people of Belestan are so relieved to be alive that they'd buy my wares at any price!

Start.text: These men are too badly wounded to fight.
As the barony is occupied, I'm afraid I'll be too busy seeing to my own survival to help you. However, I may have heard that the surviving Guards are gathering on the Market Square…

Next1.text: Now that the Skelmar stench has abated, the air in Belestan is more refreshing than ever. Its cool breezes even blow fascinating news my way at times.

Done.text: Do I smell the scent of revenge?

line0.props.tipText: The Skelmar are supposedly using the Ormance Sawmill to consolidate their defences.

line1.props.tipText: Some say Saint Guilhem Citadel has been cut off from the world, but that would be underestimating the Smugglers' cunning.

line2.props.tipText: It seems the Bandits of Ormance acquitted themselves nicely during the siege of Lycia by helping the survivors.

line3.props.tipText: The Skelmar are supposedly preparing an attack on the kingdom's capital, preventing the Legion from helping Ormance.

line4.props.tipText: Rumour has it that the Skelmar are at each other's throats in the Barony of Goella. There must be a way to turn this to your advantage.

R3Sawmill.text: The Skelmar are supposedly using the Ormance Sawmill to consolidate their defences in Puy-Corbin.

R2Tower.text: Some say Saint Guilhem Citadel has been cut off from the world, but that would be underestimating the Smugglers' cunning.

R4Hideout.text: It seems the Bandits of Ormance acquitted themselves nicely during the siege of Lycia by helping the survivors.

R5BorderPost.text: The Skelmar are supposedly preparing an attack on the kingdom's capital, preventing the Legion from helping Ormance.

R6Stables.text: Rumour has it that the Skelmar are at each other's throats in the Barony of Goella. There must be a way to turn this to your advantage.

DeliverMission1.text: How nice to hear news that's not about the Skelmar!

End.text: I can't smell any other leads.

Start.text:
My stable boy ran off two weeks ago.
Who would have thought that little coward would survive this long?

End1.text: Now that Belestan is free, my stable boy is asking for his job back. I'm not entirely sure I want that deserter to come back.

MissionDesc.text: Wait for the Ghost Pack to appear in the suburbs.

Start.text:
Haha!
Finally, a poster that says what everyone is thinking!

Try.text:
Hey! What are you doing with that poster?
You can't take it down! It's the voice of the people!

Threat.text:
Fine! Fine! No need to draw your weapons.
I don't want to die over a poster!

Convinced.text:
I admit it, the artist may have gone a bit overboard.
Do whatever you like.

Start.text: First the riots, then bandits, and now the Ghost Pack is attacking the suburbs!

Next1.text: I don't know how these people can live under these conditions, but I can't work like this! Do you know how many rabbits I've lost in just the last two days?

Start.text: All this nonsense about the Parliament has made people completely mad.

Next1.text:
When my brother found out he'd lost his election, he fled the city in tears.
No one has seen him since!
Who's going to take care of his kids?

Next2.text:
I'm told you were seen with my brother.
Were you able to reason with him?

line0.props.tipText: Hand over the unsuccessful candidate to his brother.

Next3.text: I suppose just bringing him back is a good start.

Next4.text: The reward will be ready for you in the usual place, but allow me to add this. After all, you did go to the trouble of escorting him!

EndConvince.text:
I heard at the Tavern that you're the ones who convinced my brother to return home.
I owe you one, Mercenaries!
I really had my hands full with his four kids.

EndInform.text:
I heard at the Tavern that you're the ones who convinced my brother to return home.
I'm not sure if I should thank you – now he's constantly carrying on about the Hierophant this and the Parliament that.

Start.text:
Come, come!
The finest ponies in all of Isandrin!
Shiny manes and a steady step!

GhostPack.text:
Buy these ponies from me! Please!
I want to go home! I don't want to get eaten by monsters!

Start.text:
My animals are raised in strict accordance with Edoranian tradition!
You won't find better wool anywhere!

GhostPack.text:
Once I've finished selling my livestock, I'm out of here!
Riots are one thing, but the Ghost Pack? Forget it!

Start.text:
Have you ever seen such healthy pink pigs, Mercenaries?
I can sell them to you live, or sliced into the finest cuts!
The perfect snack for late nights around the fire!

GhostPack.text: Am I supposed to just carry on as normal when the Ghost Pack is prowling around the Market each night?

Start.text:
What's the point of teaching farmers to read, I'd like to know! Cabbage doesn't grow any faster if you read poetry in the field.
General Maxime is wasting our taxes on useless projects!

Next.text: Sorry, I'm a bit distracted. Anything else I can do for you?

Alt1.text: What can I do for the heroes of Isandrin?

Alt2.text: It's so nice to see you under more pleasant circumstances!

Start.text:
Get back, Censors!
You'll never catch me!

<narrator>This copy of Saint Serene's writings has been made available for use by worshippers who know how to read.
The last page is dog-eared.</narrator>

Next1.text: So Saint Eleor turned to the grieving crowd and said: ”My People! Be not afraid! Do not lament the death of Saint Jeru, and do not tremble before the Darkness.”

Next2.text: ”Be glad of heart, for his son shall guide you, and his sons shall guide your sons in turn. Bow before your new emperor, Septimus Halios, and rejoice! For if you follow in his footsteps, your path shall be ever bathed in Light.”

MissionDesc1.text: Find where Colonel Marcus is being detained.

MissionDescGeneral.text: Claim your reward from General Maxime.

MissionDescFinal.text: Take on Hierophant Guillhem VII's mission.

MissionDescChurch1.text: Join Hierophant Guillhem VII in an attack on the General's Palace.

line0.text: Talk to Hierophant Guillhem VII.

line1.text: Take on Hierophant Guillhem VII's mission.

line2.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: I am most pleased to finally meet the gallant souls whom so many have praised in my presence.

Ormance.text: High Inquisitor Demius says that it was your heroics that saved Saint Guillhem Abbey from being sacked, when all thought it lost. And that it was you again who united the baronies of Ormance to defeat the High Jarl and drive the invaders from our lands.

DrombachInquisition.text: High Inquisitor Dexera was most impressed with your ardour in dealing with the heretic Ærald Adr Alazar. We owe you our thanks for capturing the prince and destroying the heathen relics that had brought the Eye's Reckoning down on Drombach.

Thanks.text: Allow me to thank you in person: in the name of the Church and the God of Light, I bless you.

DrombachPrince.text:
It is quite unfortunate that you did not show the same ardour in Drombach.
The loss of High Inquisitor Dexera, not to mention the triumph of Ærald Adr Alazar, were both bitter defeats for the God of Light. And for his Church.

ThanksBis.text: May Saint Jeru light your path to Isandrin, and may the God of Light deliver you from heresy.

OnlyPrince1.text:
Are you the Mercenaries I have heard so much about?
The ones spreading death, heresy and destruction?

OnlyPrince2.text: High Inquisitor Dexera's death did not prevent tales of your impiety from spreading to Isandrin. I know that you protected Ærald Adr Alazar and his ungodly machines from the avenging retribution they deserved.

OnlyPrince3.text: I hope you will be more discerning in Isandrin. The holy city holds a bitter fate for heretics.

Neutral1.text:
Receive my blessing, pilgrims.
You may present your offerings to one of the Mystagogues.

Neutral2.text: May Saint Jeru protect you on your return voyage.

End.text: Isandrin has returned to the calm and quiet for which it is known as the Eternal City. The God of Light illuminates the future of our kingdom once again.

Start.text: I shall never forget the fervour you brought to your fight against the heretic prince of Drombach.

Next1.text: Men of faith such as yourselves are welcome in the God of Light's abode.

End.text:
I knew that we could trust you fully.
Your faith has saved our city.

Start.text: I am not surprised one bit to see pious men like you coming to pray at the Basilica!

Next1.text: Hierophant Guillhem VII knows all about your exploits in Ormance. I made sure to tell him everything. Down to the tiniest details!

End.text:
I am glad to have intervened on your behalf with the Hierophant.
Your support of the General was only a passing moment of blindness.

Start.text: In these troubled times, we must focus on what defines the essence of Isandrin: the God of Light.
The goal is not to buy forgiveness through offerings, but to repent by surrendering any excess of earthly possessions to the divine.
His Majesty claims that he wants to uplift his kingdom to the glorious heights of the Ancients.

Next1.text: Yet isn't it peculiar to choose as one's model a people of whom nothing remains but their Tombs?

End.text:
Mystagogue Gedeon recently vanished.
I wonder what became of him.

Start.text:
To guide believers on the path of Light, Mystagogues learn every line of the holy scriptures.
All of your questions shall be answered.

line0.props.disableReason: You don't have a specific question to ask.

line0.props.tipText: Ask how to slip into the Inquisition's Commandery.

Mission1.text: Oh! A most interesting question, which deserves my full attention. I suppose it was whispered to you by a mutual friend?

Mission2.text: You will find the answer you seek behind the curtain to the left of the Hierophant, near the staircase that leads to the gallery.

Start.text: Ah! Mercenaries! We've been waiting for you. What an honour to welcome those who are already known as the saviours of Isandrin!

Next1.text: Your company's efforts to restore order in the city certainly drew my attention. As well as my admiration, I must admit. I had gone to such trouble to stir up chaos…

End1.text: Mercenaries! If you're here, that must mean you've made your choice!

Start.text:
The General's plans for Edoran will cause the kingdom's downfall. Handing power to the common rabble is heresy and political madness!
Surely you've observed their intellectual weakness for yourselves.

Next1.text: The people listen to a juggler, look at a poster, and are instantly enemies of their beloved General. They'd rather remain ignorant than see their taxes raised. As for their convictions, what do those matter compared with their families' safety? …

Next2.text:
The peasants are prey to their changeable moods and passing desires. They are not made to govern – it's against the proper order of things.
It is the Church's duty to maintain Edoran and the stability of its power. Even if that means overthrowing its General.

Next3.text: I was close to achieving that goal when you arrived in Lombelle. Alas, your efforts to thwart my plans have put me in a difficult position, as the General and his Colonels are about to unmask me. If they strike against me, any hope for Edoran to escape its tragic fate will be lost.

Next4.text:
So I propose that you repent for your mistakes by helping us to act first. We shall depose the General together, in the name of the God of Light and the greater glory of Edoran.
Take some time to think about it – the kingdom's future depends on your decision.

Wait.text:
Take some time to think about my proposal, even sleep on it perhaps, then come back to see me.
My only wish is to protect the kingdom from its young General's eccentric ways.

End1.text:
The sword arm of the Church, our proud Inquisition, is finally ready to attack the General's Palace!
We shall cast that wretched Maxime down from his throne and save Isandrin the Eternal and the Kingdom of Edoran from his foolishness!

End2.text: I am counting on you to join our ranks. You shall fight under my banner for the glory of the God of Light!

EndAccept.text:
May Saint Jeru guide you, Mercenaries!
May the Order and the Faith emerge triumphant!

Start.text:
The people want to eat their fill and be protected from Bandits.
And what does the General propose?
To teach them to read!

The Ancients destroyed themselves.
Why take inspiration from their downfall?
We're tired of wearing these rags, but wear them we will until the Hierophant and our Church are victorious!
The Church's voice will only be weakened if forced to share power with the people.

Next1.text: Heresy stalks the kingdom once known as Jeru's Empire!

Start.text: The General's reforms are destroying Edoran! Even now, the Legion is but a shadow of its former self!

O, God of Light!
Bring victory to your servants!

The Church's voice will be at the same level as the people's?
And we're expected to pay for that?

Next1.text: It's an insult and a shocking heresy!

Start.text:
The people will govern Edoran according to their changing moods and whims.
The peasants are small-minded, selfish, and unfit to rule!

The writings of Saint Serene are clear: only the pious and faithful shall rule.
How can we be sure of the faith of every peasant who makes their way into Parliament?

General Edor drove the descendants of Saint Septimus from the throne.
And now, General Maxime wants to hand over power to the people!
What will remain of our holy heritage?
To be honest, I would have preferred to avoid such a bloody battle. But isn't that what's expected of an Edoranian General? To lead the Legion with an iron fist and crush the kingdom's enemies?

Next1.text: Neglecting that role only encouraged plots and schemes. If I had been more feared, less concerned with my people's happiness, Guillhem might never have dared to oppose me.

Next2.text: Fortunately, we put an end to his rebellion before it brought Isandrin to ruin. Your help was a decisive factor. And for that, I shall be eternally grateful to you.

Accept1.text: No treasure in this kingdom is more precious than the sword of my illustrious predecessor, General Edor. It now belongs to you. Please do not refuse it.

Accept2.text: I have not proven myself worthy of it. But I intend to do so by continuing with my reforms. I will make the people of Edoran the true heirs of the Ancients. This kingdom will become the most powerful, the wisest and the best educated.

Accept3.text: Our influence will then spread to our neighbours, and we will finally unite these lands into a single empire. Just as General Edor intended.

Wait.text: Take good care of this sword. I may come to reclaim it from you one day.

Start.text: Colonel Symaque came from the old nobility. His family supported the Halios in the days of the Empire.

Next1.text: Even so, his betrayal brings disgrace to the Legion.

Start.text:
The Mystagogues' and Inquisitors' ranks will be purged under the Legion and its new Hierophant.
No conspirator will escape their cleansing fire!

I will strike Symaque's name from the Legion's registers and cast his body into the sea.
His very existence is a source of dishonour.
Now that Guillhem VII is no longer the Hierophant of Edoran, he won't be needing his mitre…

What a stroke of fate to find a mitre awaiting me here that's exactly my size!
Some might see this as the will of Saint Jeru!

Next1.text:
I'm eager for the tailor to finish my chasuble.
A Hierophant must look presentable for his followers, wouldn't you agree?

Next2.text: And speaking of looking presentable, I've found Guillhem VII's mitre. I don't know if your Companions will have any use for it, but at least it will make a nice souvenir, don't you think?

Start.text: Heretics! What have you done?

MissionDesc1.text: Save the residents who have been captured by bandits.

line0.text: Listen to the citizens' conversation.

line1.text: Talk to Alderwoman Mara.

line2.text: Take on Alderwoman Mara's mission.

line3.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Where are our children? Our brothers and sisters? Where are our parents?

Next0.text: What did the Guard and the Legion say? Did the General grant you an audience?

Next1.text: I… Well, the Guard just suggests that we pay.

Next2.text: Pay? What do you mean, pay? Did you tell them how much those fiends are demanding?! We'd have to clear out the coffers of a half-dozen guilds just to save one of our people!

Next3.text: And even if we did pay, what's to stop the bandits from doing the same thing again? With all this chaos in town, they can do whatever they please!

Next4.text:
How can the General remain unmoved?
I'm a future parliamentarian!

Next5.text: He's incompetent! I never should have supported him!

Start.text:
Oh! Saint Jeru have pity on me! I'm at a complete loss.
I've tried everything to save our people from the Bandits. Everything! I swear by the Eye!

Next1.text: I've begged the General, the Guard, the Legion, I've tried negotiating with the Bandits… I even hired Mercenaries from the Brotherhood! But nothing! None of it achieved anything! All we have left are our tears.

Next2.text:
You think you can succeed where the Brotherhood failed?
Well, I certainly won't try to talk you out of it.
If you want to try and save our loved ones, the reward is yours.

Accept.text:
We know where our friends and family are being held. Or at least, there was a meeting point mentioned in the ransom demands. I've marked it on your map.
May Saint Jeru guide you – you're our last hope.

Wait.text: May Saint Jeru guide you!

EndDead1.text: You're back! Where are our loved ones? Will they be here soon?

EndDead2.text: Dead? All of them? Oh! By Saint Jeru! No! It can't be!

Reward1.text: What's this? A list of names? Why is mine on there? Does this mean someone was deciding who the Bandits should kidnap?

Reward2.text: By Saint Septimus' beard, all of these names are future parliamentarians or members of their families! Someone is targeting the new government!

Reward3.text:
I'm going to bring this evidence to the General! He can't keep ignoring the threat after this! He'll be forced to act!
His own work is at risk now as well!

Reward3Dead.text:
Thank you, Mercenaries. I'm sorry you couldn't save our people, but this list will be of great use to us.
I wish I had more to give you, but alas, the city has so many victims to bury…

Reward3Mid.text: Thank you, Mercenaries. On behalf of the families of the captives you were able to save... and those of the others. You've been such a great help.

Reward3Alive.text:
Thank you, Mercenaries. Your help was invaluable.
The prisoners' families insisted on adding their contribution to your pay.

EndAlive1.text: Mercenaries! You're back! Oh! By all the saints, it seems we've been waiting forever!

EndAlive2.text:
Our families told us of your exploits.
It's incredible!
You're all heroes!

EndMid1.text: Mercenaries! I'm so relieved to see you! I was afraid something had happened to you on the way back.

EndMid2.text:
The survivors came in before you. They told us all about your exploits.
It was really moving. I'm just sorry you weren't able to help all of them.

Final.text:
Someone is trying to intimidate us. It worked for a while, but thanks to you, we're determined not to give in!
Isandrin and Edoran will have a Parliament of the people!

AltEndDead.text: There's a rumour going round that the Bandits who were occupying the Emperor's Beacon were killed by Mercenaries. Was that you? What's become of their prisoners? Are they safe?

AltEndAlive.text: Mercenaries! Did you save the citizens who were kidnapped by the Bandits at the Emperor's Beacon?

SettingLog.text: You discovered that someone is intimidating the future parliamentarians of Isandrin.

Start.text: All this nonsense about reforms and Parliaments have only led to chaos throughout the kingdom!

Next1.text:
My boy got elected, and for what? Just to be kidnapped moments later!
I want him back!

Start.text:
My mother was so proud when I told her I'd be a member of the new Parliament!
Oh, Saint Jeru! Please let her be alive!
What good are all these changes if my son isn't there to see them?
When I get my hands on whoever dared to go after my son...

Dead.text:
Why didn't you do something to save my son?
What will I become without him?

Start.text: My mother has nothing but praise for your courage! I hear your men slipped into the Bandits' tower without those scoundrels even noticing! How ingenious!

Dead.text:
The men who killed my mother will pay, I swear it!
The Parliament will hang them without a trial on Soldiers' Square!

Start.text: As soon as the Parliament is up and running, I'll sponsor a law to make Apothecaries treat Mercenaries for free! I'll even name it after your company!

Dead.text:
Why? Oh, Saint Jeru, why?
Why my son?

Start.text:
What do you say, Mercenaries? Isn't this a lovely Travel Post? And it's in the very heart of the Eternal City!
Everyone will be so envious of you!

Next1.text:
I've set up a place for you and your tired Companions to store any extra items weighing you down.
As for your travels, I'm fully qualified to plan them for you.

Next2.text: Have you got a destination in mind, Mercenaries?

line0.props.disableReason: Build Travel Posts in other villages to get there quickly.

line0.text: Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your first Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your second Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your third Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fourth Trade Route.
Provide 1000 and 1500 to build your fifth Trade Route.

Start.text: With no Trade Route, I can only sell local items. Goods from further away tend to just rot on the way here.

Next1.text:
Looking for exotic items? You won't be disappointed, Mercenaries!
Thanks to the Trade Routes you've built, I've got all the wares you could ever need.

Start.text:
You're in luck, Mercenaries!
The warehouse that stood here was burnt to the ground by rioters! This location is now free for you to build your Travel Post.

Next1.text: Isandrin's workers are a bit busy with building the Parliament, of course, but if you're willing to part with a few Krowns, I'm sure some of them would be happy to work for you!

line0.props.tipText: Build the Lombelle Travel Post.

Build.text: Don't worry about a thing, I'll take care of all this. Consider it settled!

Start.text:
I won't let anyone speak unkindly of General Maxime!
Agitators and traitors aren't welcome in my forge!

Repair.text:
You're ready to jump back into the fray!
Hit ‘em where it hurts! Don't show those traitors any mercy!

Start.text: That fanatic refuses to hoop my barrels just because I had the audacity to say that the General's a bit young.

Next1.text: Where am I going to put my wine now?

MissionDesc1.text: Find a man named Gedeon, the General's spymaster.

MissionDescGeneral1.text: Join General Maxime and the Edoranian Legion in an attack on the Saint Septimus Basilica.

MissionDescHierophante.text: Claim your reward from the Hierophant.

line0.text: Talk to General Maxime.

line1.text: Take on General Maxime's mission.

line2.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line0.text: Talk to General Maxime.

line1.text: Take on General Maxime's mission.

line2.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Nestled in the crimson velvet is a legendary weapon: General Edor's Sword.

E3GeneralPalaceLibrary.npc.name: Chronicles of the Kingdom of Edoran

Start.text: General Edor was not only the kingdom's most brilliant tactician and the greatest swordsman of his time, he was also a merciful soul and a ruler who cared deeply for his people's fate.

Next1.text: After ordering the immediate decapitation of Emperor Severone Halios and his traitorous Hierophant Septimus IV, he pardoned the family of the former and the Mystagogues of the latter. The Empress and her children were exiled to a charming estate in Belerion, and he allowed the priests to freely choose the new leader of the Church of the Light.

Next2.text: Lastly, he created the Assembly of Colonels, who, upon his death, would choose his successor from among his most capable subjects, and not simply from among his natural descendants as in the days of the emperors. Praise be to the great wisdom of General Edor, who thus protected his people from decline.

E3GeneralPalaceLutrin.npc.name: Archives of the Kingdom of Edoran

Start.text: <narrator>In accordance with the law of succession to the Edoranian throne, the Assembly of Colonels of the Legion then convened. The new General was elected in closed session, the morning of…</narrator>

Next1.text: Results of the vote: Tactical Lieutenant Maxime: five votes to one, Colonel Symaque: one vote to five, Tactical Lieutenant Maxime is elected General.

Next2.text: Colonels voting: Colonel Volusia, Colonel Rhoveres, Colonel Ansald, Colonel Basile, Colonel Symaque, Colonel Marcus Absent: Colonel Alexa

Start.text: Are you the heroes of Ormance? The Mercenaries that Colonel Volusia always speaks so highly of?

Next1.text: It is a great honour to welcome you to Isandrin, and a blessing from the God of Light. If your talents are as impressive as they say, you might be able to save Colonel Marcus.

Next1Bis.text: The Inquisition is detaining him under false pretences, and unfortunately, I cannot call on the Legion to rescue him without risking a civil war with Hierophant Guillhem VII.

Next2.text:
But you…!
Who would notice one Mercenary company among all those I've brought to the capital? You could set Colonel Marcus free! And if by some fateful chance you were arrested, you could simply claim you were carrying out an anonymous contract!

Accept.text: My spymaster tells me he knows of a way to infiltrate the Commandery. He's on a mission at the Saint Septimus Basilica. Find him – Gedeon is a trustworthy man.

Wait.text: I shall pray for you to bring Colonel Marcus back safe and sound.

NoSkelmar1.text:
I have little time for audiences, my dear subjects.
Speak to one of my advisors, and he will look into your complaints and requests as diligently as I myself would do.

Start.text:
For the Inquisition to be holding one of our men is an affront!
You mustn't wait any longer!

Next0.text:
You know our men make no distinction between caution and weakness! You must show them that you are a strong General!
Let us take the Commandery by force!

Next1.text:
Colonel Ansald, your anger is clouding your judgement. Colonel Marcus is accused of heresy! It is no longer up to the Legion to decide his fate – the law is clear on this.
Taking him from the Inquisition would amount to a declaration of war against the Church. The Hierophant…

Next2.text:
May the Beast devour that bloody Hierophant! This is all a conspiracy!
That old fox Guillhem is turning the Legion against you, and you're letting him do it!

Start.text:
General Maxime has great ambitions for the Kingdom of Edoran!
Soon, its people will be as educated and enlightened as the Ancients were!
It is an honour to take part in this glorious effort!

Next1.text: The only thing I can't understand is the people's own reluctance. Can't they see what's in their own interest?

Start.text: Not all of His Majesty's subjects have yet grasped the full glory of his plans. His Partisans will make it their duty to inform the populace and fight seditious ideas.

End.text: With Guillhem's death, all the slander and lies about the General and his plans will cease! The Partisans' work will be much easier!

Start.text: Arresting a Colonel?! It's a provocation! An insult to the Legion's prestige!

Gedeon warned me that the Inquisition was growing restless.
Do you have good news for me?

line0.props.tipText: Hand over Colonel Marcus.

End2.text:
Colonel Marcus! What a pleasure to have him with us again!
Did he suffer? He looks much thinner… Do you think he was tortured?

End2Bis.text:
Ah, but I digress, Mercenaries.
Colonel Marcus is one of my closest advisors and a hero to the Legion. His arrest was very upsetting for our men, and his return is sure to ease their minds.

End3.text:
The reward is yours – Colonel Ansald assured me that it was worthy of the help you've provided me.
I daren't imagine what Isandrin's fate would have been if I'd lost the Legion's support.

SettingLog.text: By saving Colonel Marcus, you have preserved the Legion's unity.

NoSkelmar3Bis.text: One of my Colonels is being held by the Inquisition – under false pretences, I can assure you! Sir Marcus is a pious and courageous man who doesn't deserve such vile treatment.

NoSkelmar3Ter.text: The Legion cannot rescue him or enter the Inquisition's Commandery without sparking a civil war with the Hierophant. Isandrin is already troubled, so I can't bear to aggravate the situation any further.

NoSkelmar4.text: But you… you could set Colonel Marcus free! No one would notice one Mercenary troop among all those I've brought to the capital. And if you're discovered, you could easily claim you don't know who's behind the contract…

NoSkelmarAccept.text: My spymaster tells me he knows of a way to infiltrate the Commandery. He's on a mission at the Saint Septimus Basilica. Find him – Gedeon is a trustworthy man.

Wait.text: I shall pray for you to bring Colonel Marcus back safe and sound.

Start.text:
The Inquisition won't be able to accuse me of escaping without admitting they let a heretic slip through their fingers.
Don't worry about me.

End.text:
What brings you here, Mercenaries?
If you're looking for Colonel Ansald, he's gathering up all the wealth and goods that belonged to Symaque.
He won't leave any of it behind, believe me.

Start.text: The Mercenaries of Arthes! Your company has changed quite a bit since we last met.

Next1.text:
Isandrin is already in a delicate situation, and it doesn't need your chaotic services.
As for me, I'd appreciate it if you kept away from our General.

Start.text: The current state of Isandrin tells you all you need to know about the success of the Skelmar invasion.

Next2.text: I hope you can help us here like you did in Ormance.

Start.text:
I was afraid you wouldn't answer my call, Mercenaries.
My spymaster informs me that you have spoken with the Hierophant.

Next1.text:
Did he confess his crimes?
He's the traitor behind the uprising in the city! The Inquisition, disguising themselves as rioters! And the Church, paying for kidnappings and the slanders of bards and scholars.

Next2.text:
There are no words for such a devious plot!
Now that we've exposed it, we must put a stop to it!

Next3.text:
Since it was your feats in battle that put the Legion on the path of truth, my Colonels and I would like to offer you the honour of fighting by our side.
Are you prepared to depose Hierophant Guillhem?

Next4.text:
Then we shall march on the Basilica together!
May Saint Jeru bless us and grant us victory!

Start.text:
Mercenaries! How wonderful to see you!
I hope you'll stay to enjoy the charms of Isandrin now that it is free of the chaos that plagued it.

Between Ormance and Lombelle, our Order is extremely busy.
We've had to turn down three projects in Alazar.
I'm told that His Majesty King Wilburt is most upset.

Your skills on the battlefield are entertaining, to say the least, Mercenaries. I thank Saint Jeru for allowing me to witness such an impressive performance.
The reward I plan to give you will honour your great talents.

Next1.text: Take General Edor's sword without fanfare, and sell it without shame if it does not suit you. Its value is far greater than any bounty I could pay you.

Next2.text:
As for the kingdom's future, fear not – it is in good hands.
Colonel Symaque has kindly offered to serve as General. He shall remain in that role whilst I examine the possibility of restoring a Halios to the throne.

Next3.text:
Order is restored in the city, and your mistakes have been more than made up for by our victory.
I absolve you of your sins and of your debt to the Church. Go forth in peace, Mercenaries. May Saint Jeru guide you on your path.

End.text: The Legion considers General Edor's sword to be a sacred relic. Personally, I must admit I'm not sorry to see it leave the kingdom.

Start.text:
The Colonels sent on missions to other Counties will have to submit to the Hierophant's will.
As the new General, I will not tolerate any dissent.

End1.text:
Ah! You've returned to pay your respects, Mercenaries?
Excellent, I happen to have a gift for you. As a sign of my gratitude for your efforts in Isandrin.

End2.text: Maxime's head was far too small, so I've no use for his helmet. Take it! Perhaps one of your Companions will appreciate it.

Start.text: You can count on me to set the Scholars back on the right path!

The young General's remains have been unceremoniously left on the ground.
No one will mind if you take his helmet.
Judging by the bloodstains, these bonds have held many a prisoner.
This shelf contains a variety of torture manuals and implements that your Companions would rather stay away from.

MissionDesc1.text: Find the key and free Colonel Marcus.

MissionDesc2.text: Help Colonel Marcus escape.

MissionDesc3.text: Bring Colonel Marcus back to General Maxime.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Well, well! If it isn't those bothersome Mercenaries!

Next1.text: My greatest regret is not having you killed the moment you arrived in Drombach.

Start.text: Who are you? Was that you making all that noise?

Next1.text:
The General sent you to rescue me? By Saint Eleor's shield, hurry up and open this cage!
With all that noise, the Inquisitors will likely be here any second! Find the key! Hurry!

Wait.text: Keep looking, Mercenaries. That key's got to be somewhere!

Exit.text: Stop! In the name of Saint Eleor… Don't leave without me!

Start.text:
We must hurry! There's not a moment to lose!
We might still have the element of surprise on our side!

Next1.text:
As soon as we leave the jail, take the fight directly to them! Don't give the Inquisitors time to gather their wits!
Take me to the General!

Start.text:
The tunnel doesn't look stable – fresh rubble is blocking the way.
A miner could risk breaking through it.

By opening one passage, your Companions have shut down another.
Better not destabilise the tunnel any further.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the coast for any sign of a Skelmar presence.

MissionDesc2.text: Find and question the Smugglers about their activities.

MissionDesc3.text: Find out what's put the city on high alert.

MissionDesc4.text: Claim your reward from Sergeant Izore.

line0.text: Take on Sergeant Izore's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Mercenaries! Please, you must listen to me! Isandrin is in terrible danger.

Next1.text: I've been seeing lights on the coast for days now. Strange lights! And when night falls, I see shadowy figures on the moor! I'm afraid it all points to an imminent Skelmar invasion!

Next1Bis.text: My superiors are convinced it's just a gang of smugglers. They refuse to give me any men!

Next2.text: If they think that'll stop me from protecting Lombelle, they're mistaken! I'd rather pay Mercenaries out of my own pocket than let barbarians invade my county!

Next3.text:
We must leave right away!
I won't be able to focus on the riots until I'm certain that no other enemy is threatening us.

Start.text: It's an honour to receive your visit, Mercenaries!

Next1.text: You'll be happy to know that I'm now in charge of the troop that patrols the area around the Parliament.

Start.text: I never want to speak to you again, you sickening fanatics!

How did this poster end up in our Barracks?
I'd tear it down, but if anyone sees me holding it, they might think I'm complicit in all this!

Remove.text: Ah! What a relief to have that awful thing out of my sight! I hope you're paid well for your services!

Start.text: The Legionaries fell asleep in the middle of their training.

Saint Eleor be praised, the grip of my shield has come off!
While the Blacksmith takes care of that, I've finally got a moment to catch my breath.

Next1.text: I hope she's short of supplies – I'm exhausted!

Start.text:
How long can we go on like this?
This is my first break in two days!
I don't have time to talk to you, Mercenaries! Ever since Captain Evrusque died, I've had to manage two cohorts at once, spread across the whole city!

Next1.text: And I'm not the only one… We're short on officers, and almost all of our captains are overwhelmed. Not to mention our messengers, who are worn out from running all over Isandrin.

Next2.text: By Saint Eleor's shield, I'd rather be at war!

EndHierophante.text:
General Symaque has started sacking some of his officers.
It's not much fun in the Legion just now.

EndGeneral.text:
Almost all of our soldiers are on leave.
A gift from the General, after all their hard work to protect Isandrin.

Start.text: The juggler has drawn an impressive throng around him.

line0.props.tipText: Watch the performance.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the area to find the juggler.

MissionDesc2.text: Follow the juggler's trail and capture him.

MissionDesc3.text: Bring the captive juggler back to Lieutenant Mireva.

line0.text: Talk to Lieutenant Mireva.

line1.text: Take on Lieutenant Mireva's mission.

line2.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Since the Hierophant's victory, the people of Isandrin have abandoned the area...
Do you know the tale of the General of Isandrin? He was once a young man by the name of Maxime!

Song1.text: He loved his mum's stories, like all good little boys. And built a Parliament once he tired of his toys!

Song2.text: He began stealing gold from whomever he could! Preachers, merchants and farmers – and all “for their own good”...

CampDialog.text: You may have captured me, but you can't take away my freedom of thought.

Start.text: I'd rather die than be silent!
Lies! Slander! Outrage!

Next1.text: Soldiers! Seize this buffoon!

Minstrel1.text: By Saint Septimus' beard, this scoundrel's a slippery one!

Minstrel2.text: He's mocking the General! He's stoking discontent and encouraging the rioters by spreading these lies about our lord. Arresting him is a matter of public safety!

Minstrel3.text: How much can I pay you to capture him, Mercenaries? No price is too high to restore our city's peace!

Minstrel4.text: So find him! Wherever he's hiding! That ruffian can't have simply disappeared!

Captured1.text:
Ah! Mercenaries! You're back.
I hope you've got that son of a crocswine.

line0.props.tipText: Hand over the juggler to the lieutenant.

Captured2.text: He wasn't acting alone? What are you talking about? Rioters were being paid to protect him?

Captured3.text: And here I thought that once that juggler was behind bars, all our problems would be over! Now we've got to find out who this mysterious patron is, before he finds another seditious singer.

Captured4.text: The Legion won't admit defeat! We'll lock up every juggler in town if we have to! We'll find their benefactor, and we'll hang him right here!

Captured5.text: As for his corruptive influence, I've got something to keep it in check until the Legion can shut this scheme down! The greatest poet in the city has composed an ode to the General's glory at my request.

Song.text:
It wasn't supposed to be played until the juggler's execution, but the circumstances have forced our hand!
If you've got a Bard in your company, then have them play it as often as they can! That should calm things down until the Legion can silence this rebellion.

Wait.text: I'm taking this patron business very seriously. You can count on me to conduct the investigation personally. Our captive will talk.

SettingLog.text: You arrested the dissident juggler and learned of a mysterious patron.

Start.text:
I almost had him!
Why didn't you clear the way? Are you helping him?!

Just look at that scum! They're vermin, the lot of them!
They come swarming like rats to listen to the vile rantings of a juggler, then scatter like cockroaches when they see the Legion coming!

I've never written a song this quickly before!
I hope Lieutenant Mireva is satisfied!

To mock the General is to insult the Edoranian people!
I hope that juggler rots in prison!

I see things more clearly now that the juggler's been arrested.
I wonder how I let myself be so easily influenced.

The jugglers are free to sing whatever they like, as long as it's all to the General's greater glory.
The Legion's tasked me with ensuring it!

MissionDesc1.text: Tear down the poster mocking General Maxime.

MissionDesc2.text: Tear down the poster mocking General Maxime.

MissionDesc3.text: Tear down the poster mocking General Maxime.

MissionDesc4.text: Tear down the poster mocking General Maxime.

MissionDesc5.text: Find the Partisans at the University of Edoran.

line0.text: Show the Partisans your hands.

line1.text: Take on the Partisans' mission.

line2.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Think this is funny, Mercenaries?

Next1.text: I'm sure they're the ones who put up that blasted poster! We've got them now!

Next2.text: Show us your hands. And no funny business.

Quest1.text: No fishy smell. No traces of glue. They didn't do this.

Quest2.text: Just as well! The last thing we need is for our enemies to be hiring Mercenaries! We're the ones who need backup, not those miserable thugs!

Quest3.text: Yes, the Partisans wouldn't be opposed to a bit of extra help...
