Quest3Bis.text: Our group is made up of honest city-dwellers and farmers who want only to defend our General's honour – and his reforms. His Majesty wants to make his people true citizens, empowered to govern at his side, just like the Legion and the Church!

Quest4.text: Not everyone's happy with this revolution! Our opponents are putting up these dreadful posters all over the city. They're aimed at the people, turning them against their own interests by making the General look like a fool! Duty demands that we tear them down!

AcceptQuest.text:
Glad to hear it, Mercenaries! You take care of this district, and we'll handle the southern part of the city.
I've marked on your map where those posters have been spotted.

Remove1.text:
Perfect! You've got a knack for this!
Keep it up, for the glory of our General!

End1.text: Ah! Mercenaries! We've been waiting for you! Have you torn down all the posters in the district? By all the saints! Come here, we've discovered something troubling…

End1Bis.text: Remember the places we sent you to check? Well... Did you notice anything strange?

End2.text: There are posters all over the district. Even in the Legion Barracks. Except for one place...

End2Bis.text:
The University of Edoran!
Those hypocrites! We should have known! Who else would have enough ink and parchment to make all those accursed posters?

End3.text: As Partisans, it is our duty to take action! This flood of posters will end today! Will you join us, Mercenaries?

EndAccept.text:
Prepare yourselves.
The Scholars have managed to hide their true opinions from all of Isandrin, so who knows what else they're hiding?

Wait.text: Tear down those blasted posters, and don't let anyone stop you! Remember that you're working for the good of the people and the General's honour!

SettingLog.text: You tore down defamatory posters at the Partisans' behest.

Start.text: The traditionalists don't know how lucky they are to have a General like His Majesty Maxime!

EndPope.text:
It seems the destruction of the Parliament has begun.
By all the saints, what a waste!

EndGeneral.text: You know what? I wouldn't be surprised if all this chaos is Guillhem's doing! That old fogey got exactly what he deserved!

Start.text: The General only wants to share power with the people because he's not strong enough to rule alone! The Colonels should elect someone else!

EndPope.text: Colonel Symaque is the man this city needs! He'll make an excellent General!

EndGeneral.text: Have you heard about the new Hierophant? This Gedeon character… where'd he come from?

Start.text:
Thanks to the General and the schools he plans to build, Edoran will be the first kingdom whose subjects can all read!
Ah! Alazar and its Scholars are in for a shock!

EndPope.text:
Maybe learning to read wasn't all that important.
Just look at me, I've always got along fine without reading!

Start.text: Oh! I don't get involved in Edoranian politics. The situation in Gosenberg is complicated enough for my tastes!

People are talking about you in... less respectable circles, you know? You've got a certain reputation with our kind... Want to see “the lair”? But if you want to get in, you've got to be known to the authorities, if you catch my drift...

GoOk.text: We criminals need to stick together. Put these bags over your heads and follow me – I'll take you to the lair.

GoNo.text: Sorry, lads, but you're too squeaky clean to get in. We're all in the same boat here, right? So if you haven't got a bounty on you, you've no need for us.

RewardQuest.text: You've finished one of the jobs? We won't bother going all the way over there – here's your reward.

Start.text: I also had a hard time understanding why we needed a Parliament. Or even what a Parliament was!

Next1.text:
But now I'm at peace with my ignorance.
All I know is that with this Building Site, there's no shortage of work in Isandrin any more!

Start.text: Working on this site is an honour! Just think of it – a Parliament!

Next1.text: Soon, the people will have a voice, just like the Legion, the Church and the Counts do! The people of Edoran will no longer be subjects, they'll be citizens!

Start.text: Our Order was very hesitant about helping to build the Parliament. The Hierophant and the Church aren't really in favour of it… to say the least.
Colonel…

Next1.text:
You should be proud of yourself, Sergeant!
Your actions have saved many lives. Your courage and that of your Mercenaries is most admirable. If it weren't for you, that fire…

Next2.text: Colonel! Please, sir! Listen to me! That fire… the fires in Isandrin… They weren't set by individual rebels! These aren't just accidents or spontaneous events!

Next2Bis.text:
I've discovered that the rioters are organised! Someone very rich is funding them!
They're using large quantities of Alazarian powder, and…

Next3.text: Enough!

Next3Bis.text: No one ordered you to conduct an official investigation, Sergeant Izore. Your unfounded musings are useless and without merit. A military tribunal might even call them insubordination…

Next3Ter.text:
You should thank your Mercenaries, for their heroism today will spare you that humiliation.
Pay them their due, and return to your barracks. Your superiors likely have no shortage of tasks for you.

Next4.text: Out of my sight.

Start.text:
A military tribunal… Oh! Saint Eleor save me. I should have stuck to following orders.
Please, take your reward and forget about me. Forget everything.

Next1.text:
Colonel Symaque's attitude really was rather strange…
I wonder if I should take this matter to another Colonel? Or perhaps keep investigating discreetly on my own…

SettingLog.text: You discovered that someone was funding the series of fires in the capital.

Start.text: The report's not even finished and I've already lost count of all the men and materials that were lost in the fire. The construction delays will be enormous.

Next1.text: Ah! Mercenaries, if you have anything that could help the craftsmen's guilds and the disciples, we'd appreciate it. The General and his people have been waiting for this Parliament for too long. Any kind of progress will be very reassuring to them.

line0.props.tipText: Make a donation to the Parliament Building Site.

Reward1.text: Saint Lenaid bless you! Your gift will be used wisely.

Reward2.text: The guilds send me a list of their needs and requests every day. I don't want to take advantage of your generosity, but...

EndChurch.text:
I'm sorry to have wasted your time.
The Hierophant's orders are very clear: the Parliament must be removed from the city.

EndGeneral.text:
I'm happy to inform you that this Building Site no longer requires your generosity!
The General will be using Guillhem the Heretic's personal fortune to pay for the Parliament.

Start.text:
I thought the Eye's Reckoning had struck the Building Site!
Damned Alazarian powder! An unbeliever's invention!
How dare these men attack the Building Site? There were so many workers and disciples of Saint Lenaid inside!

Next1.text: I'm going to complain to the Hierophant! I demand those rioters be excommunicated!

EndChurch.text: Well, I suppose the Order of Saint Lenaid is in charge of dismantling this Building Site now.

Start.text:
They can try and destroy our Parliament, but we'll rebuild it as many times as it takes!
No one will stop us from deciding our future!

EndLegion.text: We may need a few more years to finish building the Parliament, but we remain determined as ever!

MissionDesc1.text: Fight the juggler's protectors and capture him.

Start.text: Old junk that's been packed away and forgotten.
Shame on the Partisans! Shame on the infidels who support General Maxime! Shame on all those who seek power, for they are the ones least worthy of it!

Next1.text:
The peasant's place is in the field! The soldier's place is on the front lines!
The Scholars and the clerics are the rightful leaders of the people!
True believers follow only Hierophant Guillhem VII!

Next2.text:
Faithful disciples! Turn your faces to the Light!
Remain on the path laid out by Saint Jeru, our guide! Protect your city from General Maxime with your faith, or Isandrin will be struck by the Eye's Reckoning!

Start.text: I pray every day for General Maxime to abandon his heretical reforms!

Next1.text: I don't want to be hit by the Eye's Reckoning.

Start.text: I didn't know Edoranian priests got so involved in politics.

Next1.text:
They've got too much free time, if you ask me.
Make them take care of people with the Plague like in Gosenberg, and the General and his Partisans will have nothing to worry about.

Start.text: Are you here for the juggler?

Next1.text:
I'm afraid you won't be getting that bounty, Mercenaries.
His patron is paying us handsomely to keep him alive.

Bride1.text:
Haha! Keep your Krowns.
That patron is richer than you'll ever be.

Bard2.text:
That juggler is under our protection!
His patron is paying us handsomely to keep him alive.

Start.text: My patron will hear of this! He'll come to get me! The Legion won't be able to do anything for you!
Tell me what you want, but be quick about it. Whenever I take my eyes off my servant, she's skiving off before you know it.

NoServant.text:
What do you want?
Going to steal another servant from me?

Start.text:
I used to think my troop was invincible, too!
I'd swan about in the taverns like I was the queen of Alazar!
And then Isandrin happened...

Next1.text: Don't take any contracts, just get out of Lombelle! Or you'll end up like me, cleaning privies for this damn tavern keeper!

Recruit1.text:
You... you want me to join your troop?
Oh! Saint Eleor has answered my prayers!

Recruit2.text: I'll join you right away! I'll prove myself worthy, I swear!

Start.text: I forbid you to touch that poster! Hands off!

Next1.text: The people need to know they're being ruled by an incompetent liar!

Next2.text:
All the Partisans can think of is a lovely Parliament building where they can play at being Ancients, but we know it'll just mean taxes that prevent us from feeding our children!
That poster's simply telling the truth!

Start.text:
Easy to get distracted in a city like Isandrin, isn't it?
Do you need a little help to refocus on what really matters?

Done.text: I was just as intrigued by this information as you are.

line0.props.tipText: Seditious posters are popping up all over Isandrin, much to the Legion's dismay.

line1.props.tipText: A juggler's satirical performances are fanning the flames of discontent and making General Maxime into a laughingstock.

line2.props.tipText: Disturbing things are happening after nightfall in the suburbs of Isandrin.

line3.props.tipText: Palace authorities have lost contact with the cart that collects taxes in Lombelle.

line4.props.tipText: The Legion's colonels are furious: one of their own has been captured and jailed by the Inquisition.

line5.props.tipText: Rumour has it that a Skelmar invasion of Lombelle is imminent.

line6.props.tipText: Alderwoman Mara's pleas have had no effect: city authorities are too busy to go after the bandits.

Mission1.text: Seditious posters are popping up all over Isandrin, much to the Legion's dismay.

Mission2.text: A juggler's satirical performances are fanning discontent and making General Maxime into a laughingstock.

Mission3.text: Disturbing things are happening after nightfall in the suburbs of Isandrin.

Mission4.text: Palace authorities have lost contact with the cart that collects taxes in Lombelle.

Mission5.text: The Legion's colonels are furious: one of their own has been captured and jailed by the Inquisition.

Mission6.text: Rumour has it that a Skelmar invasion of Lombelle is imminent.

Mission7.text: Alderwoman Mara's pleas have had no effect: city authorities are too busy to go after the bandits.

DeliverMessage1.text: I hope they used the right code this time...

End.text: I have no other rumours to sell you. My apologies.

Start.text: A poster is caught under this closed door.

line0.props.tipText: Pick the door's lock.

Start.text: It seems another purge is under way at the University of Edoran.

MissionDesc1.text: Search the area for clues about the posters.

MissionDesc2.text: Attack and defeat the Scriptorium Students.

MissionDesc3.text: Demand an explanation from the Dean of the University of Edoran.

MissionDesc4.text: Claim your reward from the Partisans in the Scriptorium.

Start.text: Just look at that! Those Edoranian Scholars and their fancy airs...

Next1.text: I bet they think we're too stupid to govern!

Next2.text: Let's keep our eyes peeled. Someone or something will give them away eventually.

Start.text:
The University of Edoran is proud to count General Maxime among its alumni.
It was here that our beloved leader learned everything he knows about the Ancients.

Next1.text:
Our predecessors' legacy was a great source of inspiration for his reforms.
We take pride in guiding him on this path, even to this day.

Start.text: Before General Maxime's reign, the theologians were the most respected and influential Scholars at the University of Edoran.

Next1.text: They were very quick to criticise the new reforms, but fortunately, we were quick to get rid of them!

Start.text:
Scholars are a part of the people. We too shall sit in Parliament.
Those who oppose the General are too stupid to be part of the University!
Isn't General Maxime going a little too fast?

Next1.text: Oh! I was just thinking out loud! Far be it from me to criticise His Majesty!

Next2.text: Just look at it from the people's perspective, and the Church's! With all these changes coming in left and right, it's throwing off everyone's routines!

Wait.text: Please forget what I said. I don't want to be thrown out of the University!

Start.text:
You won't hear anyone criticising His Majesty here!
The university insists on it!
The Students are trying to lay low until they learn what's in store for them.

Next1.text: The Students don't seem all that thrilled with their new subject.

Start.text: A barrel full of glue. From the smell, you can confirm it was made from boiled fish.
Oh! By Saint Eleor! Intruders! We're under attack!

Next1.text:
You shouldn't have come here, Mercenaries.
You're disturbing the Scholars' concentration.

Start.text: By all the saints! What's going on here?

Next1.text:
Don't try to act innocent, Dean!
We know all about your scheme!

Next1Bis.text:
Your Scholars are working with the rioters!
They're the ones drawing these vile posters!

Next2.text:
The University is guilty of insults to the Crown!
The Legion will hear of this! They'll tear this place down! All these lovely stones will come in handy for building the Parliament!

Next3.text: What…?

Next4.text:
That's impossible! The University has always been loyal to General Maxime! I was even his professor! It was I who purged our ranks when he ascended to the throne!
Oh! As Saint Serene is my witness, I knew nothing of this… this treason!

Next5.text:
Please! Don't tell the Legion about this dishonour!
I'm sure we can come to an agreement!

Wait.text: How could the students have sullied our University's honour?

Start.text:
The Dean has proposed putting the Students to work in support of the Partisans' cause.
Starting right now, they will draw posters to the glory of our General!

Next1.text:
Thanks to these posters, the people will finally understand His Majesty's true greatness!
City-dwellers and farmers from every County will unite under his banner!

Next2.text: None of this would have been possible without your help. And so, in addition to the promised reward, allow me to present you with the first set of posters drawn up by our new allies.

Next3.text:
Paste them up wherever you can! And don't lose hope!
Our adversaries have only a limited supply remaining! The war of the posters will inevitably turn to our advantage!

SettingLog.text: You recruited artists to defend the General's cause.

Start.text:
Welcome to the County of Lombelle, Mercenaries.
I hope your Companions didn't get too seasick!

Next1.text: My ship runs the Arthes route in both directions. Just give the signal, and I'll take you back where I found you!

line0.props.tipText: Sail to the County of Arthes.

Alt1.text:
I'm ready to set sail for Arthes.
Will you be on board for the trip, Mercenaries?

line0.props.tipText: Sail to the County of Arthes.

Start.text: Whatever your motivations may be, what matters is that you help the General to restore order in Isandrin.

MissionDesc1.text: Help the Legion to get the cart out of the rut.

MissionDesc2.text: Collect your reward from Corporal Berthus.

MissionDesc3.text: Escort Corporal Berthus and his cart to the capital.

line0.text: Take on Corporal Berthus's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: The cart's wheels are sunk deep in the mud. It'll take the strength of several men to get it out.

Aha, some Mercenaries!
You couldn't have come at a better time!

Next1.text: This damn cart is stuck. We've tried everything to get it out, but it simply won't move. This is one tough rut; you have no idea!

Next2.text:
Could one of your strong lads give us a hand?
I can compensate you for your efforts, but be quick about it. After all, this thing contains the taxes for the whole county of Lombelle!

Chariot.text: Choose your helpers carefully! This cart is extremely heavy!

Success.text:
You've done it! We can finally get moving again!
Let's hitch up the pony!

End1.text: Ah! Your reward – I almost forgot. Take it, you've earned it! Haha!

End2.text:
Say, while I've got you here, could you perhaps escort us to the capital? Just in case this damn cart gets stuck again!
We're already quite late, you see...

End3.text: Wonderful, glad to hear it! Just follow us, then! Isandrin's not too far off.

SettingLog.text: You helped the tax collectors get back on the road.

Start.text: Colonel Ansald will kill us when he finds out the tax income for the whole County is stuck in a damned rut!

Next1.text: What strength! Have you ever thought of joining the Legion?

Start.text: Oh! No! It's not that we don't want to help the Legion!

Next0.text: This cart is much too heavy for us. We're just simple farmers!

Next1.text: Oh! By Saint Eleor, they weren't supposed to leave so soon!

Start.text: What do you want me to say? The fields are full of ruts! Those soldiers should have just looked where they were going instead of counting our gold!

Next1.text:
Why d'you hafta get involved, anyway?
Ain't you got enough bandits to chase?

Start.text: Are you from Omelas' family? His death and his wife's weren't enough to make up for their crimes! There's still a hefty fee to pay.

Next1.text:
They plotted with a gang of looters! Set a trap for Legionaries! Attempted to steal the County's taxes!
And Saint Jeru only knows what other crimes those two are guilty of.

Start.text: Do you think that with a Parliament, we'll be able to keep hanging peasants like that? Without getting a judge involved?

Next1.text:
A Parliament would only have complicated things!
With traitors and peasants, there's no need for a trial!

Start.text: The bear known as Old Brown has been dead for a while. Just because the meat smells a bit strong doesn't mean we should let it go to waste!
The troop's full at the moment. If we need a new Companion, we'll let you know.

Next1.text: Right now, we'd just like to relax. After the contract we just finished, we could use some peace and quiet.

Start.text:
Go ahead and mine some iron deposits if you like!
A few pickaxes won't wake Martial up. He sleeps like a log.
The Mercenary is sound asleep. His last mission must have been exhausting.

Mercenaries! It's me! Melkior!
I've remembered the place marked on the map! …

Next1.text:
You've already killed everyone?
Damn! It's better to be with you than against you!
Well, at least you solved the problem...

Next1Bis.text: What do you mean, the problem isn't solved? You're telling me those men were hired to execute the Trackers?

Next2.text:
Whoever is paying them must really not like those savages! Laying hands on Trackers is a crime!
Maybe I should talk to the Legion directly about this. It might earn me a promotion...

Next3.text: Well... I don't think I have any further need of you! My boys will collect those killers' heads, and I'll handle the report. The Saviour of the Suburbs and the Protector of Peace, that's what they'll call me now!

Wait.text: The Saviour of the Suburbs and the Protector of Peace, that's what they'll call me now!

SettingLog.text: You discovered that Mercenaries were hired to take out Lombelle's Trackers.

Start.text: Judging by the dagger stuck in this woman's back, a couple of Inquisitors had a score to settle.
With everything going on in the city, you'll have no shortage of Outlaws to bring to us! You should know that the Guard offers a handsome reward to those who help keep the peace in our fair city!

Deliver.text: Take your Krowns, Mercenaries, and fear not: this rogue will have a fair trial.

DeliverEnd.text: Take your Krowns, Mercenaries, and fear not: this rogue will have a fair trial.

NoSlotAvailable.text: Come back in a few days, Mercenaries. The prison is full to bursting.

Start.text: My patron never came to get me. After all I've done for him, he's abandoned me!

Next1.text: I couldn't even get my revenge by telling the Legion his name. That hypocrite made sure he never told me who he was!

Next3.text: By the saints! I'm going to be hanged, Mercenaries! Hanged like a common bandit!

Recruit1.text:
What makes you think I'd want to join your troop after everything you've put me through?
It's your fault I'm in this mess!

Start.text:
No! Don't leave! Please!
I was only joking!
Don't leave me here! I'm coming!

MissionDesc1.text: Search the camp, and leave nothing behind!

MissionDescAlt1.text: Search the camp for anything that might be of interest to Alderwoman Mara.

MissionDesc2.text: Report on your mission to Alderwoman Mara.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: A few scrolls are scattered on the table, and one of them in particular catches your Companions' attention.

line0.props.tipText: Take the list of names.

Start.text: By the saints! What incredible talent, Mercenaries! How did you know which of your men to send in?

Next1.text:
I must admit, none of mine are even a tenth as good as yours.
It would be most rude of me to lay claim to the reward, or even to the Bandits' possessions.

Next2.text:
We'll settle for the leftovers – I won't make a fuss. Just let me know when you're done robbing the corpses and searching the chests.
Don't miss anything you'll regret leaving behind!

Failure1.text:
Huh! What a bloodbath.
I doubt you'll get any reward at all for this.

Failure2.text: If I were you, I'd collect some souvenirs of the city-dwellers to bring back to their families. With any luck, the alderwoman will at least pay you for that.

Mid1.text: At least there are a few prisoners left to testify on your behalf. I've seen contracts come to worse ends... And better ones, too...

Mid2.text: If I were you – Saint Eleor forbid! – I'd collect the personal effects of the dead city-dwellers and bring them back to their families. Otherwise, I don't think you'll get much by way of a reward for this mission.

Wait.text: Did you find anything?

End1.text:
What did you find?
Mind if I take a look?

End2.text:
It looks like those Bandits weren't just kidnapping people at random. Look – there are more names than hostages.
And isn't that the alderwoman's name?

End3.text:
You'd better show her this.
The city-dwellers seem to be facing a more powerful enemy than a mere gang of bandits. In my experience, this kind of information is worth its weight in Krowns.

End4.text:
I'll take care of the prisoners, Mercenaries – you go on ahead.
Be careful out there, it looks like the Bandits weren't acting alone.

EndAlt.text:
Well... This is where we part ways.
The Brotherhood won't want its members to be associated with your failure!

Start.text: <narrator>This poor man has been dead for some time. Maybe since the Brotherhood's first attack on the Bandits' lair.</narrator>
You've saved us! Oh, Saint Jeru be praised!

Next1.text: Those Bandits made our lives hell, Mercenaries! If you only knew!

Next2.text: Once I'm sworn in to Parliament, I vow to tear this place down and drive out every single Bandit who dares to set foot in Lombelle!

Mid1.text: I... Oh! By Saint Jeru! So many dead!

Mid2.text:
I know you did what you could, but...
These people didn't deserve to die like this.

Mid3.text:
I swear that as soon as I'm sworn in to Parliament, I'll fight to avenge their memory!
This place will be torn down to the very last stone!

MissionDesc1.text: Search the camp for clues.

MissionDesc2.text: Look for the place marked on the Assassins' Map.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: This bag doesn't look like those used by the clans in Harag.

Bah! Now I understand why the Ghost Pack turned up so close to Isandrin.
What a bloodbath! Even the druid was killed.

Next1.text:
Of course, this means war. War, Mercenaries! Harag will attack us! Will the General send me to the front?
Oh, Saint Eleor! I don't want to die in a swamp!

Next2.text:
We've got to send the killers' heads straight to the Clans! I don't see any other way to calm those savages down!
Think of something! Anything! The killers must have left some kind of clues!

Wait.text: Did you find something?

Map1.text:
What's that? A map?
Is that all?

Map2.text:
Oh, for the Eye's sake! And meanwhile, the General's spending all our gold on his stupid reforms!
The Legion isn't ready for a war with Harag! Not ready at all, Mercenaries!

Map3.text:
You've got to find the place marked on this map.
As for me, I'm going to buy us some time. Yep! I'll hide the bodies so no one can find them!

EndWait.text: Hmm, am I better off burning the bodies or burying them?

Start.text:
The competition between Mercenary companies is really tough in Isandrin!
Don't rest on your laurels, or your rivals will take everything you've worked for!

Respec.text:
Now that's what I call a strategic decision!
May Saint Eleor guide your Companion on the path of excellence.

Start.text: Three riots! And that's only today!

Next1.text: By the saints! How did these commoners learn to fight like that?

Start.text: Did anything strike you as odd about where the Brotherhood members come from? It seems they're all from Gosenberg.

Next1.text: Mercenary companies don't tend to be too picky about such things. I wonder what's behind it.

Start.text: Sending the Edoranian Legion to attack the Saint Septimus Basilica? This is blasphemy, General Maxime!

Next0.text:
I have no intention of attacking a holy site, if Hierophant Guillhem agrees to surrender.
Once he's turned himself in, I vow that he will be judged fairly…

Next1.text: Hierophant Guillhem VII is a sacred individual! No man can judge him for his actions!

Next2.text:
Symaque! Accursed traitor!
Have you no shame? How dare you show your face before the General?

Next3.text:
Enough!
Negotiation is useless. I have already been too lenient with the Church.

Next4.text:
Colonels! Soldiers! Mercenaries!
Prepare for combat!
We must enter the Basilica! The Hierophant must answer for his crimes!

Start.text:
This is my final offer, General.
Step down now, and you will be spared from the stake.

Next1.text:
What gives you the right to threaten me like that, Hierophant?
You! The traitor who pushed Isandrin into chaos!

Next2.text:
I was only protecting the kingdom and our faith from your harmful influence.
With just one word from me, order will be restored. I will guide the people along the path of the Light, as is my role.

Next2Bis.text: You will guide…? So you think you're a General now? Shame on you, Guillhem, and on all the fanatics who support you! You're the ones who deserve to be burned alive!

Next3.text: Well, if that's how it's going to be…

Next4.text:
Inquisitors! Mercenaries!
General Maxime has refused my clemency. I order you to attack the Palace!
Today, the God of Light retakes control of the kingdom!

Start.text:
It seems the Legion suspects Alazar of being involved in the city's troubles.
As if we were behind everything that goes wrong!

Mercenaries? Are you Mercenaries?
Oh! Please! You've got to help us!
Someone's got to do something!

Next1.text:
The situation's completely out of control! It's outright civil war!
The flames will consume our homes and businesses! And the plundering…

Next2.text: You are General Maxime's guests! You're in his debt! The Legion needs your help! You must help them contain the Riot.

Next3.text: Tell us what you need, and the craftsmen of Isandrin will do whatever it takes to ensure your victory.

Again1.text: Oh no, not again! By all the saints! Why won't the General just give up on his ridiculous plans?

Again2.text: May the Beast devour you, you great coward!

Again3.text: If you need the Isandrin craftsmen's help, then we're all determined to help you! What do you need?

Done.text:
So? Are you ready to go and fight for Isandrin now?
You're going to fight, aren't you?

MissionSupportCrisis.text: The Isandrin craftsmen are asking for your help.

Start.text: By all the saints! This tower is better defended than a fortress!

More Mercenaries?
By the saints, that alderwoman's been hiring anyone she can find.
So, how goes it, dear colleagues?

Next1.text: My men and I are looking for some way into that tower to free the Isandrin residents held by those cursed Bandits. We've already tried attacking head-on as we usually do, and it turned into a bloodbath...

Next2.text:
Oh! Not for us, of course. But for the prisoners, yes!
Any time those fiends felt threatened, they ran straight to the nearest city-dweller and cut their throat. I'm not sure the alderwoman will pay for dead bodies!

Next2Bis.text:
The best strategy we've come up with is to send in a small group of men, get the prisoners to safety, then eliminate the bandits.
The only problem is, it's such a risky plan that none of us wants to volunteer.

Next3.text:
If you want to try your luck, we'll gladly step aside.
I don't want to be responsible for losing any more prisoners.

line0.props.tipText: Infiltrate the camp.

Alt1.text:
Well, well! Mercenaries! Are you here for the reward?
City-dwellers have been kidnapped by the Bandits in this tower. The alderwoman of Isandrin is promising a nice bounty to whoever can set them free.

Alt2.text: My men and I have been trying to find a way in. With very little success, I'm afraid. We've already tried attacking head-on as we usually do, and it turned into a bloodbath.

Alt3.text:
Oh! Not for us, of course. But for the prisoners, yes!
Any time those fiends felt threatened, they ran straight to the nearest city-dweller and cut their throat. I'm not sure the alderwoman will pay for dead bodies!

Alt3Bis.text:
The best strategy we've come up with is to send in a small group of men, get the prisoners to safety, then eliminate the bandits.
The only problem is, it's such a risky plan that none of us wants to volunteer.

Alt4.text:
If you want to try your luck, we'll gladly step aside.
I don't want to be responsible for losing any more prisoners.

line0.props.tipText: Infiltrate the camp.

Start.text: Where did you come from? What the...

Next1.text: The Colonel! He's getting away! Don't let him escape!

Start.text:
I... I think we've lost them.
You're better than I thought.

Next1.text:
Well! Let's not hang around here.
The Inquisitors are known for their tenacity. I won't be safe until I'm back in the General's Palace!

Start.text:
Move along, Mercenaries.
Only Inquisitors are allowed inside the Commandery.

Next1.text:
Hold on, Mercenaries.
Your faces look familiar, somehow. Come a little closer...

Start.text:
Take cover! Get behind the walls!
The Ghost Pack is attacking the city!

Next1.text: Oh! By Saint Jeru! Every man for himself! The suburbs are lost! There's nothing more to be done for them!

line0.props.tipText: Face the Pack yourselves.

Next2.text:
You... you want to fight the monsters?
Have you lost your minds?

Start.text:
The Pack disappeared with the first rays of sunlight.
Do you think they'll come back tonight?
Are the monsters really dead? Are you sure? Would you swear to it before the God of Light?

Next0.text:
Phew, what a relief!
I really thought we had lost the suburbs. The General's popularity would have taken a serious hit – and my career, too! Ha!
You've earned your reward... unlike those savages from Harag!

Next1.text: Where were they, anyhow? It's the Trackers' job to hunt the Ghost Pack! Not the Guard's job, and certainly not yours, Mercenaries'!

Next2.text:
I won't let this injustice go unpunished! They're going to pay you for doing their work for them!
Meet me at their pathetic camp. I swear I won't let them pay with those disgusting fangs of theirs!

Start.text:
What do you want?
Where did you find that map?

Next1.text: Yes, it was our company who took care of the Trackers. I can't say it was the most enjoyable contract we've ever taken on, but you know how it is. When you're a Mercenary, you don't always get to do what you want.

Next2.text: Oh! You want to send our heads to Harag? Our sponsor warned us this might happen. And we're ready.

Start.text: What the... The pony!

Next1.text:
We're under attack! To arms! Protect the cart!
Those sons of crocswine mustn't get their hands on the tax money!

Next2.text: And you, Mercenaries – get ready to cover us! We must reach Isandrin, whatever it takes! If we stop moving, we're dead!

Start.text: May the Beast devour me if those rioters weren't in cahoots with that other yokel, Omelas! I'll send a Guard patrol his way as soon as we're through the gates of this damn city... that'll teach him to rebel!

Next1.text: Those peasants! Did you see how far they're willing to go to avoid paying? People want parliaments and schools, but not the taxes that go with them! Illiterate ingrates!

Next2.text:
Bah! You're not here to talk politics, though, are you, lads?
Here, take your reward.
We're close enough to Isandrin now, so we should be able to cross the drawbridge without you holding our hands!

SettingLog.text: You discovered that farmers and rioters had joined forces to lay a trap for the Legion.

Start.text:
By Jeru! I feel so stupid.
My superiors were right: all those lights and that suspicious activity were just a gang of Smugglers! I'm sorry to have bothered you for something so trivial.

Next0.text: That being said, I have a bad feeling about that smell. The Smugglers must have been hauling an ungodly amount of Alazarian powder for the smell to persist like that.

Next1.text:
I know I must be trying your patience, but I've got to find out who that cargo was going to.
Please, help me just a little more.

Next2.text:
Oh! Saint Eleor bless your kindness!
This would have bothered me for days.
Let's find those Smugglers!

Next3.text:
None of this makes any sense. A rioter who's rich enough to get his hands on Alazarian powder? And what was he going to do with it?
Unless...

Next4.text:
The city's bells! It can't be a coincidence!
Quick! We must return to Isandrin! The city is in danger!

Start.text: Sorry, Mercenaries, you're too late! We've already sold off our stock, and...

Sergeant... ! I didn't recognise you.
Wh... how... how much did you hear...? ?

Next1.text: Enough to know that you're the men I've been looking for!

Next1Bis.text:
Who did you sell your cargo of Alazarian powder to? And how much of it was there?
Tell me, or I'll send you to rot in prison for the rest of your days!

Next2.text: Come on, now! Alazarian powder?... We'd never bring something that dangerous into Edoran!

line0.props.tipText: Force the Smuggler to tell the truth.

line1.props.tipText: Convince the Smuggler to tell the truth.

Convince.text: So you give me your word? My men and I will be free to go?

Fire1.text: All right, it's true. We did sell some Alazarian powder. And not just a little bit, Sergeant. The order was so big, our boats nearly sank under the weight of it.

Fire2.text: The buyer was a man. He wore an armour with no colours on it, and had a strong Isandrin accent. At first, I thought he was a deserter or one of your rioters, but he paid for the whole cargo then and there! I don't know many outlaws who carry that much cash around with them!

Start.text: Don't kill me! Please! I'll talk!

Next1.text: We did sell some Alazarian powder! A lot of it. Our boats nearly sank under the weight of it!

Next2.text: The buyer... the buyer was a man! He wore an armour with no colours on it, and had a strong Isandrin accent. I... I thought he was a deserter, or some kind of rioter! But... he could afford to pay for all that Alazarian powder!

Start.text: The Parliament! The Building Site is on fire!

Next1.text: And that smell…

Next2.text:
By Saint Jeru, those rioters have lost their minds!
We must stop them – there are dozens of labourers at the Work Site!

Start.text: I was so excited at the thought of becoming one of the first parliamentarians of the modern era! I had hundreds of ideas to share with His Majesty to improve the daily lives of our citizens.

Next1.text: But alas, no one voted for me. No one. Not a single vote. Absolutely humiliating.

Next2.text: What's the use in carrying on if everyone hates me?

line0.props.tipText: Convince the man he will win the next election.

line1.props.tipText: Tell the man that the Parliament no longer exists.

line2.props.tipText: Take the man back to Isandrin by force.

Start.text: You think so? You really think I've got a chance to win in the next election?

Next1.text: You're probably right! All my opponents are idiots. Once the voters realise that, they'll give me their votes.

Next2.text:
Thank you for helping me see the truth, Mercenaries!
Take this, I kept it in case death took too long to find me.

Alt1.text:
What? The Parliament's gone?
The Hierophant's taken control of the city?
General Maxime is dead?

Alt2.text:
Well, good! That's all I have to say!
Ha! The people didn't want to elect me – that's proof enough they can't be trusted with the vote!

Alt3.text:
I had set this aside in case death took too long to find me.
Take it, please – I don't need it to make my triumphant return to Isandrin!

Start.text: If you're looking for Inquisitor Drucille's killer, look no further. It was me.

Next1.text: She'd gone delusional, accusing everyone of being a heretic – merchants, legionaries, bears…

Next2.text: When she attacked those poor people fleeing from the Skelmar, that was the last straw. I lured her into the Mount Pride Mine and stabbed her until she was dead. It's what Saint Eleor would have done.

Next3.text:
You can try to capture me, Mercenaries, and turn me over to the Inquisition so they can burn me alive.
Or you can act in accordance with the precepts of the Light and let me escape with these poor people.

line1.props.tipText: Help the refugees make their way to Alazar.

Help.text:
Finally, some true believers!
You can trust me, I'll lead these refugees to safety and disappear with them.
You can just say you killed me and claim your reward.

MissionGhostPack1.text: Inspect the suburbs to find out what has been terrorising the residents.

MissionGhostPack4.text: Wait until nightfall to attack the Ghost Pack.

MissionGhostPack5.text: Meet up with Guard Melkior at the Trackers' camp.

MissionGhostPack6.text: Kill the mercenaries who murdered the Trackers.

MissionGhostPack7.text: Claim your reward from Guard Melkior.

MissionPropaganda1.text: Inform the Partisans of your success.

MissionRansom1.text: Agree to help the Brotherhood free the hostages.

MissionRansom2.text: Infiltrate the Bandits' tower to save the city-dwellers.

MissionFinalGeneral.text: Listen to what General Maxime has to say.

MissionFinalHierophante.text: Listen to what Hierophant Guillhem VII has to say.

MissionCrisis.text: Help the [Legion] restore order in the city.

MissionRiot.text: Help [TheGuard] prevent chaos from taking over the city.

MissionDescDesignMission1.text: Bring the failed candidate back to his family.

Start.text: Carefully hidden boats and a fire that someone tried to camouflage... There's no doubt about it, this is a Smugglers' camp. The only odd thing is that stench of sulphur.
These Smugglers came to an unfortunate end.
This poster is shockingly effective at disparaging General Maxime: your Companions are already starting to doubt him.

StartLegion.text: A poster to the glory of General Maxime Aclesien.

Start.text: The Legionaries never saw the danger coming. They died in their sleep.
These Merchants never made it to Lombelle Harbour.
A poster mocking the General has been put up here.

line0.props.tipText: Replace this poster with another one glorifying the General.

Start.text: Wait, are you sure you want to go down? What if it is another trap?!

line0.props.tipText: Go down anyway.

MissionDesc.text: Speak with the apothecary's apprentice.

Start.text: What took you so long? Was it that difficult to capture a mere apprentice?

Next2.text: Who are you? Where are my men?

Start.text: This man has been dead for a long time, but you notice he is wearing an apothecary's outfit. He may have relatives who want to know what became of him.
He was... my uncle. He is dead.

Next.text:
How can this be? Why would anyone murder an apothecary?
And who would go to all that trouble to try and kill me, too?

Next2.text: Go on without me, I can't possibly leave him like this. Thank you for bringing me here so I could learn of his fate.

SettingLog.text: You discovered what happened to the apothecary from Marheim.

End.text: Please go, I'd rather do this on my own.

Start.text: Welcome to the local arena! You can register up to four fighters. You are not allowed to kill your opponent, but no holds are barred.

NoBeginArena.text: Too bad... I live for the arena!

OnLeaveArena.text: Feel free to come back when you're up for it!

Completed.text: Congratulations - you are now the reigning champions of the arena! As the rules dictate, you can walk away with the weapon of the previous champion, Smot.

Reward1.text:
If you want to fight again, get ready for an even greater challenge
now that our fighters know you!

ArenaLost.text: So close! All you needed was a bit of luck... or talent!

ArenaDiff.text: Smot is available and wants a rematch. Are you ready?

line0.props.tipText: Take on the Arena again in Hard mode.

CompletedDiff1.text: By the Beast's fangs, you don't mess around!

CompletedDiff2.text: Here's your reward. Well deserved, once again.

CompletedDiff3.text: Enjoy it. It's the last one you'll get in this arena. Feel free to come back for the sake of it.

ArenaAgain.text: Do you need exercise, Mercenaries? This arena will gladly be of service. Let me just remind you that there won't be any rewards to claim.

line0.props.tipText: Take on the Arena again in Hard mode.

CompletedAgain.text: As usual, you gave us an amazing tournament. Come back whenever you want!

Start.text: My wares are aplenty, but I only sell to Arena Champions! Prove your worth and come back to see me.

Alt.text: It is a great honour for me to offer you my wares!

Start.text: Yes, I was sold as part of the mill. It was a real selling point for the new owners.
I bought this mill with the gold I earned during my time as a gladiator.

Next1.text: I sometimes miss the atmosphere of the arena, but I don't miss the risk of losing a limb at the slightest mistake.

Next2.text: I can teach you a few of my dagger techniques. But first, you'll need to prove your skills in Smot's Arena.

Next3.text: So I hear the arena was a doddle for you? Ah! In that case, you definitely deserve a small reward from a veteran like myself!

End.text: Passing on my knowledge almost brings a tear to my eye: you are a bit like my successors now.

line0.title: Gladiatorial Legacy
line0.props.helpTip: Return to the former gladiator after completing Smot's Arena.

Start.text: Animals can't pick locks as far as I am aware, so this cage must have been opened by a human.
I tame wild animals for a living... But without a wild animal to tame, I am nothing!

Next1.text: It took me years to perfect this wolf's skills! I taught him everything: to sit up and beg, to walk on embers and even to fish!

Next2.text: If you ever come across my partner, bring him back to me. You can't miss him; he is quite large and wears a collar.

line0.props.tipText: Bring Buddy back to its owner.

line1.props.tipText: Inform him of Buddy's passing

Give1.text: Oh my! Buddy, my little one!

Give2.text: I was so worried I'd never see him again, and yet, here he is!

Give3.text: Thank you, Mercenaries, I have found my purpose again! Take this. It's my most prized possession, after Buddy, of course.

End.text: We're going to get some rest before setting out for Gosenberg.

Warn1.text: Did you have to kill him? Oh! By the All-seeing Eye! No! My poor Buddy!

Warn2.text: Here, take this, I no longer need it. Without my partner, I am no artist. I am nothing!

line0.title: The Wild Animal Tamer
line0.props.helpTip: Find the tamer's wolf somewhere in Vertruse.

Start.text: If we don't find the damn wolf, we'll miss the Arena Clash! This tournament is only held once a year!

Given.text: Glad to see that beast back in its cage.

Dead.text: Dead? Oh, by the All-seeing Eye! That idiot is going to cry his eyes out for hours!

Start.text: How could this animal open its cage unnoticed in the dead of night?

Given.text: Glad to have him back. He was never any good on stage, but with him around, we don't have to take turns keeping watch at night.

Dead.text: Poor Buddy. I'd really started to care for the beast.

Start.text: The canvas covering this tent looks like a tapestry. A very expensive one...

line0.title: An Exquisite Tent
line0.props.helpTip: Retrieve the tapestry covering one of the tents in the camp.

Start.text: Buy something from me. We need the money to pass the Harag border without having to climb the mountains.
Apologies if we made you feel unwelcome. We've been hiding in the forest for a week now. We're a bit on edge.

Next2.text: So, erm... welcome to our camp. Please share a meal with us.

Tent.text: You! Don't touch that, it's ours!

line0.props.tipText: Threaten to take the tapestry.

line1.props.tipText: Take the tapestry forcefully.

line2.props.tipText: Convince them that the weaver needs it back.

Threat1.text: We trusted you! We welcomed you into our camp and this is how you repay us?

Threat2.text: There, take the blasted tapestry and leave!

Convinced1.text: Oh, I had no idea its maker needed it so much. To be honest, I only took it because it was large enough to be used as tent canvas.

Convinced2.text: But you can take it back to him, we will make do without it.

Start.text: Stay away from me!

Next1.text: Leave me in peace! Let me be!

Next2.text: The young man is sobbing and struggles to speak.

line0.title: Hot coals
line0.props.helpTip: Get the Vertruse Black Market reward.

Start.text: I came here for business, but I won't say no to a little bet.
This pit's theme is incredibly exciting.
I first learned about Black Markets whilst visiting Vertruse. No one told me there was one in Ludern, too!
You're the Baron's guests? He'll really let just anyone in!

Next1.text: You can sign some Companions up for a pit fight, if you think they've got any chance of winning.

line0.props.tipText: Fight in the pit.

FightLost1.text: I can't say I'm surprised. It was obvious you weren't up to the challenge.

line0.props.tipText: Fight in the pit.

FightWin1.text: How did you manage to win?!

FightWin2.text:
Tsk! You got lucky.
I'm willing to bet you won't win the next fight.

line0.props.tipText: Fight in the pit.

Renounce.text:
Well? Giving up, Mercenaries?
Just as well, you're not ready for this pit.

FightRedo.text:
You want me to congratulate you for winning the same fight again?
Pff...
Try taking on something new, then we'll see.

line0.props.tipText: Fight in the pit.

WholePitWin1.text: I have to admit, that was an impressive fight... In fact, that makes five impressive fights! Here's your special reward, then. Happy?

WholePitWin2.text: Enjoy it, this is the first time I've given this helmet out to strangers.

WholePitWinAgain1.text:
All right, you've managed to finish all the fights we offer here.
I'll admit it – you're tough. Is that what you want to hear?

WholePitWinAgain2.text:
This is the last reward: no one will pay for fights if they know what the outcome will be.
But if you want to try again in your free time, I won't be the one to stop you.

PitNoGain.text: Again? Remember, there's no reward, Mercenaries! You'll be fighting for nothing!

line0.props.tipText: Fight in the pit.

Start.text:
I can't attend your fight, of course.
It wouldn't be too smart to leave my goods unsupervised.
The stall is filled with special rewards for the best pit fighters. The henchman watches carefully to make sure you take only your own reward.

line0.props.tipText: Get the reward corresponding to your level of Fame.

MissionDesc.text: Find Corene and free her.

Start.text: You! You abducted me! I will have you hung as soon as...

Next1.text: ... You killed Brunhilde Adr Alazar to free me? But weren't you following her orders?

Next2.text: I am confused... I... I just want to get out of here.

MissionDesc.text: Find Clemens Ald Marheim's men with Corene.

Start.text: It is my duty to protect the Alazar family.
I consider this place as my home: Alazar and Gosenberg formed a single kingdom before it was divided by the Brokers' treachery.
How ironic! Clemens sent my own people to kill me! I don't suppose you mentioned abducting his fiancée...

Next1.text: Aha! Of course you didn't! You are going to slaughter Clemens' men and let me go.

Next2.text: Why, you ask? Because you need me to escape, of course! I'm taking Corene with me, along with any evidence linking you to me. No one will ever know of your actions here.

Next3.text: And if that doesn't convince you to bend the rules, I am offering you a reward and giving you access to Alazar. So, what do you say?

Accept1.text: You are not as stupid as you look. I am proud of you.

Start.text: I agreed to see you as this meeting could be mutually beneficial for us. You see, I need to hire Mercenaries for a very delicate mission.

Next.text: I want you to capture a woman who represents a threat for the future of Alazar and Gosenberg.

Next2.text: Needless to say, her identity is on a need-to-know basis only. You shall bring her back alive, take your reward and never speak of this mission again. Are you interested?

AcceptMission.text: Good, I am pleased. This woman usually travels in a small caravan between the Winfel Estate and Marheim.

Wait.text: Remember, I want her alive.

MissionDesc.text: Ambush the caravan and capture the woman.

End1.text: Well, well! What have we got here?

Give1.text: Hiring you was the right decision, after all! This woman was a source of endless trouble, but thanks to you, she is now my captive.

Give2.text: Please accept this reward and the gratitude of the honourable Adr Alazar family.

SettingLog.text: You helped Brunhilde Adr Alazar capture a woman named Corene.

Narrator.text: A grim smile dances on Brunhilde Adr Alazar's face.

line0.text: Take on Brunhilde Adr Alazar's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Do you want to add flowers to the bride's crown?

End.text: You have already given flowers.

Start.text: Do you want to add your donation to the bride's banquet?

End.text: You have given your donation.

Start.text: I can't wait for this wedding. It is customary to give slaves and servants a day's leave on such occasions.

Next.text: Shame this family only has two children.

End.text: My Lady doesn't want me to clear these tables, but every time she looks at them, she starts crying again.

Start.text: Are you here to congratulate my daughter? She's marrying into a good family, isn't she?

Next.text: We welcome all donations to her flower crown and the banquet. It'll bring you luck, you know!

line0.title: The Wedding Banquet
line0.props.helpTip: Provide flowers and food to help prepare the wedding.

Start.text: Do not touch these tables! They are all I have left of my daughter!
Our wealth was built on this vineyard. My son is now studying at Gosenberg University, and my daughter is marrying a man of high social standing.

Next.text: But the disease affecting our crop is a great concern. Could it be a bad omen? Should I postpone the wedding?

Start.text:
Oh! Corene! My dearest child!
Where have they taken you?
This is a groattle trap. The pig used as bait looks somewhat appalled.
Shhh! You'll scare the groattle!

Next1.text: This beast, it's half-goat, half-pig and half-rabbit. And it's got golden guts!! If we capture one and gut it, we'll be loaded!

Next2.text: No more working as stable boys! Rich as Brokers we'll be!

Next3.text: Why d'you tell 'em? Now they're gonna to steal our trap!

Next4.text: By the Beast's fangs, you're right! We gotta kill 'em!

line0.props.tipText: Explain that groattles only exist in minstrels' tales.

Convinced1.text: Well... if that's true, does it mean we bought a pig and wasted a whole day here for nothin'?

Convinced2.text: The boss ain't gonna be happy!

Convinced3.text: We can't tell her none of it. Take this, and promise you'll keep your traps shut.

line0.title: Groattle Hunting
line0.props.helpTip: Bring the stable boys to their senses by any means necessary.

Start.text: Sorry! No, please! You win, we shouldn't have attacked you.

End1.text: You take the groattle trap and all our stuff, but please don't kill us!

Start.text: The door is sealed shut by some sort of mechanism.
If you have any Antiquities, you should show them to me. None of my competitors can match my prices.
I was experimenting with Alazarian Powder.

Next1.text: I had to run away to avoid paying the Broker Council for the consequences of my research.

Start.text:
Oh! Here come our new members! It's a pleasure to meet you in person!
Welcome to the <narrator>Fellowship of Knowledge</narrator>!

Next1.text:
We are a group of Scholars and like-minded individuals who dedicate our lives to researching Ancient Artefacts.
We are united by our common quest for Knowledge.

Next2.text: As I like to do for all new members, I have a welcome gift for you! Yours is this amazing <narrator>Ancient Pendulum</narrator> and its <narrator>instructions</narrator>. We haven't quite managed to unlock its secrets yet, but I am certain you will be able to!

Next3.text:
Your reaction is perfectly natural: who wouldn't be amazed by Ancient technology?
Well then, don't let me keep you! It's time for you to take your first steps on the path of archaeology, find out what your gift can do, decipher its instructions...

Next4.text:
So many exciting adventures, don't you think?
That's another facet of the Fellowship of Knowledge!

Tresor1Wait1.text:
So? Have you discovered the Pendulum's purpose? Oh! Praised be Saint Jeru and the God of Light! You are amazing, Mercenaries!
As soon as we find another page of the journal, you can be sure we will give it to you!

line0.props.disableReason: Your Troop must reach Tier 9 of the <narrator>Mysteries and Wisdom</narrator> Path.

Tresor2Next1.text:
Well? Have you discovered the Pendulum's purpose? Oh! Praised be Saint Jeru and the God of Light! You are amazing, Mercenaries!
As soon as we find another page of the journal, you can be sure we will give it to you!

Tresor2Next2.text: What really matters to the Fellowship is Knowledge. Material things are superfluous. Here! It just so happens that we found a second page of the instruction manual. I bet you can't wait to decipher it.

Tresor2Next3.text: Be brave, Mercenaries! The path of Knowledge may be fraught with hardships, but it will take you farther than any other!

Tresor2Wait1.text: You discovered another secret location? By the All-seeing Eye, I must find more pages of this instruction manual!

line0.props.disableReason: Your Troop must reach Tier 10 of the <narrator>Mysteries and Wisdom</narrator> Path.

Tresor3Next2.text: Why not complete your artefact collection? We've just found a third <narrator>Instruction Page</narrator> that was placed in the middle of a completely unrelated codex.

Tresor3Next3.text: I can't wait for you to find this new Artefact! I've already started writing a treatise about the first two!

Tresor3Wait1.text: You found the Artefact in Arthes? I can't say I'm surprised. Saint Eleor Abbey was built on the ruins of a city that the Ancients called Lahearta.

line0.props.disableReason: Your Troop must reach Tier 11 of the <narrator>Mysteries and Wisdom</narrator> Path.

Tresor4Next1.text: You found the Artefact in Arthes? I can't say I'm surprised. Saint Eleor Abbey was built on the ruins of a city that the Ancients called Lahearta.

Tresor4Next2.text: By the way, while studying the archives of this very same abbey, we found a page that looks a lot like the ones you already have...

Tresor4Next3.text:
Marvellous!
I have a feeling the relic you'll find will be even more fascinating than the others!

Tresor4Wait1.text: I'm still eagerly awaiting news of your adventures. It's like reading a multi-part story...

line0.props.disableReason: Your Troop must reach Tier 12 of the <narrator>Mysteries and Wisdom</narrator> Path.

Tresor5Next1.text: I'm still eagerly awaiting news of your adventures. It's like reading a multi-part story...

Tresor5Next2.text:
Ahem!
I've got a new <narrator>Instruction Page</narrator> for you. I'm afraid it's the last one...

Tresor5Next3.text: Meaning this will be our final collaboration. I hope you'll find an Artefact as astonishing as the others.

Final1.text: I came across a caravan of merchants who told me that you found another Artefact. Is it true?

Final2.text: The Fellowship of Knowledge will never forget what your Troop contributed to our understanding of the mysterious Ancient civilisation. You are now among its most distinguished members.

line0.text: Accept Professor Hermann's gifts.

line1.text: Find the treasure of the Ancients using Chronicler Erius' Journal - I and the Pendulum.

line0.text: Accept Professor Hermann's gifts.

line1.text: Find the treasure of the Ancients using Chronicler Erius' Journal - II and the Pendulum.

line0.text: Accept Professor Hermann's gifts.

line1.text: Find the treasure of the Ancients using Chronicler Erius' Journal - III and the Pendulum.

line0.text: Accept Professor Hermann's gifts.

line1.text: Find the treasure of the Ancients using Chronicler Erius' Journal - IV and the Pendulum.

line0.text: Accept Professor Hermann's gifts.

line1.text: Find the treasure of the Ancients using Chronicler Erius' Journal - V and the Pendulum.

Start.text:
I've been studying the smooth tablet for years.
Unfortunately, I think only a special quill can reveal it.
We came all the way here! We won't be intimidated!

Living in Gosenberg is a privilege! Thanks to the Brokers, everyone affected by the Plague is offered treatment. All they have to do in return is to isolate in an abbey for a short while. Needless to say, that is a small price to pay!

Scapegoat.text: They... They're not going to kill us, are they?

ChoiceInProgress.text: Saint Lenaid, defender of craftsmen and labourers, protect us from the Vintners and guide the Mercenaries in their choices!

EndConvinced.text: We thought our end had come! Thank you for saving us, Mercenaries. We will make offerings to the All-seeing Eye in your honour as soon as we are back on our feet.

Start.text: You're not going to stop us from killing the Plague-ridden, are you?

line0.props.tipText: Convince the Vintners that the Plague-ridden have done nothing wrong.

line1.props.tipText: Drive the farmers away from the abbey.

Convince.text: I guess it would have been difficult for them to poison our fields without leaving the abbey... Besides, other regions should have been affected, too. You're making a good point here.

Convince2.text: Very well, we'll let them be. Half of your due will go the abbot, as an apology. I hope it'll be enough to stop him from reporting us to the Inquisition.

SettingLogConvinced.text: You convinced the vintners to spare the lives of the Plague-ridden.

Execute.text: One less thing to worry about! I was worried you might be swayed by the abbot, but you are sensible people!

Execute2.text: Here is your payment, you've earned it. As for us, we will try and buy healthy vines in other provinces. Here's hoping the Inquisition will not hear of what happened in the abbey.

SettingLogKilled.text: You helped the Vintners get their revenge.

MissionDesc.text: Talk to the Saint Lenaid Abbot.

Start.text: I will not let them lay a finger on these poor souls! Whatever is killing their crop is a botanical disease, not a medical one!

line0.props.tipText: Kill the priest and let the Vintners slay the Plague-ridden.

End.text: I was worried you were going to side with the Vintners. Thank you for sparing the sick.

End2.text: I do not know what they promised you, but here is what I hope is a fair compensation.

SettingLogConvinced.text: You convinced the vintners to spare the lives of the Plague-ridden.

SettingLogFight.text: You protected the Plague-ridden from the Vintners.

Purifiers.text: The Purifiers have already been paid. We're just waiting for them to come and free our sick from the Plague.

Start.text: Do not fear these poor souls. They were infected by the Plague but they are well-fed: they are no more dangerous than you or I.
Out of the way, Abbot. We demand justice.

Priest1.text: You slaughtered our defenders, forced your way into an abbey and now you threaten to kill innocent people. How dare you speak of Justice ?

Farmer1.text: We... we have no choice! The Plague-ridden spread their disease and wreaked havoc on our lands. It is our duty, our right, to punish them!

Priest2.text: How could these people, who have been confined in this abbey for weeks, spread the Plague to your fields? You have no evidence to substantiate this claim.

Farmer2.text: Of course we do! Gosenberg is the only kingdom where the Plague-ridden are looked after for so long. It is hardly a coincidence if we are the only ones who lost our crop!

Priest3.text: This is absurd! Only Vertruse is affected. The vines from other provinces are perfectly healthy! The disease affecting your vineyards has nothing to do with the Plague.

Farmer3.text: There is only one way to be sure: kill all the Plague-ridden and see if it rids us of the disease. Only then will we truly know!

Priest4.text: For the Eye's sake! Mercenaries, stop them from killing these poor souls! Can't you see that the men you are escorting have lost their minds!

MissionDesc.text: Decide in favour of the Plague-ridden or the Vintners.

line0.title: The Scapegoats
line0.props.helpTip: Take a side in the argument.

Start.text: Don't worry, the Black Market is known for its discretion and respect for its customers' anonymity.
Hey! You! Are you the ones who killed these Bandits?

Next1.text: Blessed be the All-seeing Eye! Thank you! They slipped through the Guard's net so many times, I thought they'd never get caught.

Next2.text: Sorry to be a bother, but would you mind untying me?

End1.text:
Ah! Thanks a lot. I couldn't feel my ankles.
Try as I might, these shackles were too strong.

End2.text: Ironically, I was stuck here because of a key! When the Bandits saw it, they figured that I was rich even though I have no idea what it actually opens.

End3.text: It's a family heirloom that we keep as a mere lucky charm. If you want it, you are welcome to it. It has completely failed its purpose.

Accept.text: I'll go back to my fishery now. It's not far from Smot's Arena. If you ever happen to go there, come and pay me a visit.

line0.title: The Unlucky Charm
line0.props.helpTip: Pick open the chains restraining the fisherman.

Start.text: Someone dug a hole in the jail floor. It is too dark to see where it leads.

End.text: Someone dug a hole in the jail floor. It is too dark to see where it leads.

Start.text: You can hire me if you want, but I won't rat on my friends.
Go on, laugh all you want!

Next.text: You don't know what it's like not to be re-elected! I was going to lose everything because of those blasted sewers! I had to prepare for my life after politics!

Start.text: I just don't understand! We had six prisoners yesterday, and today, there's only one left!

Next1.text: The lock is intact, and the remaining scoundrel refuses to explain anything. We couldn't get him to talk, and believe me, we tortured him properly!

End1.text: You found them? By Saint Lenaid's hammer! You made short work of that!

End2.text: Take this reward. You deserve it. If you were merciful enough to take some of them alive, you can speak to my colleague and claim their bounties.

Alt1.text: What the... Where have the prisoners gone? The lock is intact!

line0.text: Find out how the prisoners escaped.

line1.text: Find the Sawmill described by the fugitive.

line2.text: Report to the warden.

Start.text: We reward anyone who brings in <inf>outlaws</inf>. As you can see, we've got room to spare.

Deliver.text: Looks like this scoundrel deserves his place here.

NoSlotAvailable.text: You've done so well, the Jail is now full!

line0.title: Left Behind
line0.props.helpTip: Tend to the fugitive and interrogate her.

Start.text: I broke my leg while trying to escape the jail, and my accomplices left me behind. The gutless oafs!

Next1.text: I'll tell you everything I know if you give me some medicine!

line0.props.tipText: Heal the woman.

line1.props.tipText: Convince the woman to talk.

Next2.text: We'd been digging together for weeks. They said we were going to form a gang and set up our lair in an abandoned sawmill near the Tiltren border.

Next3.text: But when they saw my broken leg, they abandoned me without a second thought. Dispatch them or take them back to jail and let them rot there! I'd be most grateful.

line0.props.tipText: Let her join the Troop.

line1.props.tipText: Try to capture the fugitive.

line0.text: Find out who the sawmill workers really are.

line1.text: Decide what to do with the sawmill workers.

Start.text: Move along, Mercenaries. Our sawmill has no need of your services.

Next1.text: Hello, Mercenaries... Oh... You know who we are.

Next2.text: So that whiner ratted us out, eh? We should've slashed her throat when we had a chance.

Next3.text: But surely we can come to an agreement? After all, we are all sensible people.

Next4.text: How about we pay you off nicely, and you let us leave the province unnoticed? The Guard will be rid of us, it'll free up more room in the local jail, you'll be rich and we'll be on our way. It's a win for everyone involved, really.

line0.props.tipText: Capture as many fugitives as possible.

Wait.text: We'll gather our belongings and go.

Start.text: Ah! Are you Mercenaries? Good... Very good.
Yes, these machines aren't working. But that's none of your business!
You should focus on the disease affecting the vines instead, Mercenaries.
The door is blocked by some sort of mechanism.
There is something written on the bowl.

Read.text: The inscription reads: Skilled negotiators or wealthy travellers, welcome!

Done.text:
You hear a faint click as soon as the bowl is filled with your Krowns.
Before the Companions can react, the gold coins are swallowed by the Ancient shrine.

Start.text:
I'm trying to get in, but I can't open this blasted door.
I guess you’re supposed to make an offering, but what could an Ancient want?

End.text:
You did it!
The treasure is mine!

Start.text: There is something under the mud. You will have to clear it away.
Suddenly, your torches light up a monstrous face.
The room below is flooded and none of the Companions can swim.

It’s a statue of Nepti.
He’s holding a gem in his right hand, but his left hand is empty.

line0.props.tipText: Place a ruby in the statue’s left hand.

line1.props.tipText: Place a sapphire in the statue’s left hand.

line2.props.tipText: Place sandstone in the statue’s left hand.

EndRuby1.text:
This is Nepti's statue.
Do you want to retrieve the gems?

EndSapphir1.text:
This is Nepti's statue.
Do you want to retrieve the gems?

End.text: This is Nepti's statue.

Start.text: You can hear water behind the wall.
The staircase is flooded.

Something is following you.
The Companions speed up, but it’s too late: the creatures are upon you.
Among rusted items, you find Krowns that look strangely familiar.
The merchant must have been swept away by the current.
The hallway collapsed, but you can feel a slight draft.
The staircase is flooded.
Something is blocking the door from the other side.
The door is sealed shut by some sort of mechanism.
The atmosphere in the halls is strained. The Companions can sense eyes watching them.
It's easy enough for Broker Ald Marheim to say we should be patient. He's not the one who's about to lose it all!

Farmer2.text: I won't stand idly by while my crops wither away! Those responsible must be punished!

Farmer3.text: By the All-seeing Eye, we will fight back! Grab your pitchforks! To the abbey! We'll knock the doors down!

Farmer4.text: First off, we need to deal with the Brotherhood. These blasted Mercenaries guard the abbey day and night.

Farmer1.text: We could hire our own goons to dispatch them. If we all pitch in, we'll have enough to employ the best!

Mission.text: Did you hear everything we said? Good, at least you know what you're getting yourselves into. Fighting the Brotherhood is not for the faint-hearted.

FarmerEnd.text: So far, nothing has changed... We are working with what we have now.

Accept.text: Great. We shouldn't dally. Let's go.

MissionDesc.text: Help the Vintners enter Saint Lenaid's Abbey.

line0.text: Take on Jehan Molen's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: The nest obstructs waste water drainage.
The creatures are protecting their nest.
Of course we reported the attack! That's the first thing I did after chasing this ruffian away!

Next1.text: The Guard searched the area all day with no luck. They suggested we hire some Mercenaries. This is preposterous! Where does our tax money go if not in our protection?

Start.text: I saved my mistress by pure reflex. But frankly, when I thought about it later, I regretted it.

Next.text: Risking my life with two months to go before I can be a free woman again? How stupid of me!

Start.text: It may not be obvious at first glance, but I was a scholar before becoming a slave. One piece of advice: however rich or intelligent you are, never gamble on arena fights.
You're Mercenaries, right? I need your help and I'm willing to pay. Just name your price!

Next1.text: My vineyard's the only healthy one left in the whole province. So I have to guard it at night in case some jealous so-and-so tries to get to my crop.

Next2.text: But I was attacked! I was knocked unconscious, and if my daughter and slaves hadn't chased the rascal away, I'd probably be dead!

Next3.text: I can deal with thieves, but murderers?! That's a task for professionals like you. Do you think you could guard my vineyard at night?

Accept.text: Perfect! You must be in the fields by nightfall and guard the place until dawn.

Wait.text: Any news on my attackers? You enlisted the help of the Trackers?

End1.text: So this tuber has special properties...?

End2.text: Wait! You mean this repulsive root is responsible for our ordeal?

End3.text: The men in my field... I saw them trying to plant the blasted thing! They were knowingly poisoning my vines! This is extremely serious! Broker Ald Marheim must be notified at once.

End4.text: Here is your reward. Take it and enjoy it while I go to the castle. Stay alert, the Broker could send for you at any time.

SettingLog.text: You discovered that plants from Alazar are smothering the Vertrusian vineyards.

MissionDesc.text: Protect the vineyards from 8pm until 7am.

line0.text: Take on Rosel Loop's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line0.title: Empty casks
line0.props.helpTip: Bring 30 Gosenberg Wines or find the caravan near the Grinmeer border.

line1.title: Rouste
line1.props.helpTip: Win a Rouste match in Vertruse.

Start.text: Gosenbergers undeniably have a drinking problem.

Next1.text: But what can I say? It's good for business.

Start.text: Not one drop of alcohol! The tournament is doomed!
It's over! We're calling off the whole thing. Go home!

Next1.text: We're out of wine! The casks are empty, there's nothing left!

Next2.text: Grinmeer vintners were supposed to send us a caravan, but it never arrived! We don't even know if it crossed the <narrator>border</narrator>.

Start.text: Without booze, Rouste has no flavour.
I came from the other end of the province to play!

Next1.text: And what do I find? Empty casks!

Start.text: The vineyard disease destroyed the entire crop this year.

Next1.text: And now, Gosenberg City doesn't even bother fulfilling our orders!

Start.text:
You...
This is...

Next1.text:
Wine! Wine's here, lads!
Let the Rouste begin!

Next2.text: Join us, Mercenaries! You'll see, our players are completely different after a drink or two!

Rouste1.text: Our players may be vintners, but they turn into warriors the minute they set foot on the pitch. Are you ready to face them?

Rouste2.text:
I think we just witnessed the greatest Rouste match in Vertrusian history!
This trophy is yours!

Rouste3.text: If you want a rematch, know that our vintners haven't shown you the full extent of their talent yet! After a few more drinks, you'll be facing wild beasts!

RousteDiff1.text: Our lads want a rematch and this time, they almost finished the wine you brought. There will be blood!

line0.props.tipText: Play Vertruse's team in Hard mode.

RousteDiff2.text:
What's your secret, Mercenaries? This match was even more amazing than the last!
Here's your reward. You've earned it!

RousteDiff3.text: You won all of the rewards we had to offer, but feel free to come back and play! If only to enjoy the atmosphere.

RousteEnd1.text: Would you like to play a friendly match? No stakes, just for the love of the game!

line0.props.tipText: Play Vertruse's team in Hard mode.

RousteEnd2.text: We never tire of watching you play, Mercenaries.

Start.text: Not to be finicky, but I've had better wine.
Just because you saved the day doesn't mean I'll let you win on the pitch.
Ah! We can finally play in proper conditions!

Without you, I'd have had to close up shop.
Is there something you'd like? A cup, perhaps?
The stable boy pretends he doesn't know you.
I'll never believe a minstrel's tales again. Not after the earful we got from the boss!
I entertain my hosts with tales and fables in exchange for a hot meal.

Next.text: I recently told the story of the Groattle, a beast that hides in the mountains and plays nasty tricks on farmers.

Next2.text: The stable boys in particular seemed to enjoy it.

Start.text: You haven't seen two stable boys on your way here, by any chance? They've been gone for a while, and I am starting to worry.

Next1.text: They are decent lads, but not the sharpest tools in the box. I am concerned they took the minstrel's story a bit too seriously.

Next2.text: And I did warn them of the dangers of Brownrock Mine.

End.text: I am so glad to have my stable boys back. Thank you for bringing these gullible fools back in one piece.

End2.text: The stable boys are strangely quiet in your presence.

line0.text: Investigate the missing stable boys near Brownrock Mine.

line1.text: Make sure the stable boys are back.

Start.text: Do you need a new mount or have one that needs tending to?
We work for a pittance all day and sometimes all night, in stuffy galleries that could collapse at any moment.

Next1.text: We won't go back to work until the boss agrees to our conditions! We want more Krowns, enhanced safety measures and a day off for the festival of Light.

Next2.text: If you negotiate for us, we will pay you handsomely.

line0.props.tipText: Convince the strikers to resume work.

End1.text: That miser is threatening to buy slaves? If there's any chance to change his mind, we must try. For our families.

End2.text: Tell him to calm down, we'll get back to work.

Reward.text: He agreed, you say?

Reward2.text:
It's a miracle! We've been trying to convince him for weeks!
Brokers beware, these Mercenaries are master negotiators! Take this reward, with our heartfelt thanks.

Wait.text: Please do come by again, we may have bonuses to negotiate.

Stop.text: Hey! Oi! You blacklegs! Do you mind?

line0.title: Workers Union
line0.props.helpTip: Put an end to the strike to resume mining operations.

Start.text: I knew I should have bought slaves!

Next1.text: Look at them! Striking! How will I feed my family if all work at the mine has stopped? Help me! You simply must!

line0.props.tipText: Scare the boss into agreeing to the strikers' demands.

End1.text: These wretches are threatening to bury me alive in my own mine? The louts! They are insane!

End2.text: I should have known. The strike itself was an act of wanton savagery. Thank the Eye you warned me. I probably owe you my life.

Reward.text: You obviously know how to handle such situations! Here is your reward: Krowns that won't end up in these slackers' pockets!

Wait.text: We're back in business!

Wanted.text: You threatened the owner of the mine.

Start.text: We are drapers. If you wish to buy fabric, I can assure you ours is of the finest quality!
Why? Why me? Why today, when I thought my wealth made! Why must Fate punish me so?

Next1.text: Five years I spent on this tapestry! This masterpiece was supposed to make me famous throughout Gosenberg. A lifetime's work gone overnight!

Next2.text: The Guard told me to stop looking. They said my tapestry was long gone across the border, likely never to be seen again. I am left with nothing!

End.text: But... that's my tapestry! ... Words cannot express how grateful I am! I hope this reward speaks for itself.

End2.text: I am still struggling to catch my breath after what I've experienced.

Start.text: I wasn't ready for my first encounter with the Ghost Pack. Not only did I nearly die, but I also became a burden for my colleagues.
You can join the Hunt if you wish, but be warned.

Next1.text: We're not tracking regular game, this the Ghost Pack. These creatures only appear in the dead of night. They spring out of the mist and bring terror and misery to all who cross their path.

Next2.text: This indicates where the freshest traces of the Pack are: you will have to go up the whole trail to fight it.

Accept.text: In that case, I wish you good luck. You'll need it.

Wait.text: Make sure you are well prepared for this fight, or you won't make it.

End.text: To be honest, I didn't think you'd make it back alive. But obviously, I misjudged you. Not only did you survive but you also defeated the Ghost Pack. This armour layer is yours.

End2.text: To be quite honest, I didn't think I would see you alive again. I misjudged you: not only did you save your own skin, but you also triumphed over the Ghost Pack.

line0.title: Hunt down the Pack of Vertruse

line0.text: Agree to join the Hunt.

line1.text: Follow instructions from the Vertruse Hunt item to find and defeat the Ghost Pack.

line2.text: Report your victory to Master Tracker Istos.

Start.text: No one is safe from the Ghost Pack, not even in the most sheltered and peaceful regions like Vertruse.
