Ah, well, not to worry. We'll find a solution!
I'll head to Redane. Master Tracker Versinn will know what to do.
Rest up and enjoy your rewards. You'll need all your strength for what lies ahead.

MissionDesc1.text: Find a Huntsman who's willing to share their knowledge with you.

SettingLog.text: You have found where the Beast's lair is located.

line0.text: Take on Master Tracker Videss's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

line2.text: Find at least ::vars.amountCount:: traces of the Beast before reporting back (::vars.amount::/::vars.amountCount::).

line3.text: Report to Master Tracker Videss.

Start.text:
Knowing Master Tracker Versinn, he'll want to climb the mountain.
Get ready, this won't be a pleasure hike.

The icy winds that blow on Urach will make the climb pure hell.
Not to mention that we'll have to get a whole army of Trackers to climb who are more used to swamps than high places!

I'm sorry that your help was in vain.
Climbing that Eye-forsaken mountain is impossible!

Next1.text:
Ah! Damn it! The Beast will escape and devastate the Five Kingdoms!
What can we possibly do?

Start.text:
Might as well head straight back to Ludern and prepare for the Beast's arrival!
There's no way I'm going to die climbing a mountain!
Part of the bag's contents has become mouldy.
There's some sort of notebook next to the skeleton.

Read1.text: Day 34 of the Hunt We found Llyr at the edge of the forest! Alive! For someone who faced the Beast in single combat, he was in fairly good shape! Credne ordered us to make camp and open the bottles of mead in his honour.

Read2.text: Day 36 of the Hunt Many of us think that Llyr's mind has been shattered by terror, but Credne refuses to believe us. He claims that Llyr's behaviour is merely due to his sadness at losing his companions, and that it will pass before long.

Read3.text: Day 39 of the Hunt Llyr has completely stopped talking. This morning, I noticed he had a strange gleam in his eye and that his hair had turned white. I don't think this is just from either sadness or terror. There's something else.

Start.text: The Beast is asleep! Now's your chance to attack!

line0.text: Help Tracker Issa to escape.

Start.text: So wait, I'm not allowed to take part in the Hunt, but you are? Outsiders?

Next1.text:
Treason! Treason!
Curse them all! May the Tules drown them! May the gods reject them! May the Beast devour them alive!

Next2.text:
I must get out of here! Open this cage, Mercenaries!
I've got to make them pay! This affront can only be avenged with blood!
Take my fangs and let me out!

Start.text:
They'll be sorry they ever locked me up! I won't give them a moment's peace!
They'll see I was ready for combat!
The lake feeds directly into the basin.

line1.props.tipText: Fill a flask with water from the lake.

Alt.text: The water in the basin looks different somehow.

line0.props.disableReason: No animals influenced by the Beast.

line0.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text:
Curses! Those bastards can really fight.
Not sure we could have taken them alone.

Next1.text:
Good thing you came along to straighten things out!
Business can get back to normal!

Next2.text: The Trackers believe that the water in this lake has been blessed by their gods. They claim it cleanses their animals of the Beast's influence. Needless to say, they all rush here during the Hunt.

Next3.text:
We figured it would be a waste not to take advantage of it. Especially since the Ghost Pack doesn't come around these parts.
Minimum risk, maximum profit.

Wait.text: As long as the Trackers pay, they can drink all the water they want.

SettingLog.text: You allowed a group of Bandits to sell access to the Mirror of the Ancients.

Start.text: What's the big idea? You think just because you helped us, you can drink our water for free?

Next1.text:
The best I can do is a friendly discount.
After all, your animals' lives are at stake here! Surely they're worth a few krowns!

Start.text:
There's something weird sparkling down there in the water.
Did you see it too?

What's all this nonsense about krowns?
Why doesn't anyone chase those bandits away?
<narrator>The Beast's influence is starting to show.</narrator>

What have you done?
Why is the lake different?

Next1.text:
We've got a business to run! If this water isn't magic any more, it's worth nothing!
Give us back what you took! Right now!

MissionDesc1.text: Eliminate the witnesses to your misdeeds.

MissionDesc2.text: Talk to Huntsman Mervice.

Start.text:
They stood between the Trackers and their sacred mission!
These bandits deserve a punishment worse than death! Curse them! May their bodies rot unburied!

Next1.text: You, the outsiders who restored justice! You deserve to be rewarded!

Next2.text: In the name of the Gods in the depths of their tombs! In the name of the Tules who rule over nature! Accept this gift from the hands of druid Abraxa!

Accept1.text: Thanks to you, the Blessing of the Ancients will ward off the Beast's influence. Yes! The Trackers will give their loyal companions lake water to drink, and it will save them from the monster!

Accept2.text: The Beast will die, again and again! The clans will accomplish their mission!

SettingLog.text: You let the Trackers retake possession of the Mirror of the Ancients.

Start.text:
The Ancients have given us their blessing.
It is an immense honour and a great responsibility.
I swore that I'd be worthy of it.

Bellarde managed to drink the lake water in time, but it was all very last minute.
I was this close to paying those bandits.
A she-wolf in top form.

What have you done?
Why has the lake stopped shining?

Next1.text:
You've broken the Ancients' blessing! You've doomed us all!
You filthy traitors!

MissionDesc1.text: Eliminate the witnesses to your misdeeds.

MissionDesc2.text: Talk to Huntsman Mervice.

Start.text:
All those people dead...
Was it you who killed them?

Next1.text:
Oh! By the gods! Murdering a druid...
I'll be banned from Harag!

Next2.text:
We have no other choice! This has just got to work!
These horrors can't have been committed in vain!
Let's hurry and get this over with!

Bandits1.text: Well, I suppose it was the will of the gods. Daring to steal from the brave souls fighting the Beast... they deserved a harsh punishment! You've done well.

Bandits2.text:
Let's hurry back to the Tomb of the Ancient One.
The Trackers will need the blessing. I don't want to keep it to ourselves any longer than necessary.

MissionDesc1.text: Place the blessing on the door of the Tomb.

Start.text: A seal is needed to open this door.
You've interrupted some creature's meal…
According to the inscription, this man is called Urashu.
The Companions notice two red eyes in the shadows.
There's something under the bookshelf.

line0.props.tipText: Select a Miner.

line1.props.tipText: Select 2 Companions strong enough to move the bookshelf.

Start.text: A seal is needed to open this door.
Something is moving in the darkness.

The door is stuck.
A sufficiently nimble Companion might be able to slip through the gap and open it from the other side.

line0.props.tipText: Select a nimble Companion.

Start.text: The remains of a very old machine.
The Companions recognise the outlines of an ancient workshop. Half of a Copper Seal has been abandoned here.

line0.props.tipText: Reassemble the two halves of the seal.

Start.text: The stone is covered with intricate inscriptions. You'll need a Scholar's help to decipher them.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Scholar from among the Companions.

End.text: The Companions have deciphered the recipe for the Iron Seal. They should be able to craft it now.

Start.text: A seal is needed to open this door.
The door is locked.
Someone used this anvil to break a steel seal.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Blacksmith to repair the seal.

Start.text: The door to the Tomb is completely closed.

Next1.text: The door to the Tomb is completely closed.

Start.text: You came? Oh! By the Eye!

Next0.text: May the Tules forgive me for what I'm about to tell you!

Next1.text: I know how to reach the top of the mountain and the Beast's lair... By passing through the Tomb of the Ancient One! It's the only way to defeat the Beast without running the risk of losing all of our men on the climb.

Next2.text:
You've got to help me! No Tracker will agree to set foot in these ruins. It's taboo for our people!
I beg of you, this scourge affects all of the kingdoms... and... and you can keep the reward from the Hunt all to yourselves!

Accept1.text: I thought for sure you'd refuse.

Accept2.text:
First let's open the Tomb.
If our legends are true, we'll have to commit the first of our blasphemies.
Follow me, and let's pray together for the gods to have pity on us.

NextLudern1.text:
I'm no better than those Alazarian looters!
May the Tules forgive me for what I'm about to tell you!

MissionDesc1.text: Help Huntsman Mervice.

MissionDesc2.text: Find Huntsman Mervice.

End1.text:
Here we are. All that's left is to place the blessing in its receptacle.
Here's hoping I interpreted the druids' chants correctly...

OpenDoor1.text:
I was right! The doors are open! We've done it!
The Ancient One will lead you straight to the Beast's lair!

OpenDoor2.text: Once you're face to face with the sleeping monster, show it no mercy! Hit as hard as you can! The first strike must be powerful enough to bring down its defences! You won't get a second chance!

OpenDoor3.text: One last piece of advice, Mercenaries. Our legends say that this tomb is truly immense. As tall as the mountain itself! Some druids even claim that the tomb was built before the mountain. So... prepare yourselves. And be careful.

MissionDesc3.text: Make your way through the Ruin to find the Beast's lair.

line0.text: Take on Huntsman Mervice's mission.

line1.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: By the Tules!

What do you want?
Can't you see I'm praying?
This man is still breathing, but his life is hanging by a thread.
Why did you heal me? Why didn't you let me die? My clan has been wiped out! I don't deserve the title of Master Tracker!

Next1.text: Look around you! It's all my fault! My clan was counting on me, and... when the Herald showed up to join the fight, I lost it! I panicked!

Next2.text:
Here, take this. It was supposed to be for our return trip...
I can't bear to show my face to their families.

Start.text: This Tracker was crushed by an immense paw.
This woman was thrown by something with titanic strength. Her skull split when she hit a rock.
Huge teeth have ground up this Tracker's legs.
This woman's face is frozen in fear.
Did you see those blokes curled up on the stretchers? That's all I've got left to fight the Heralds of the Beast! The others were devoured!

Next1.text:
Damn it! We can't kill the Beast as long as its damned lackeys are alive! It'll summon them as soon as we start to get the upper hand!
The Hunt will fail because of us! The whole clan will be dishonoured!

Next2.text:
You've got to help me, Mercenaries!
Rid us of those Heralds! The fate of the Five Kingdoms depends on it!

Accept1.text: Take the scouts' reports. They'll tell you where the Heralds were last seen. Then just wait for nightfall and follow the trail.

Accept2.text: Stay alert! These creatures aren't just ordinary monsters from the Ghost Pack. These are Heralds. They're much stronger and smarter!

Wait.text: Take this mission seriously. My whole clan is counting on you.

End1.text: Back already? Please tell me you got at least one!

End2.text: All three? You defeated all three Heralds that quickly? That's incredible, Mercenaries! How on earth did you manage? You're... This is a feat worthy of the best Trackers of Harag!

End3.text:
I hope this reward will be sufficient.
Not only has my honour and that of my clan been saved, but now we finally have a chance of bringing this Hunt to a successful finish. The Beast won't be able to call on its lackeys for help!

EndWait.text: I'll be there to help take on the Beast! You can count on me!

SettingLog.text: You have killed all three Heralds of the Beast.

line0.text: Take on Master Tracker Tiercos's mission.

line1.text: Use the scouts' reports to track down and kill the Heralds of the Beast (::vars.amount::/3).

Start.text: The incompetence of Tiercos and his clan is putting us all in danger.

Next1.text: The Beast will call on its Heralds if it finds itself in any trouble. Fighting all four of those monsters at once is a guaranteed death sentence!

End1.text: Do you know why those monsters are called the Heralds of the Beast?

End2.text: They appear before the Beast is reborn. Those creatures are how we know that Harag has to prepare for the Hunt.

Start.text: I... I'm fine...
The Tracker is struggling to breathe.
Something is wrong. The Tracker isn't moving.
Mercenaries! Is that you?

Next1.text:
Then you know what to do!
The ambush was successful, all that's left is to finish off that monster!

Alt11.text: Tules take me, this monster just won't die!

Alt12.text:
It's already nearly escaped from our ambush!
Hurry, Mercenaries! Help us finish it off!
My Trackers are exhausted!

Alt21.text: This time the Beast was easy to find! You haven't missed anything!

Alt22.text: Are you ready to fight? It's time for the grand finale!

Ludern1.text:
The rebirth happened much too fast!
What did Alazar do?

Ludern2.text: My men are still exhausted from the last Hunt! We won't last long without your help!

Start.text:
This obviously isn't your first Hunt!
Your movements are much more confident than last time.
Take your part of the reward, you've earned it.

Next1.text: May the Tules see to it that our paths cross again someday.

Alt11.text:
You have answered our call once again. I am honoured by your loyalty.
Here is your part of the reward. For risking your lives alongside us once again.

Alt21.text: I knew you'd come! The men couldn't stop talking about you during the Hunt.

Alt22.text: You're part of our team. This reward is nothing compared to the high esteem Harag has for you.

Ludern1.text:
Damn! That could have been a lot worse.
How did Alazar manage to summon the Beast? Can they do it again?

Ludern2.text: I need to go to Canopus to make my report. If the Northerners can control the Beast's rebirths, we're all doomed.

Start.text: Don't come any closer! I can do it! Velba will return to her senses! Whatever you do, don't distract her!

Next1.text:
Calm down! Please!
The Mirror of the Ancients isn't far now! We're almost there, you can do it!

line1.props.tipText: The Beast's influence is too strong. The bear will never make it to the Mirror of the Ancients in time.

Start.text:
Noooo!
What have you done?!

Thank you! Thank you! Whoever you are!
Velba has been my partner for as long as I can remember. I don't know what I'd do if I lost her.

Next1.text:
Here! This is our share.
I'm sure the clan will be relieved to have us both back.

Start.text:
You're monsters! Why didn't you listen?
Why didn't you give us a chance?
Versinn and the clans thought we were mad, but we were right all along! The mercenaries who joined the Hunt... that was you!

Next2.text: Do they know what you did in Ludern? Desecrating the Tomb of the gods? Murdering Master Tracker Brighid? Summoning the Beast?

Next3.text: Oh! You can count on us to tell them all about it! Including how we avenged Ludern by killing you!

line1.props.tipText: Pretend you're someone else.

Convinced1.text: Why do you outsiders all love robbing corpses so much? We were just about ready to kill you!

Convinced2.text:
We should arrest you for looting!
If it were anyone other than these scum, you'd be rotting in the Ludern Jail by now!

Convinced3.text: There's no way I'm giving you the whole bounty. You've already helped yourselves more than enough.

Start.text:
Well, Mercenaries? Heading out to hunt some monsters?
You're letting out your wild side, is that it?

Next2.text: Ah! Your Troop is exactly as you were described. A ramshackle gang who betrayed Alazar and turned their back on Knowledge to protect the superstitions of some barbarian horde.

Next3.text:
The King of Alazar is very unhappy with the loss of his greatest scholars. And as for me, I'm very unhappy I've had to come all the way here from Drombach to find you.
I'll make you pay for that.

line1.props.tipText: Pretend you're someone else.

Convinced1.text:
Other mercenaries?
You mean you're wearing the armour of those scoundrels who killed Hadwige and Winfrith?

Convinced2.text: Ugh! This habit you mercenaries have of looting your victims' bodies is positively disgusting.

Convinced3.text:
Well, if the traitors are dead, there's no reason I should keep wading around through this kingdom's muck.
Go back to your scavenging, I suppose.

Start.text: They're all dead! Every last one! The Ghost Pack has killed off my clan!

Next1.text: They locked me in this cage to protect me! They knew I wasn't ready yet... They wanted me to survive! They saved me!

Next2.text: I'll never doubt my companions' word again! I'll trust in them! I'll be Harag's most reliable Tracker! I'll keep my clan's memory alive!

line2.props.tipText: Offer something to honour Limbre's clan.

Recruit.text:
Count on me, Mercenaries!
I'll follow you wherever you go!

Empathize1.text:
That's a nice offering. I think they would have liked it.
Count on me to conduct the most beautiful ceremony for them.
Take this, for what you've done for me.

Start.text: It was an honour to meet you, Mercenaries. I'll never forget your trust in me.

Next1.text:
Going on this mission with you was the most terrifying thing I've ever done – and the most heroic.
I hope you'll forgive me for making you break so many taboos.

Next2.text: Farewell, my friends. I'll pray for our paths to cross again one day.

Start.text: The Beast...

Next1.text:
The Beast is dead! The Five Kingdoms are saved!
May the gods bear witness to our courage: we have fulfilled our sacred mission!

Next2.text: No words can fully express my admiration and gratitude, Mercenaries.

Next3.text: Huntsman Mervice told me how you decided to climb the mountain barehanded rather than putting our Huntsmen' lives at risk.

Next4.text: Not to mention the mortal blow you dealt to the Beast, up there in its lair. Try as it might to escape, it was so weak that our reinforcements had no trouble stopping it. That final battle only added to your legend.

Next5.text: The reward is all yours, Mercenaries. Accept it on behalf of the people of Harag. Your valour is an example to us all.

Accept1.text: May the gods grant us many years of peace before the Beast is next reborn.

Start.text: This way, Mercenaries! Over here!
Unbelievable! You're alive!

Next1.text: When I saw the Beast crashing down the mountain with no one behind it, I thought for sure you'd sacrificed yourselves, or something along those lines...

Next2.text:
But here you are! Still alive, while the creature is in its death throes!
I don't know what you did up there, but it was a huge success!

Next3.text: Come on, then! Finish what you started! The Hunt ends today!

Start.text: We have no choice: to defeat the Beast, we must climb Urach.

Next1.text: I've asked the few mountain climbers that the Trackers have in their ranks to go ahead as scouts. I hope they'll find a route that the others can manage without too much trouble.

Start.text: Have you been here before? If so, you must have noticed that there's something shining at the bottom of the lake. The druids say it's the mark of the Ancients' blessing. Well, I think that is what will open the door to the Tomb.

Next0.text: Of course, if we take it, there's a risk that the lake water won't heal the animals any more...

Next1.text: We'd only be borrowing it! I swear on my honour that as soon as we don't need it any more, I'll put everything back where it was!

Next2.text: Go on, Mercenaries! Just think of all the lives we'll be saving!

Accept.text: Once we're inside... the occupants of the Mirror of the Ancients may not approve of our methods. Try to act natural. Blend in with the crowd, all right?

MissionDesc1.text: Grab whatever's shining at the bottom of the lake.

Start.text:
You're joining the Hunt?
Best of luck, Mercenaries.
It warms my heart to see the other Kingdoms finally giving a damn about this mission!

Next1.text:
Oh! You want to know how to track the Beast?
It's a complicated art, it'll use up a lot of my valuable time...

Convinced1.text:
By the Tules, you're right! The time I spend teaching you the basics of the Hunt will be time saved in our search for the lair!
Now, listen carefully!

Bribe1.text:
That's very generous of you. I never imagined I'd be paid for my art!
Let me explain how I go about it...

Trapper.text:
...and then once you've found the print, your Huntsman will have to examine it very carefully. Take your time with it! Even the tiniest detail might reveal where the lair is located!
Give it a try with this one. I'll be right here beside you!

Wait.text: Don't be shy, Mercenaries. I know you can examine this trace properly!

End1.text:
Fine work, Mercenaries! Many Master Trackers wouldn't have done as well!
I guess I must be a good teacher! Ha ha!

End2.text: Keep it up, you're on the right track! Gather as much information as you can, and it will lead you to the Beast's lair. Once you know its location, come back to the Monstrous Carcass to make your report.

MissionDesc1.text: Give ::vars.amount1:: Fangs or ::vars.amount2:: to Huntsman Mervice to benefit from his knowledge.

MissionDesc2.text: Examine the trace left by the Beast.

Start.text: Come on over, folks! Four crowns per person! A real bargain!

Next1.text: You're making a profit off the blessing of the Ancients! It's despicable! It's a sacrilege!

Next2.text:
A sacrilege?! Let's not get carried away!
We're just earning a living!

Next3.text: Besides, you and your boors should be grateful we even let you into our hideout. I don't know many other gangs as accommodating as ours.

Next4.text:
Don't talk down to us, you great souse!
This isn't your lair! The Mirror of the Ancients belongs to the people of Harag!

Next4Bis.text: Kill them, Mercenaries! Kill them! The Trackers won't pay to fight the Beast!

Next5.text: Yeah, they'll defend us! These Mercenaries are civilised people! They can see that you're all just barbarians, and that we're honest folk willing to pay for their services!

Start.text: Damn it! They're surrounded! We've got to get them out of there!

Next1.text:
My clan will create a diversion!
Take care of the scouts and run for it! Don't stop!

Start.text:
We... we survived! Oh, thank you!
Without you and Sevella...

Next1.text:
Wait!
Where's Sevella?

Start.text:
Curses...
That's her, all right. That's Sevella.

End2.text:
May the Tules curse me! She gave her life for us.
I'll never be able to look her parents in the eye again.

End3.text:
I'd better take what's left of her body back to the village of Redane... and report to Master Tracker Versinn.
Come with us, Mercenaries. I'm sure he'll want to hear your version.

NotifEndFirstEncounter.text: You've managed to escape the Beast.

MissionDescEndFirstEncounter.text: Find Tracker Sevella in the area.

MissionDescIntro2.text: Give your report on the fight to Master Tracker Versinn.

MissionDescSpawnKill.text: Talk to Master Tracker Tiercos to get your reward.

MissionDescTrackEnd.text: Report back to Master Tracker Videss.

MissionDescLakeBandits.text: Talk to the Bandit Chief to get your reward.

MissionDescLakeTracker.text: Talk to the Harag Trackers to get your reward.

MissionDescBeastFight1.text: Catch up to the Beast and defeat it.

Start.text: You dug up a chest.
This Brotherhood Mercenary must have been one of the outsiders who came to try their luck in the Hunt.
The dismembered body of a Tracker.
The corpse gives off an unbearable smell, as though the Tracker had died of some gruesome disease.
The Beast crushed this wolf with all of its weight. It's now little more than a smear on the ground. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information from it.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: Among the animal remains, ::vars.name:: discovered a tuft of fur belonging to the Beast. It's covered with some sort of black dust.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

Start.text: There's not much left of this animal, which appears to have been chewed up in a gigantic maw and spat out again. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information from it.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: While inspecting the wolf, ::vars.name:: discovered petals from a snow iris, a flower that only grows at high altitude.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: Enormous tracks sunk deep into the ground. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: ::vars.name:: has made a surprising discovery in one of the tracks: a pair of mole-rat incisors. The Beast may have been unwittingly carrying them around.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: These tracks are less widely spaced than usual. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: These shorter strides indicate that the Beast was moving more slowly than usual. Perhaps it was tired when it headed eastward?

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: Another crushed animal. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information from it.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: Upon closer inspection, ::vars.name:: found a small fragment of painted stone in the wolf's fur. It may have fallen from the Beast as it trampled the animal.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: Trees knocked down and heavy prints in the ground. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: Among the branches, ::vars.name:: found one of the Beast's many arms. Though torn off, it still holds a piece of rock in its claws.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: The Beast damaged this Ancient structure. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: The damage is considerable, even for the Beast. The only possible explanation is that it fell onto the aqueduct.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: Nothing remains of this Trackers' Camp, utterly ravaged by the Beast and its Pack. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: Among the collapsed tents, ::vars.name:: catches sight of a sticky mass – the remains of a very old spider web. It must have got caught in the Beast's fur, then fallen off during its rampage.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: The trees have been blown flat, smashed to the ground by some incredible force. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information here.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: Upon lifting a fallen trunk, ::vars.name:: discovered petals from flowers that don't grow at this altitude. This snow iris is far from its mountain home.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: The bear is still warm: the Beast must have feasted on it recently. A Huntsman may be able to glean more information from it.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Trapper.text: It's not the bear carcass that most interests ::vars.name::, but the direction of the tracks, which point toward the top of the mountain.

SettingLog.text: A trace has provided some information on the Beast's lair.

StoryDone.text: This trace left by the Beast is quite old. It will not lead the Companions anywhere, but could tell you more about the creature.

line0.props.tipText: Choose a Huntsman from among the Companions.

Start.text: An offering to the Tules certainly wouldn't go amiss when facing the Beast.
The Tules are described as curious spirits who accept all kinds of offerings.
A fair portion of the offerings have already been nibbled at.
You found the previous lighthouse keepers.
Be sure to stock up well – you never know what might happen in Brigga...

People are talking about you in... less respectable circles, you know? You've got a certain reputation with our kind... Want to see “the lair”? But if you want to get in, you've got to be known to the authorities, if you catch my drift...

GoOk.text: We criminals need to stick together. Put these bags over your heads and follow me – I'll take you to the lair.

GoNo.text: Sorry, lads, but you're too squeaky clean to get in. We're all in the same boat here, right? So if you haven't got a bounty on you, you've no need for us.

RewardQuest.text: You've finished one of the jobs? We won't bother going all the way over there – here's your reward.

Start.text: I'm not familiar with your faces. What clan are you from?

Ludern.text:
How did Alazar manage to get the Beast out of Brigga?
Do they have the power to control it?

Start.text: Don't worry, I'm a veteran of the Hunt. This is actually the third one I've been on.

Heal.text: With a bit of luck, you might make it through unscathed!

Start.text: Oh my, what an honour! I'm being forced to go along with the Trackers! Just wait until I find out who volunteered me... I'll make them wish they were never born!

Repair.text: I've done what I can. Your armour should hold together a little while longer.

Start.text:
The bridge guard let you pass?
You must really be good at your jobs, Mercenaries!
I just so happen to have some information for people like you...

Done.text: Excellent choice. I can't wait to see where that leads you.

line0.props.tipText: The temporary village of Redane awoke to a violent dispute.

line1.props.tipText: A gang of Bandits has apparently taken refuge in one of Brigga's most sacred places.

line2.props.tipText: The lair remains elusive, but the Huntsmen show no signs of giving up the search.

line3.props.tipText: The heralds of the Beast are still on the prowl in Brigga. Master Tracker Tiercos must have failed in his mission.

Sevella.text: The temporary village of Redane awoke to a violent dispute.

Lake.text: A gang of Bandits has apparently taken refuge in one of Brigga's most sacred places.

Carcass.text: The lair remains elusive, but the Huntsmen are redoubling their efforts to find it.

Spawn.text: The heralds of the Beast are still on the prowl in Brigga. Master Tracker Tiercos must have failed in his mission.

DeliverMission1.text:
And here I thought I'd been forgotten in the wilds of Brigga! I'm so glad to see that we're still in the race.
Thank you very much, Mercenaries!

End.text: You know as much as I do about Brigga.

Start.text:
I've got an army of Trackers to feed, so I'd better warn you, this is no time to be picky.
We're not in Gosenberg here.

MissionDesc1.text: Follow Sevella to the Beast.

line0.text: Listen to the interaction between the Trackers.

line1.text: Talk to Tracker Sevella to learn more.

line2.text: Take on Tracker Sevella's mission.

line3.text: Follow mission instructions to complete this objective.

Start.text: Sevella has already been buried. A few of her Companions have placed offerings on her grave.

line0.props.tipText: Pay tribute to the Tracker.

Start.text:
Evros told me what happened.
She and her men fought hard for their lives.

Next1.text:
I don't blame you for anything. Sevella was as stubborn as a crocswine. She would have sacrificed her life with or without your help.
At least your support allowed her to achieve her goal. So her promise has to be honoured.

Next2.text:
You survived, and your spirit doesn't seem to have been broken by terror. I'd be happy to have warriors like you in my ranks.
This Hunt is turning out to be tougher than the previous ones.

Next3.text: Stopping the Beast from spreading destruction is the most sacred mission that the Ancients have entrusted to the people of Harag. Each time that behemoth emerges from the bowels of Brigga, the clans come together to defeat it. Time and again.

Next4.text: Facing this monster head-on is certain to fail, though. Our only chance is to take it by surprise, when it's vulnerable and separated from its ghostly lackeys.

Next5.text: Harag's various clans have already divided up the task. Help them, and you'll be rewarded.

Wait1.text: Finding the Beast's lair is the only way to take it by surprise.

Ludern.text: The Beast has been seen in Ludern. This rebirth is different to the others. I hope there's still time to find its lair.

Moutain.text:
How do we get to the lair?
I'm thinking, Mercenaries. I'm thinking.

SettingLog.text: You helped the scouts to avoid their grim fate.

Start.text:
Don't worry.
Master Tracker Versinn will find a solution to our problem.
That's why the clans chose him.
<narrator>The animal's name suits it well.</narrator>

Scabby won't let me near him. He hates me!
He knows it's my fault Sevella died.

Next1.text: But I've got to get him to the Mirror of the Ancients! Without that lake water, he'll turn into a monster like the other animals!

Next2.text:
Versinn has only given me a couple of days to heal him of the Beast's influence. After that, I'll have to put him down myself...
He's asking me to kill Sevella's boar!

line0.props.tipText: Recruit Scabby the boar.

Accept1.text: Are you sure? Then hurry up and heal him! Take him to the Mirror of the Ancients or find a cure before he changes.

Wait.text: Take good care of Scabby. He's all I have left of Sevella.

Start.text:
Sevella should have let us die!
She was killed because of us.
Scabby has every reason to hate me.

BoarDead.text:
Sevella should have let us die!
She was killed because of us.
I couldn't even save her boar!

End.text:
Versinn led the others to the foot of the mountain.
I haven't the strength to go with them.

Start.text: I can't mark the face of a non-initiate. Only those who have completed the ritual of Tules' Glade are worthy of such an honour.

Tatoo1.text:
War paint is a gift from the Tules to the people of Harag.
No Tracker would confront the Beast without the forest spirits' protection.

Tatoo2.text: Does another one of the Companions want war paint?

Start.text: We can't just let our scouts die like that! We've got to send in some men!

Next1.text: Send in some men? I won't sacrifice lives to save others!

Next2.text: Our best Huntsmen are with them! How do you expect to find the Beast's lair without their help?

Next3.text:
How will we deal with the lair if we have no one to send there?
Focus, Sevella! Your men know the risks!

Next4.text: By the Tules! You can't let them be eaten like that!

End1.text:
Attacking the Beast head on is bound to fail. These scouts are already dead.
My duty is to protect the living.

Start.text: I don't give a damn what Versinn thinks! I won't sit around and let my brothers be slaughtered!

Next1.text:
Come with me, Mercenaries! We can still save them!
My clan will give you whatever you want in exchange!

Next2.text: There's no time to lose! Follow me!

Start.text: Letting your companions die is sometimes the wisest path.

Ludern.text:
If the Beast was really seen in Ludern, then Master Tracker Versinn is right to be concerned.
The Beast isn't supposed to leave Brigga that quickly.

Start.text: Of all the Master Trackers who join in hunting the Beast, the clans chose Versinn to guide us.

Next1.text: We must be willing to put our lives in his hands.

Start.text:
After each rebirth, the Beast stays in Brigga for a while to gather its strength.
We can't miss this opportunity!

Ludern1.text:
They say that Alazarian scholars were able to draw the Beast to Ludern.
What would have happened if it hadn't returned to Brigga?

Ludern2.text:
Foreigners don't understand what a scourge it represents!
They don't know what we go through every cycle to protect them!

CrimePath1Started.text: You've received a letter bearing the Baron's seal: a client requests your presence at the Gosenberg border crossing.

CrimePath1MissionDesc1.text: Go to the Gosenberg border crossing to meet with your client.

CrimePath1MissionDesc2.text: Attack the Guard and make sure Septelle is never forgotten again.

CrimePath1NotifLieutenant.text: The lieutenant lets you know that he's ready to negotiate and is in a field west of Stromkapp.

CrimePath1MissionDesc3.text: Take Septelle to meet with Lieutenant Perault.

CrimePath1MissionDesc4.text: Take Septelle back to the Gosenberg border crossing.

TradePath1Started.text: You've received a letter bearing the seal of a Gosenberg family: a client requests your presence at the Stromkapp Tavern.

TradePath1MissionDesc1.text: Go to the Stromkapp Tavern to meet with a mysterious client.

TradePath1MissionDesc2.text: Negotiate the terms of a trade partnership between a Tiltren merchant and Aldeberth.

TradePath1MissionDesc3.text: Negotiate the terms of a trade partnership between a Marheim merchant and Aldeberth.

TradePath1MissionDesc4.text: Meet with Aldeberth in the Tiltren Tavern.

TradePath1MissionDesc5.text: Go back to speak with the Tiltren merchant.

TradePath1MissionDesc6.text: Go back to speak with the Marheim merchant.

MightPath1Started.text: You've received a letter bearing the Brotherhood's seal: a client requests your presence at the Mother Bear Tavern.

MightPath1MissionDesc1.text: Go to the Marheim Tavern to meet with the Brotherhood.

MightPath1MissionDesc2.text: Defeat the groups of Bandits so that you can easily assault the lair.

MightPath1MissionDesc3.text: While you were busy, the Harag's Bane gang defeated a group of Bandits.

MightPath1MissionDesc4.text: Join the Harag's Bane gang outside the Bandits' Lair.

MightPath1MissionDesc5.text: Go to the Marheim Tavern to collect your reward from the Brotherhood.

MightPath3MissionDesc1.text: Go to the Armoury on the first floor of the Brotherhood Fortress.

MightPath3MissionDesc2.text: Go to the Brotherhood's Rouste Pitch to play a game.

MightPath4MissionDesc1.text: Go to the Armoury on the first floor of the Brotherhood Fortress.

KnowledgePath1Started.text: You've received a letter bearing the Universities' seal: a client requests your presence at the Edoranian border crossing.

KnowledgePath1MissionDesc1.text: Go to the border crossing to meet with your client.

KnowledgePath1MissionDesc2.text: Find the artefact hidden in Saint Eleor Abbey.

KnowledgePath1End.text: You won't learn anything new here. You must inform your client of what happened.

TradePathBuilding.text: You can now access the special building of the Trade and Craftsmanship Path in Arthes.

KnowledgePathBuilding.text: You can now access the special building of the Mysteries and Wisdom Path in Vertruse.

KnowledgePathMission.text: Visit <narrator>the Fellowship of Knowledge</narrator> in Vertruse.

CrimePathBuilding.text: You can now access the special building of the Crime and Chaos Path in Tiltren.

MightPathBuilding.text: You can now access the special building of the Power and Glory Path in Grinmeer.

DragonBonesMission.text: Take the dragon bones to Professor Maurith.

MissionDescMightPathArena1.text: Go to the Arena of Legends and win a fight.

MissionDescMightPathArena2.text: Go to the Arena of Legends and defeat the Fourth League.

MissionDescMightPathArena3.text: Go to the Arena of Legends and defeat the Third League.

MissionDescMightPathArena4.text: Go to the Arena of Legends and defeat the Second League.

MissionDescMightPathArena5.text: Go to the Arena of Legends and defeat the First League.

MissionDescKnowledgePath1.text: Meet the members of the Fellowship of Knowledge.

MissionDescKnowledgeEnd.text: Return to Professor Hermann at the <narrator>Fellowship of Knowledge</narrator>.

MissionDescTradePath1.text: Talk to a Pedlars' Guild spokesperson.

MissionDescCrimePath1.text: Talk to the Tiltren Informant at the Stromkapp Tavern.

MissionDescCrimePath2.text: Talk to the Arthes Informant at the Cortia Tavern.

MissionDescCrimePath3.text: Talk to the Vertruse Informant at the Marheim Tavern.

MissionDescCrimePath4.text: Talk to the Ludern Informant at the Garussa Tavern.

MissionDescCrimePath5.text: Talk to the Drombach Informant at the New-Asthel Tavern.

MissionDescCrimeEnd.text: Return to the Drombach Informant in New-Asthel.

MissionDescBeastRespawn.text: Face the Beast once again alongside the Trackers of Harag.

MissionDescTavern3.text: Purchase the ruined Tavern in Gosenberg City.

MissionDescEdoran2.text: Go to Ormance County to find out more.

MissionDescBeast.text: Enter the wild lands of Brigga to learn more.

MissionDescFiefdom.text: Inspect the ruins of the Mount Altis fortress to learn more.

MissionDescAlazar2.text: Head to the County of Rigel to find out more.

MissionDescEdoran3.text: Go to the port of Arthes to learn more.

MissionDescEdoran3Bis.text: Go to the Ormance Border Crossing to learn more.

MissionDescSkill15Sword.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new sword specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Axe.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new axe specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Mace.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new mace specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Polearm.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new polearm specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Bow.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new bow specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Dagger.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new dagger specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Crossbow.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new crossbow specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Fist.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new katar specialisation.

MissionDescSkill15Censor.text: Meet with the Master-at-Arms to unlock a new Censer specialisation

QuestAudience_10.text: Some residents of the Fief have disappeared! Find them and punish their captors.

QuestAudience_24.text: A Ghost Pack is haunting Mount Altis and threatening your residents.

QuestAudience_25.text: It's only a question of time before the Mount Altis Rat Infestation spreads the Plague to your Fief.

QuestAudience_26.text: Send your Mercenaries to inspect the place where a caravan disappeared and recover its cargo.

QuestAudience_44.text: Some Smugglers are shamelessly enriching themselves on your backs. They need to be taught a lesson.

Locate_A1CryptAdmiral.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_S1CryptBuilder.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_E1CryptExplorer.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_G1CryptFighters.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_G2CryptMaker.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_G2CryptMerchant.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_H1CryptCitizen.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_H1CryptGeneral.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Locate_IR1CryptArtist.text: Explore the Sepulchre revealed by the Fief's Scholars.

Start.text: What? You want to leave?

Out.text: All right, let's go – and don't forget the bags.

Start.text: Looking for contracts a bit more exciting than the ones in the taverns? I've got something for you... if you don't mind getting your hands dirty.
Want to see my wares? I can buy everything you've got, or sell you anything you need... Just don't ask where anything came from, and I'll do you the same courtesy.
Nothing more invigorating than a bit of alcohol when they're after you, eh?
So you've caught their attention, eh? I can help you... In exchange for a small fee, of course...

Next1.text: Excellent choice... I'll spread the word. The folks up above will have forgotten about you soon...

Start.text: How dare you attack the Brothers?

Next1.text: Wait! What? Was it the Brotherhood who put a price on our heads?

Start.text: Do not oppose the will of the All-Seeing Eye!

Next1.text: Tis the Eye's command that heresy be purged by fire!

Start.text: Defending the weak and the fatherless is easy on a full belly!

Next1.text: But when you go hungry, chivalry and fealty go out the window!

Start.text: Out of our way, peasants! You cannot begin to understand the noble intentions we pursue!

Next1.text: Colonel Deteore's legacy is rotting away in the Ludern swamps! We must wrest her belongings from the mud and the hands of these savages!

Start.text: The Guard was already after me long before you were born!

Next1.text: If you think you can do better than your predecessors, you're as foolish as they are.

Start.text: I will not back down! Animals must be treated with respect!

Next1.text: Minstrels are treating them like dirt! They beat them if they don't comply, deprive them of food, all for the plebs’ entertainment!

Next2.text: Our cause is worthy, you will not stop me!

Start.text: I can't stand these yokels and their constant moaning. You have burned down the Tavern!, Bartes is a drunk!, He gives the Brotherhood a bad name...

Next1.text: They'll rebuild that hovel in no time!

Next2.text: I don't get what they're complaining about!

Start.text:
Oh! Mercenaries?
Has the good king of Alazar finally forked out the Krowns?

Next1.text: Had he given us the raise we deserve, I wouldn't have spat in his face!

Next2.text: Believe me, whatever the old miser promised you for our heads is nowhere near enough!

Start.text: You're too late to save the children: they've gone up North with the slave traders.

Next1.text: Don't look so disappointed, Mercenaries. Most parents would be dismayed to see their offspring return so quickly...

Next2.text: In these times of famine, I barely have to negotiate to buy their young ones. These peasants are all very keen to sell off a few mouths they won't have to feed.

Start.text: Run, heretics! Fear the divine wrath of the All-Seeing Eye and Saint Jeru!

Next1.text: These lands must be cleansed of ungodly souls! Blood will wash away their sins.

Next2.text: Death to the heretic Trackers! Let the Light sweep away their pagan idols and bestial gods!

Start.text: Why confront us? We are only doing what the Guard dares not do!

Next1.text: Trials, prison... It's all pointless! Look at what has become of this Province! Look! Honest folk can't live here in peace!

Next2.text: It's high time someone rid us of the bandits, the raiders, the thieves... Pure and simple extermination... These parasites deserve nothing less!

Start.text: Go away, Mercenaries. This is no concern of yours. The Legion alone will deal with this matter.

Next1.text: What? The Broker Council wants to drive us out? They have no right! The Legion can go wherever it pleases in Gosenberg! This land is theirs only because we allow it.

Next2.text: Go on, then! Fight me! And they better not come crying when Alexa Grathan tries to take over their kingdom, too!

Start.text:
Slave traders? You must be joking, Mercenaries!
We are but humble traders looking to satisfy our clients.

Next1.text: There aren't enough convicted criminals in chains to meet the demand. If the laws weren't so strict, people like us could stay nice and warm in our homes.

Next2.text: This is no mean feat! These Harag savages can sure put up a fight, the risks are great and the journey perilous. Now, if you don't mind, we'll take our catch and leave...

Start.text: It's true what they say, isn't it? The Legion never gives up...

Next1.text: We've been in hiding for over five years but they've still managed to track us down.

Next2.text: Ha! No matter. We're tired of running from these bloodhounds! If this is our last stand, then so be it! We won't go down without a fight!

Start.text: I'd recognise your stench anywhere. People like you reek of greed and indifference.

Next1.text: For the right price, you'll turn a blind eye to what your employers are selling.

Next2.text: Who cares about slaves as long as you bring in the Krowns!

Next3.text: You're no better than them. I will enjoy killing you.

Start.text: I warn you, Mercenaries! Call me a sore loser and I'll have your head!

Next1.text: Victory was ours! We were this close to winning the Rouste Tournament! But those blasted craftsmen cheated! They should consider themselves lucky we didn't kill them all before we left.

Next2.text: These Krowns are ours. If they want them back, they'll have to pry them from our cold, dead fingers!

Start.text: Looking for a little tipple? I should warn you, this Gosenberg wine is for connoisseurs. Only the most discerning palates will truly appreciate it.

Next1.text: What do you mean, “vinegar”? Since when are Mercenaries wine specialists?

Next2.text: The Gosenberg Vintners' claims are baseless! Who says they didn't get their barrels from us anyway? Huh?

Start.text: If you're here to recover what we took from the Guard, you're too late.

Next1.text: We've paid for safe passage into Gosenberg, and the Brotherhood has agreed to let us join them. The Ludern Guard will have no further trouble from us.

Next2.text: You understand, don't you? Who'd want to stay here when our neighbours live on fertile lands with more Krowns than they know what to do with?

Start.text: Don't come any closer! Back off! No one will disturb the Ancients' sleep!

Next1.text: Whoever you are, you will not enter and defile our gods!

Next2.text: Not you, nor anybody! From this day forth, we will protect the Tombs with our lives!

Start.text: On the way to the Throne Room, I couldn't help noticing that some of your residents were cooking up the soles of their shoes for food. I'm afraid they might turn to worse things yet, if you don't act to ease their hunger.

line0.props.tipText: Open the Militia's grain stores to feed the population.

line1.props.tipText: Let residents use their creativity to deal with the food shortage.

Start.text: Pardon my impudence, my Lords, but... the grain stores are empty! We've nothing left to eat! Your citizens are growing angry!

line0.props.tipText: Send the malcontents to the dungeons to discourage the revolt.

line1.props.tipText: Buy food supplies from neighbouring kingdoms.

Start.text: What a waste, my Lords, to leave so much food to spoil in your granaries!

Next1.text: Selling some of it would be a fine way to feed our customers' hungry mouths and fill your residents' pockets. What say you? Shall I order your subjects to sell their surplus right away?

line0.props.tipText: Part of the food surplus will be sold to the highest bidders.

line1.props.tipText: The surplus should be given to the orphans and paupers in the Fief.

line2.props.tipText: The surplus will stay right where it is. A poor harvest could hit us at any time.

Start.text:
What ever will we do, my Lords? The hail has destroyed everything!
Our trees are battered, our fields are ruined... There's nothing left! Nothing!

line0.props.tipText: Buy food from another kingdom.

line1.props.tipText: Open the Militia's and Scholars' grain stores.

line2.props.tipText: The residents will have to tighten their belts until the next harvest.

Start.text: It's no wonder your Fief has been invaded by mice: your granaries are overflowing with food! Your farms are turning out food faster than your residents can eat it!

Next1.text: If we don't find an answer to this storage problem soon, we'll never be able to get rid of the rodents!

line0.props.tipText: Order the Craftsmen to make enough crates and clay pots to protect the food from mice.

line1.props.tipText: Acquire a few cats to protect the Fief's granaries.

line2.props.tipText: Losing part of your production is acceptable.

Start.text: There aren't enough men to watch over your domain, my Lords. Why, just yesterday we saw a shadowy figure prowling around near the food reserves. They fled when we approached, but they could easily come back.

line0.props.tipText: Force some peasants to join the Militia.

line1.props.tipText: The Militia already have more than enough people.

Start.text:
This place is a real cesspool! Yes! It's the only word for it, my Lords!
What else can you call a city where thieves help themselves from the market stalls in broad daylight? Or rob our customers right up to the Throne Room door?
You must protect our goods, or the Merchants will leave to trade elsewhere!

line0.props.tipText: Recruit new Mercenaries to strengthen the Militia.

line1.props.tipText: Let the Merchants and traders fend for themselves.

line2.props.tipText: Throw the alderman out of the Throne Room.

Start.text: Thieves are getting far too comfortable in your city. Let's hang a few of them in the market square. That should get the others' attention.

line0.props.tipText: Approve this excellent idea.

line1.props.tipText: Death is excessive, but the punishment should serve as a deterrent.

line2.props.tipText: Refuse to use such barbaric punishments.

Start.text: The fountains have been poisoned, and many people have fallen ill. You can't claim to rule a Fief without ensuring its people the safety they deserve.

line0.props.tipText: Send the Scholars out to track down the poisoner.

line1.props.tipText: Give the Militia more resources to watch over the fountains.

line2.props.tipText: The commoners can just get their water from the lake.

Start.text: The Bandits who kidnapped your residents have also damaged the door to our sentry box. They nailed up a ransom note.

line0.props.tipText: Send Mercenaries out on the Bandits' trail.

line1.props.tipText: Your Troop will personally find the missing persons.

line2.props.tipText: Pay the ransom.

Start.text: No realm has ever been as safe as yours, my Lords! No one dares step out of line, and all the residents bow down to our Militia!

line0.props.tipText: Congratulate the Militia on their good work.

line1.props.tipText: Order the Militia to be less rigid with the residents.

Start.text: There are children among your subjects, some with promising minds. Let us not waste their potential by leaving them to chase chickens all day! Entrust them to me and I shall educate them, to raise them into enlightened adults.

line0.props.tipText: Entrust the children's education to the Scholars.

line1.props.tipText: The peasants don't need to know how to read to cultivate their fields.

Start.text: I pulled the drowned child's body out of the water. Ever since, I see his little face every time I close my eyes...

line0.props.tipText: Ask the fisherman to teach the residents to swim.

line1.props.tipText: Accidents will happen no matter what we do.

Start.text: Your residents are as dumb as a pile of rocks! They spend good money on Edoranian swill and think they can cure their baldness with potions from back-alley charlatans! Their ignorance will make those crooks the new masters of this Fief!

line0.props.tipText: Order the Scholars to educate the populace.

line1.props.tipText: Order the Militia to inspect the goods.

line2.props.tipText: The residents are free to do their own product research.

Start.text:
Your Scholars have made quite a reputation for themselves! Even in Alazar, we've heard all about their wisdom.
Our University would be honoured to host some of your finest academics.

line0.props.tipText: Send a scholarly delegation to Alazar.

line1.props.tipText: The Fief needs its Scholars.

Start.text: Children running amok in the streets may seem cute, but for how long? Idleness will soon turn them into drunkards and thieves! Send your subjects' children to the Militia! We'll turn them into strong, proud soldiers!

line0.props.tipText: Hand the children over to the Militia.

line1.props.tipText: Children should enjoy their innocence while they can.

Start.text: I had three tables broken last night alone! And last week, those good-for-nothings set fire to my stools. This can't go on like this – you've got to keep your people occupied!

line0.props.tipText: Organise a Rouste tournament.

line1.props.tipText: Hire Jugglers to entertain the people.

Start.text: Among the Jugglers who perform in your Fief, my men have located one company whose material seems quite seditious. Under the guise of entertaining the people, they're mocking you and your rule. Should I intervene?

line0.props.tipText: Lock up the agitators.

line1.props.tipText: Let the artists say whatever they like.

Start.text: My Lords, the show put on by the new Jugglers' Troop has been a real revelation. Some of your residents think you should share some of your power with the rest of us. After all, we know our professions and businesses best. We could offer some good advice!

line0.props.tipText: Agree to rule the Fief with your people.

line1.props.tipText: Imprison these peons who think they have the right to govern.

Start.text: Do business? With what money, by Saint Jeru? Your residents are poorer than most other places' beggars! The Merchants will leave your domain before long if they don't find customers to sell their wares to!

line0.props.tipText: Promise to improve the Fief's financial situation.

line1.props.tipText: Well, then! Let them leave!

Start.text: The Bandits are up to something, my Lords. Some say they're going to attack to try and take this place back! We must prepare ourselves!

line0.props.tipText: Upgrade the Militia's weaponry.

line1.props.tipText: The realm is already prepared.

Start.text: The stench in our streets is unbearable! Residents don't even bother walking down to the lake to dump their filth! We must do something before your people suffocate one summer!

line0.props.tipText: Prepare to take action against the noxious air.

line1.props.tipText: Build sewers.

line2.props.tipText: All cities stink in summer!

Start.text:
The Festival of Light is coming, my Lords! The Festival of Light!
We must prepare for it right away, or the Eye's Reckoning will wipe this godless Fief from the face of the earth.

line0.props.tipText: Prepare the Festival of Light.

line1.props.tipText: Organising religious festivals is the Church's job.

Start.text: The Ghost Pack that prowls your lands is more powerful than anticipated. Three of our men have already died. The lords of foreign kingdoms are still refusing to give us any help, but it seems you're different.

line0.props.tipText: Agree to send Mercenaries.

line1.props.tipText: Your Troop is quite willing to wipe out this pack themselves.

line2.props.tipText: Refuse to send your people to fight Ghost Pack monsters.

Start.text: I... I ran as fast as I could when I saw it! A Rat Infestation! There's a nest right next to the Fief! The Plague will infest the city!

line0.props.tipText: Agree to send Mercenaries.

line1.props.tipText: Your Troop will personally handle this Rat Infestation.

line2.props.tipText: Simply prohibit the Fief's residents from going anywhere near the nest.

Start.text: For the time being, we have enough meat to prevent those sick with the Plague from losing their minds, but how long can we keep this up? We need remedies!

line0.props.tipText: Our Apothecaries must contain the epidemic.

line1.props.tipText: Send a request for help to the kingdom of Alazar.

line2.props.tipText: The sick will have to be put down to stop the disease from spreading.

Start.text: You know me, my Lords... I never come to you without a very good reason.

Next1.text: For example, I've never dared to bother you for a missing caravan! And yet, Saint Jeru knows they do vanish!

Next2.text: Ahem... Anyway, this caravan is somewhat different. It was coming back to our Fief, loaded with Krowns. A lot of Krowns. So I deemed it wise to inform you of this terrible loss for our domain.

line0.props.tipText: Agree to send Mercenaries.

line1.props.tipText: Your Troop will personally find the caravan.

line2.props.tipText: It's still just one more disappearance.

Start.text: Someone needs to watch over the eateries in your city! The “food” they're selling should be fit for consumption! I'm tired of finding sand in my meat and nail trimmings in my wine.

line0.props.tipText: Assign the Militia to watch over the eateries.

line1.props.tipText: Assign the Scholars to inspect the eateries.

line2.props.tipText: Residents should just be more careful about which taverns they go to.

Start.text:
You're all that people are talking about in Edoran.
I'd love to be your advisor. May I?

line0.props.tipText: Recruit this unknown noble.

line1.props.tipText: Send this maniac back where he came from.

Start.text:
May I talk to you about the noble you agreed to take on as an advisor?
Has he shown any talent since he started working for you?

Next1.text:
The few times I've seen him involved in the Fief's affairs, he was flirting with some peasant girl or getting drunk at the Tavern!
My Lords, it's my duty as alderman to warn you: I fear he's taking advantage of your kindness!

line0.props.tipText: Relieve the noble of his duties as advisor.

line1.props.tipText: Keep the noble in his role.

Start.text: ::vars.amount:: [Fief_Currency_Money] are missing from the Fief's coffers! And guess who disappeared without a trace three days ago? Your advisor! That petty noble who turned up out of nowhere!

line0.props.tipText: Curse your gullibility.

Start.text: I have come to inform you of my departure, my Lords. The prestigious position you offered me has helped me secure the most advantageous marriage proposal. I will be returning to Edoran with full pockets!

Next1.text: It's only fair that I should share part of the dowry with you.

line0.props.tipText: Bid this strange advisor farewell.

Start.text: A few of us lads are putting together a fishing competition. And since we like you, my Lords, we thought we'd invite you.

Next1.text: We know you're quite busy, so if you don't want to come, we understand.

line0.props.tipText: Promise the residents that you'll send a few Companions.

line1.props.tipText: Decline the invitation, but thank the residents for thinking of you.

line2.props.tipText: Throw these troublemakers in prison. You never authorised any fishing competition!

Start.text: Our informants among the population are quite certain: there's a revolt brewing. They haven't identified any leaders, but a few random hangings should be enough to bring the people back to their senses.

line0.props.tipText: Authorise the Militia to terrorise the populace.

line1.props.tipText: Ask the Militia to continue their investigation and arrest the leaders.

line2.props.tipText: Give a speech to the people to quell the discontent.

Start.text: Our harvests are good. Through our efforts, your subjects are eating their fill.

Next1.text: So, my Lords, with the Sheep Festival coming up, we were wondering if you might help us with the celebrations... as a sort of thank you, so t'speak...

line0.props.tipText: Agree to give the people what they need to celebrate the Sheep Festival.

line1.props.tipText: Send the peasants back to work.

Start.text: Your militiamen are a load of drunks! Good-for-nothings who spend more time drinking than guarding!

Next1.text: Sure, they're always there to help celebrate your Fief's prosperity... But when the time comes to defend our warehouses, your sellswords are so drunk that the thieves don't even bother running!

line0.props.tipText: Prohibit the Militia from drinking on duty.

line1.props.tipText: Your militiamen have every right to relax.

Start.text: Your management of this domain is quite impressive! Your residents eat their fill, sleep soundly, enjoy riches that some nobles couldn't even dream of, and most surprising of all, some can even read halfway decently!

Next1.text: It's only fair that your Fief pay tribute to you. Let me handle the preparations. It will be magnificent!

line0.props.tipText: Hold a festival in your honour.

line1.props.tipText: A festival would risk disrupting the management of your Fief.

Start.text: Please, this slaughter must be stopped! Your Farmers are felling every tree they find without performing any sort of ritual! The Tules will be furious!

line0.props.tipText: Suspend the construction of new districts until the proper rituals are performed.

line1.props.tipText: Throw this heretic out. The Tules aren't even real!

Start.text: My husband had a terrible fall whilst helping to build your new district. He survived, Saint Eleor be praised, but he can't get around on his own any more. What will become of us without his wages?

line0.props.tipText: Take care of the disabled and their families.

line1.props.tipText: Give this poor woman a bit of gold.

line2.props.tipText: The residents of your Fief must learn to stand on their own two feet.

Start.text: With no place for your population to pray or worship, the plague of heresy could spread at any time. Your Fief could fall prey to decadence, my Lords!

Next1.text: Preserve the faith! Preserve public order!

line0.props.tipText: Promise to build a church.

line1.props.tipText: Other buildings must be built first.

Start.text: It's all got to stop! Absolutely everything! No more construction! Nothing! Until further notice!

Next1.text: We've found traces of an Ancient site just beneath this Fief! With any luck, it could be the home town of Dagan the artist. What a discovery that would be!

Next2.text: I beg of you, my Lords! You must understand the importance of our work. Give us time to excavate the relics before they're buried forever under some miserable gambling den!

line0.props.tipText: Agree not to build anything else until the Scholars have finished their digs.

line1.props.tipText: Nothing shall prevent your Fief's development, not even the Ancients.

Start.text: Your city is certainly quaint, that much is true. Every shanty, every square seems to have been placed at the spontaneous whims of your residents. It all adds up to a very... modern look.

Next1.text: And yet, my Lords, I think that some of your subjects may desire a return to greater order and tradition. Perhaps in separate districts, to avoid inconveniencing the other residents of your Fief.

Next2.text: In a word, we nobles would like more elegant homes.

line0.props.tipText: Create homes for your noblest residents.

line1.props.tipText: The nobles can build the homes they want – at their own expense.

line2.props.tipText: All of your residents are housed on an equal basis.

Start.text: The General's birthday is coming up, but I haven't noticed any preparations here. Might I suggest that you hurry? You will never be Edoran's ally if your emissaries show up in the capital empty-handed.

line0.props.tipText: Prepare a gift for the General.

line1.props.tipText: Expel the Ambassador. You won't bend to the General's whims!

Start.text: The clans of Harag are too proud to ask for your help, but I don't share their misgivings!

Next1.text: Swamp fever is ravaging the clans, and we don't have enough Druids and Apothecaries to confront the full scale of the epidemic. I beg of you, my Lords, please help your neighbours.

line0.props.tipText: Your Apothecaries will prepare something to care for the people of Harag.

line1.props.tipText: Let the clans figure it out for themselves.

Start.text: It goes without saying that the Kingdom of Alazar sees your Fief as the trading partner it's been lacking.

Next1.text:
But since Alazar is not Gosenberg, its king requires more than a flourishing economy to consider you an ally.
The people of the north care more for Knowledge than for Krowns...

line0.props.tipText: Show Alazar the extent of your Knowledge.

line1.props.tipText: Alazar will have to settle for a trading partner.

Start.text:
Have you ever heard of the Arena Clash?
Bah! What am I saying?! Of course you have! You're people of culture!

Next1.text: Well, it seems that this year, there's a bit of uncertainty about the planning for Gosenberg's most eagerly-awaited tournament. The vineyard harvests in Vertruse have been disappointing, to say the least, and the Broker Council fears that Grinmeer's won't be enough to quench the spectators' thirst.

Next2.text: The Brokers would greatly appreciate it if their preferred trading partner – in other words, you – would graciously provide them with the drink their people require. What say you, my Lords?

line0.props.tipText: Agree to produce wine for Gosenberg.

line1.props.tipText: It won't do the citizens of Gosenberg any harm to drink water for a change.

Start.text: Do you know what I heard just this morning from some Vertrusian merchants?

Next1.text: Well, I'll tell you!

Next2.text: The Smugglers are out there selling “Mount Altis silks”! They're passing off rough fabrics from Tiltren as your residents' creations! They're getting rich off our backs and damaging our reputation! This cannot stand!

line0.props.tipText: Agree to send Mercenaries.

line1.props.tipText: Your Troop will personally handle these freeloaders.

line2.props.tipText: This is a problem for the Vertrusians to deal with.

Start.text: Oh my Lords, how happy I am to live in your Fief! I've long suffered under the tolerance of those other hypocritical lords! Oh! Cursed be those heretics who claim to revere the God of Light, but allow the common rabble to worship the Tules.

Next1.text: Allow me to offer my assistance: I shall guide you on the path of faith. Together, we will make Mount Altis a holy land.

line0.props.tipText: Accept the priest's help.

line1.props.tipText: Let the people be free to practise any religion they choose.

Start.text:
I've heard that you asked the Tules' permission before felling the trees in their domain. Is that true?
And the temple that you've dedicated to the little gods... did you really build it yourselves?

Next1.text:
Oh! Thanks be to the Ancients! You are of our tribe, my Lords!
Let us make this Fief the refuge of the true gods! Let us help outsiders to meet them!

line0.props.tipText: Accept the Druid's help.

line1.props.tipText: The people are free to practise any religion they choose.

Start.text:
Oh! What a handsome horse!
What's it doing here?

line0.props.tipText: Send to the stables.

line1.props.tipText: Appoint as general.

Start.text: My Lords! This situation simply can't be allowed to continue. All these ruffians roaming hither and yon through your Fief, rowdy and inebriated, and shouting their inanities under the very windows of our Academy! How are our students meant to concentrate?

line0.props.tipText: Ask the Militia to calm the Bandits down.

line1.props.tipText: The Scholars will just have to get used to the noise.

Start.text: What a pleasure to see noble lords like yourselves welcoming our activities with open arms!

Next1.text: Once I learned of your interest, I hurried here in hopes of offering my humble services.

line0.props.tipText: Hire the Baron as an advisor.

line1.props.tipText: Refuse to form an alliance with the Black Market.

Start.text: Though I've dedicated my whole life to Knowledge, I find no words strong enough to express the pride you've inspired in me.

Next1.text: When I left Alazar, I never dreamed I'd find lords this dedicated to the search for the Truth and the Mysteries of this world. Yet find you I did!

Next2.text: You have made this place a great centre of Knowledge, a lighthouse in the gloom of ignorance and obscurantism. My Lords, your Scholars and I are ready to govern for you.

line0.props.tipText: Celebrate the triumph of Knowledge

Start.text: Are you aware of what's going on in the cemetery? Did you authorise this?

Next1.text: It's your Scholars! They're sneaking around the graves like vultures and digging up our recently buried dead!

Next2.text: Have they lost all sense of what's sacred? What sort of Knowledge are they after in there?

line0.props.tipText: No Knowledge can justify disturbing the sleep of the dead.

line1.props.tipText: Knowledge should be gathered by any means necessary.

Start.text: We like your Scholars, my Lords. They're lovely neighbours, they don't make much noise, and they always say hello, but...

Next1.text: They stick their noses into everything! First we're not using the right tool, then we're not working efficiently enough, then the Blacksmiths shouldn't do this, and the Merchants should do that...

Next2.text: We can't take it any more! You've got to explain to them that we know what we're doing! Tell them to stay in their libraries!

line0.props.tipText: Ask the Scholars to stop meddling in other residents' affairs.

line1.props.tipText: The Scholars can bring improvements in many different domains, and the peasants should welcome that.

Start.text: All my wine... lost! Spilt out over the stones of the market square. Barrels that I brought here from Gosenberg at great expense!

Next1.text: Why? Because your residents are the worst sort of brutes! In their admiration for your Mercenaries and Militia, they seek out any opportunity to fight. One wrong look or one ill-chosen word, and they smash everything in their path.

line0.props.tipText: The Militia and Mercenaries shouldn't be role models for the residents.

line1.props.tipText: There's nothing wrong with settling conflicts on their own.

Start.text: Your Merchants are thieves! Not only do they enrich themselves on our backs, but they sell our products for much more than they're worth!

Next1.text: It's unbelievable! Yesterday I sold one of those troublemakers a leg of lamb, then saw it on sale for three times the price in another district!

line0.props.tipText: Goods will be regulated and the profits will be shared with the producers.

line1.props.tipText: It's up to the customers and producers to be more cautious.

Start.text: It was an honour to serve you, my Lords. I'll never forget my time in your Militia.

Next1.text: Oh! No! I'm not leaving the Fief! One of your Merchants has hired me, the one who sells fabrics from Vertruse. I work for him now.

line0.props.tipText: Forbid the Merchants from maintaining private Militias.

line1.props.tipText: Allow the Merchants to defend themselves.

Start.text: My cart got bogged down in your damned alleyways. Completely stuck in the ruts. And while I was off looking for help, a group of troublemakers ran off with my cargo!

Next1.text: I demand compensation!

line0.props.tipText: Send the Militia to track down the thieves.

line1.props.tipText: Have the worst streets in the Fief paved to avoid future incidents.

line2.props.tipText: Expel this impudent fool from your Throne Room.

Start.text: Finding homes for the influx of new residents has been no easy task, my Lords! As an alderman, I've had to show quite a bit of cunning and creativity!

Next1.text: Unfortunately, all of these new shanties might possibly be made entirely of wood and straw. To save time, you see?

Next2.text: I worry they might pose a bit of a fire hazard...

line0.props.tipText: Demolish the shanties and rebuild them with stone..

line1.props.tipText: Prevent fires by prohibiting residents from lighting candles in their shanties.

line2.props.tipText: The residents will just have to be careful.

Start.text: This prohibition is unacceptable! How can our Scholars study without candlelight? Do you think Knowledge can wait for daybreak?

line0.props.tipText: Allow residents to light their homes with candles.

line1.props.tipText: Knowledge isn't worth risking a fire.

line2.props.tipText: Demolish the shanties and rebuild them with stone, then allow the use of fire.

Start.text: You summoned me, my Lords? Is this about the recent fire?

Next1.text: I'm afraid that candlelight and straw roofs are a dangerous combination. Might I suggest that you either ban the one, or rebuild the other?

line0.props.tipText: Demolish the shanties and rebuild them with stone..

line1.props.tipText: Prevent fires by prohibiting residents from lighting candles in their shanties.

line2.props.tipText: None of these solutions are appropriate.

Start.text: As soon as we first met, my Lords, I knew we were cut from the same cloth. I trusted you immediately. And how right I was, by Saint Lenaid!

Next1.text: You have made this Fief into a land of plenty! We're as rich as the Brokers! Even Gosenberg City pales in comparison to your fortune!

Next2.text: The merchants of your Fief are more eager to follow you than ever, and to provide you with their best advice.

line0.props.tipText: Celebrate the Fief's newfound wealth.

Start.text: When you knocked off that old fool Alvrick, I thought you wanted to turn this ruin into another kingdom full of Guards and good people...

Next1.text: But in the end, you've made it a place of vice and debauchery. Ha! You certainly kept your cards close to your chest, Mercenaries|

Next2.text: Every Bandit I know would sell their soul to work under your command. So don't miss your chance to command them! You're the new Baron.

line0.props.tipText: Descend into crime.

Start.text: You've restored Old Mount Altis Fortress to its former glory! Not since the Edoranian War have these walls stood so tall!

Next1.text: My Lords, any soldier would be proud to serve leaders like yourselves. Thanks to you, our modest Militia has grown as powerful as an army. In years to come, it will surely rival the Legion itself.

Next2.text: Allow me to assure you of your Militia's and Mercenaries' undying support.

line0.props.tipText: Celebrate the Fief's military might.

Start.text:
Tavern Keeper, would you be so kind as to show these peasants out?
I don't care for their smell.

line0.props.tipText: Ban Peasants from the Tavern.

line0.text: No Farmers for ::vars.days:: Shifts.

line1.props.tipText: Ban Nobles from the Tavern.
