LycanBomb.name: Wolfkiller Bomblet
LycanBomb.desc: Due to their extraordinary abilities, lycanthropes are more sensitive to certain substances than healthy humans.

WaterBomb.name: Water Bomblet
WaterBomb.desc: Despite the grandiose name, this “Water Bomblet” is just a wineskin filled with water from a nearby well.

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.desc: A torch that can illuminate the darkest places as well as set infected flesh on fire.

TorchRuins.name: Looter's Torch
TorchRuins.desc: Not only does this torch light your path, it can also be used to smash the heads of overeager creepers.

Grapple.name: Grappling Hook
Grapple.desc: A large fish hook tied to the end of a rope.

AxeGrappleRareCraft.name: Combat Hook
AxeGrappleRareCraft.desc: A huge hook that was made into a formidable weapon.

PoleGrappleRareCraft.name: Combat Hook
PoleGrappleRareCraft.desc: A huge hook that was made into a formidable weapon.

DaggerGrappleRareCraft.name: Combat Hook
DaggerGrappleRareCraft.desc: A huge hook that was made into a formidable weapon.

GrapplePirates.name: Brutish Grapnel
GrapplePirates.desc: A fearsome grapnel that hooks on to pieces of armour and tears them loose.

GrappleBelerion.name: Boarding Grapnel
GrappleBelerion.desc: The element of surprise can make a world of difference when boarding, and having a grapnel like this one will catch anyone off guard.

SeaHorn.name: Foghorn
SeaHorn.desc: It doesn't matter if a foghorn is crafted from a horn or a shell, as long as it makes plenty of noise.

ThrowingAxeT2.name: Throwing Hatchet
ThrowingAxeT2.desc: This throwing hatchet is both light and deadly.

ThrowingAxe.name: Ghost Throwing Hatchet
ThrowingAxe.desc: It is said that this hatchet will come back on its own to a wielder it likes...

ThrowingAxeT3.name: Rimesteel Throwing Hatchet
ThrowingAxeT3.desc: This hatchet's edge will cleave any surface perfectly, be it wood, flesh, shoulder, stomach...

ThrowingAxeT4.name: Akhedian Steel Throwing Hatchet
ThrowingAxeT4.desc: Seldom seen on the battlefield due to its price, this efficient dagger deserves better than to be used for show.

ThrowingAxeT5.name: Vairmeil Throwing Hatchet(L:15)
ThrowingAxeT5.desc: Thrown with sufficient force, this hatchet will embed itself easily in your enemies’ skulls.

PowerfulThrowingAxeT2.name: Throwing Axe
PowerfulThrowingAxeT2.desc: Heavier and bulkier than a hatchet, this throwing axe requires some training to be used properly.

PowerfulThrowingAxe.name: Ghost Throwing Axe
PowerfulThrowingAxe.desc: This axe makes a blood-curdling noise when flying through the air.

PowerfulThrowingAxeT3.name: Rimesteel Throwing Axe
PowerfulThrowingAxeT3.desc: Considered barbaric in Alazar, the use of this throwing axe has been abandoned over time.

PowerfulThrowingAxeT4.name: Akhedian Steel Throwing Axe
PowerfulThrowingAxeT4.desc: Countless Akhedian heroes wielded this type of axe.

PowerfulThrowingAxeT5.name: Vairmeil Throwing Axe(L:15)
PowerfulThrowingAxeT5.desc: The price of this axe has given many owners pause when it comes time to throw it.

PoisonedThrowingKnifeT2.name: Poisoned Throwing Knife
PoisonedThrowingKnifeT2.desc: A greenish poison drips from the knife's blade.

PoisonedThrowingKnife.name: Poisoned Ghost Throwing Knife
PoisonedThrowingKnife.desc: A small and sturdy knife used to poison a target from a distance.

PoisonedThrowingKnifeT3.name: Poisoned Rimesteel Throwing Knife
PoisonedThrowingKnifeT3.desc: One might think that it's a waste to use rimesteel to forge a knife that is likely to get lost quickly. One would have a point.

PoisonedThrowingKnifeT4.name: Poisoned Akhedian Steel Throwing Knife
PoisonedThrowingKnifeT4.desc: Bandits like to carry such a knife on their belts as a sign of success.

PoisonedThrowingKnifeT5.name: Poisoned Vairmeil Throwing Knife(L:15)
PoisonedThrowingKnifeT5.desc: Despite its deadly efficiency, assassins are often reluctant to use this knife. Few blacksmiths craft them, making it easy to track where they come from.

ThrowingKnifeIR2.name: Beast's Throwing Knife
ThrowingKnifeIR2.desc: The thrower generally feels great relief as soon as this knife leaves their hand.

ThrowingKnifeT2.name: Throwing Knife
ThrowingKnifeT2.desc: This knife is both light and sharp.

ThrowingKnife.name: Ghost Throwing Knife
ThrowingKnife.desc: Many careless warriors lost fingers because these weapons.

ThrowingKnifeT3.name: Rimesteel Throwing Knife
ThrowingKnifeT3.desc: The sound this knife makes when it flies through the air is called requiem.

ThrowingKnifeT4.name: Akhedian Steel Throwing Knife
ThrowingKnifeT4.desc: Some believe throwing weapons are dishonourable, but many would be tempted to make an exception for a knife like this.

ThrowingKnifeT5.name: Vairmeil Throwing Knife(L:15)
ThrowingKnifeT5.desc: This exceptionally light knife can be thrown at astonishing speeds.

ThrowingSickleT2.name: Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSickleT2.desc: With its light-weight, curved blade, this sickle can cut off hands as easily as it cuts grass.

ThrowingSickle.name: Ghost Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSickle.desc: This flexible and sharp blade has already proven its worth.

ThrowingSickleT3.name: Rimesteel Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSickleT3.desc: Crafted from precious metal, this sickle barely resembles its farming implement forebear.

ThrowingSickleT4.name: Akhedian Steel Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSickleT4.desc: To a farmer, it would seem crazy to forge a simple sickle using such a precious metal. But this is not a simple sickle...

ThrowingSickleT5.name: Vairmeil Throwing Sickle(L:15)
ThrowingSickleT5.desc: By the time you see this sickle slicing through the air, it’s already too late.

ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT2.name: Petrifying Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT2.desc: This sickle is coated with a poison that can petrify the soul of its target.

ThrowingSicklePetrifying.name: Petrifying Ghost Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSicklePetrifying.desc: This sickle could be mistaken for a humble tool, if it wasn't dripping with poison.

ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT3.name: Petrifying Rimesteel Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT3.desc: Rimesteel's colour pops out when covered in poison.

ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT4.name: Petrifying Akhedian Steel Throwing Sickle
ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT4.desc: This amazing sickle is forged from steel of outstanding quality and coated in a most devious poison.

ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT5.name: Petrifying Vairmeil Throwing Sickle(L:15)
ThrowingSicklePetrifyingT5.desc: You really have to despise your opponent to add poison to a weapon already reinforced with vairmeil.

SwampFlask.name: Swamp Flask
SwampFlask.desc: A flask filled with a nauseating liquid.

HaragConcoction.name: Harag Concoction
HaragConcoction.desc: A vial containing a foul smelling liquid, designed to keep Harag swamp mosquitoes away.

ThrowingLegendaryArenaA1.name: Faithless
ThrowingLegendaryArenaA1.desc: This throwing axe was custom-made for Lisbeth. It will never fit another warrior's hand as perfectly as hers.

ThrowingLegendaryArenaA.name: Faithless
ThrowingLegendaryArenaA.desc: This throwing axe was custom-made for Lisbeth. It will never fit another warrior's hand as perfectly as hers.

ThrowingLegendaryArenaAR.name: Faithless - Billet
ThrowingLegendaryArenaAR.desc: The workpiece required to craft the special weapon.

ThrowingAxeLegendary01.name: Solar
ThrowingAxeLegendary01.desc: This throwing axe was created after an encounter between the Trackers and the Beast. Rumour has it that the names engraved on its shaft are those of Mercenaries who came to their aid.

ThrowingAxeLegendary02.name: Progress
ThrowingAxeLegendary02.desc: Professor Winfrith and his scholars were able to create this shield thanks to the artefacts found in the Ludern Tomb.

BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT2.name: Common Throwing Weapons
BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT2.desc: Learn the following <narrator>Special Throwing Weapon</narrator> blueprints:

BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT3.name: Unusual Throwing Weapons
BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT3.desc: Learn the following <narrator>Special Throwing Weapon</narrator> blueprints:

BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT4.name: Rare Throwing Weapons
BundleThrowingLeftHandSpecialT4.desc: Learn the following <narrator>Special Throwing Weapon</narrator> blueprints:

HeavyArmorCommonGeneric.name: Battleplate
HeavyArmorCommonGeneric.desc: This armour has few downsides apart from its weight.

HeavyArmorCommonLegion.name: Legion Segmenta
HeavyArmorCommonLegion.desc: This armour was originally reserved for captains, but they are now also widely used by the Legion's heavy fighters.

HeavyArmorCommonDeserters.name: Deserter's Plate Armour
HeavyArmorCommonDeserters.desc: The rattling sound this armour makes when the wearer walks can be very irksome after a while.

HeavyArmorCommonGuard.name: Guard Battleplate
HeavyArmorCommonGuard.desc: This armour inspires respect in some, and anger and resentment in others.

HeavyArmorUncoGuard.name: Knight's Battleplate
HeavyArmorUncoGuard.desc: This armour is a source of pride for those who procured it lawfully.

HeavyArmorCommonAlazar.name: Alazarian Battleplate
HeavyArmorCommonAlazar.desc: Alazar is famed not only for its quality ore, but also for its excellent blacksmiths: this armour is beyond compare.

HeavyArmorCommonSkelmar.name: Skelmar Breastplate
HeavyArmorCommonSkelmar.desc: This breastplate contains pieces from the armour of the many different armies that the Skelmar have faced.

HeavyArmorUncoMilitia.name: Militia Uniform
HeavyArmorUncoMilitia.desc: This simple breastplate is more about protecting the wearer than looking good.

HeavyArmorCommonRoyalKnights.name: Knight's Battleplate
HeavyArmorCommonRoyalKnights.desc: This elegant violet colour is obtained by heating the steel to a very high temperature. Only a handful of Blacksmiths have mastered this technique.

HeavyArmorRareSkelmar.name: Haersir's Breastplate
HeavyArmorRareSkelmar.desc: The face of the god of death is engraved on the front plate of this armour. It looks a lot like the Beast.

HeavyArmorUncoAlazar.name: Valuable Alazarian Battleplate
HeavyArmorUncoAlazar.desc: As one would be hard-pressed to improve upon the Alazarian battleplate, the craftsman merely added nicer-looking fur and used a higher quality dye.

HeavyArmorRareAlazar.name: Elite Alazarian Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareAlazar.desc: As one would be hard-pressed to improve upon the Alazarian battleplate, the craftsman merely added nicer-looking fur and used a higher quality dye.

HeavyArmorCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Segmenta
HeavyArmorCommonInquisition.desc: This sinister armour blends in with the night and glimmers in the sunlight, terrifying when you hear it, frightening when you see it.

HeavyArmorUncoInquisition.name: Elite Inquisition Segmenta
HeavyArmorUncoInquisition.desc: This sinister armour blends in with the night and glimmers in the sunlight, terrifying when you hear it, frightening when you see it.

HeavyArmorCommonPit1.name: Pit Segmenta
HeavyArmorCommonPit1.desc: After hijacking a shipment of Legion armour, the Black Market and its goons repainted it all in their colours.

HeavyArmorCommonPit2.name: Pit Battleplate
HeavyArmorCommonPit2.desc: This very simple battleplate is gradually losing ground to the segmenta, which more effectively captures the crowd's attention.

HeavyArmorUncoGeneric.name: Full Battleplate
HeavyArmorUncoGeneric.desc: This piece of armour is made of plates covered with rainproof coating.

HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT1.name: Reinforced Breastplate [L2]
HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT1.desc: This suit of armour is designed to withstand just about anything.

HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT1.name: Skelmar Breastplate [L6]
HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT1.desc: This breastplate contains pieces from the armour of the many different armies that the Skelmar have faced.

HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT1.name: Outlaw's Breastplate [L4]
HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT1.desc: This breastplate has been modified to absorb the most treacherous blows.

HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT2.name: Ghost Breastplate [L6]
HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT2.desc: Many have reported feeling uneasy while wearing this type of armour.

HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT2.name: Alazarian Breastplate [L10]
HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT2.desc: Alazar is famed not only for its quality ore, but also for its excellent blacksmiths: this armour is beyond compare.

HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT2.name: Piratical Breastplate [L8]
HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT2.desc: Though rather poorly suited for combat at sea, plate armour still has its appeal for the truly audacious pirates.

HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT3.name: Golden Breastplate [L12]
HeavyArmorAUncoCraftT3.desc: This armour is a successful blend of steel from Akhed and Five Kingdoms craftsmanship.

HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT3.name: Akhedian Breastplate [L14]
HeavyArmorBUncoCraftT3.desc: Only an admiral would be confident enough in their fighting ability to risk wearing this much weight at sea.

HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT3.name: Vairmeil Breastplate [L16]
HeavyArmorCUncoCraftT3.desc: A few strips of vairmeil can be seen under the plates of this armour.

HeavyArmorRareCraftT5.name: Vairmeil Plate Armour(L:15)
HeavyArmorRareCraftT5.desc: A few strips of vairmeil can be seen under the plates of this armour.

HeavyArmorArena.name: Arena Breastplate
HeavyArmorArena.desc: This slightly dented cuirass has been straightened multiple times, and will be yet again.

HeavyArmorUncoCompanions.name: Brotherhood's Battleplate
HeavyArmorUncoCompanions.desc: This armour does not sacrifice aesthetics, because appearance counts when you're a Mercenary.

HeavyArmorCommonOutlaws.name: Rustler's Breastplate
HeavyArmorCommonOutlaws.desc: Like the rest of the equipment, it was stolen somewhere and then recolored.

HeavyArmorUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Breastplate
HeavyArmorUncoOutlaws.desc: This breastplate has been modified to absorb the most treacherous blows.

HeavyArmorUncoSmugglers.name: Smuggler's Breastplate
HeavyArmorUncoSmugglers.desc: Smugglers are fond of this style of breastplate, not least because it's easy to repair.

HeavyArmorCommonSmugglers.name: Rustler's Chestplate
HeavyArmorCommonSmugglers.desc: Obviously it was smuggled from somewhere.

HeavyArmorUncoLegion.name: Officer's Segmenta
HeavyArmorUncoLegion.desc: What kind of officer would wear the same armour as a grunt?

HeavyArmorCommonTrackers.name: Trackers' Breastplate
HeavyArmorCommonTrackers.desc: This breastplate wasn't made to protect against a human opponent, but to resist attacks from a monstrous creature.

HeavyArmorUncoTrackers.name: Trackers' Breastplate
HeavyArmorUncoTrackers.desc: This breastplate wasn't made to protect against a human opponent, but to resist attacks from a monstrous creature.

HeavyArmorUncoPirates.name: Pirate's Armour
HeavyArmorUncoPirates.desc: This armour is somewhat rusty and exudes a faint odour of kelp.

HeavyArmorUncoRoyalKnights.name: Fine Battleplate
HeavyArmorUncoRoyalKnights.desc: Given directly by the King of Alazar to his Knight, each battleplate is unique and precisely fitted.

HeavyArmorRareGeneric.name: Master Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareGeneric.desc: The weight of this armour is so perfectly distributed, it quite deceptively seems lighter than an ordinary piece of armour.

HeavyArmorRareDeserters.name: Corporal's Plate Armour
HeavyArmorRareDeserters.desc: This armour is valued more for its resilience than for its aesthetic quality.

HeavyArmorRareInquisition.name: Paladin's Segmenta
HeavyArmorRareInquisition.desc: This armour is the whim of a senior officer in the Inquisition who desperately wanted to stand out from his underlings.

HeavyArmorRarePirates.name: Privateer's Plate Armour
HeavyArmorRarePirates.desc: Though rather poorly suited for combat at sea, plate armour still has its appeal for the truly audacious pirates.

HeavyArmorCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Breastplate
HeavyArmorCommonBelerion.desc: This breastplate is very heavy. Falling overboard with it would be a death sentence.

HeavyArmorUncoBelerion.name: Ihrian Sturdy Breastplate
HeavyArmorUncoBelerion.desc: This breastplate is very heavy. Falling overboard with it would be a death sentence.

HeavyArmorRareBelerion.name: Admiral's Breastplate
HeavyArmorRareBelerion.desc: Only an admiral would be confident enough in their fighting ability to risk wearing this much weight at sea.

HeavyArmorRareFugitiveGuard.name: Fugitive's Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareFugitiveGuard.desc: A piece of armour decorated in the Guard's colours.

HeavyArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.name: Fugitive's Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.desc: A piece of armour decorated in the Brotherhood's colours.

HeavyArmorRareLegion.name: Officer's Segmenta
HeavyArmorRareLegion.desc: Worn by the Legion's heavy units, this segmenta is as imposing as it is bulky.

HeavyArmorRareLegioU.name: Sturdy Legion Segmenta
HeavyArmorRareLegioU.desc: Worn by the Legion's heavy units, this segmenta is as imposing as it is bulky.

HeavyArmorRareCompanion.name: Peacebearer's Segmenta
HeavyArmorRareCompanion.desc: The main difference between this and a regular segmenta is the flask hanging from the peacebearer's belt.

HeavyArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.name: Fugitive's Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.desc: A piece of armour decorated in Alazarian colours.

HeavyArmorRareGuard.name: Defender's Battleplate
HeavyArmorRareGuard.desc: Some villagers are happy to pool their money together to buy quality armour for their best defenders.

HeavyArmorRareFiefCaptain.name: Militia Captain Armour
HeavyArmorRareFiefCaptain.desc: The colours on this armour probably have nothing to do with the fact that your Militia captain was expelled from the Legion.

HeavyArmorUncoCaptain.name: Militia Captain's Plate Armour
HeavyArmorUncoCaptain.desc: The choice of colours on this armour probably has nothing to do with the fact that your militia captain was expelled from the Legion.

HeavyArmorLegendaryChampionArenaE1.name: Kriskhed's Plate Armour
HeavyArmorLegendaryChampionArenaE1.desc: The breastplate is so polished that arena spectators can see their reflections in it.

HeavyArmorLegendaryChampionArenaIR1.name: Commander's Battleplate
HeavyArmorLegendaryChampionArenaIR1.desc: This showy battleplate is the very definition of prestige.

HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion20.name: High Jarl's Breastplate
HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion20.desc: Sven's armour bears witness to his great wealth and power. While he wasn't keen to share the loot from his conquests, he certainly didn't skimp on the quality of this breastplate.

HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion22.name: Llyr's Armour
HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion22.desc: Llyr's armour is almost completely undamaged. His death wasn't caused by any ordinary wound.

HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion23.name: Adelbarth's Armour
HeavyArmorLegendaryChampion23.desc: A prestigious suit of armour that has started to rust.

MediumArmorCommonGeneric.name: Gambeson
MediumArmorCommonGeneric.desc: This gambeson is in a mediocre state, still damp from the rain and its previous owner's sweat.

MediumArmorCommonDeserters.name: Deserter's Brigandine
MediumArmorCommonDeserters.desc: Consisting of leather and fabric, this brigandine mainly protects the wearer's torso.

MediumArmorCommonCompanions.name: Brotherhood's Spaulder
MediumArmorCommonCompanions.desc: Decorated in the Brotherhood's colours, this spaulder was designed to put merchants at ease.

MediumArmorCommonCompanionsStart.name: Mercenary's Spaulder
MediumArmorCommonCompanionsStart.desc: Created in the Brotherhood's style, this spaulder was designed to put merchants at ease.

MediumArmorCommonCompanionU.name: Brotherhood's Spaulder
MediumArmorCommonCompanionU.desc: Decorated in the Brotherhood's colours, this spaulder was designed to put merchants at ease.

MediumArmorUncoCompanions.name: Brotherhood's Spaulder
MediumArmorUncoCompanions.desc: A Brotherhood Spaulder is traditionally given to a brother or sister on their tenth anniversary with the Brotherhood.

MediumArmorCommonGuard.name: Guard Gambeson
MediumArmorCommonGuard.desc: The quality of gambesons varies from one region to the next, subject to the local Lord Mayors' good intentions.

MediumArmorCommonAlazar.name: Alazarian Gambeson
MediumArmorCommonAlazar.desc: This gambeson may look ordinary, but the techniques used for its padding make it lighter and sturdier than those crafted in neighbouring kingdoms.

MediumArmorCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Hamata
MediumArmorCommonInquisition.desc: This amour's plates are covered in black paint that requires regular maintenance to prevent flaking.

MediumArmorCommonTrackers.name: Trackers' Spaulder
MediumArmorCommonTrackers.desc: The iron scales covering this spaulder are reminiscent of crocswine leather.

MediumArmorUncoTrackers.name: Tule Spaulder
MediumArmorUncoTrackers.desc: The owner had this armour blessed by a druid in a special ceremony.

MediumArmorCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Chain Mail
MediumArmorCommonBelerion.desc: The front plate of this armour bears the shining face of the god Hessura.

MediumArmorCommonOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Lamellar Armour
MediumArmorCommonOutlaws.desc: Many peasants are haunted by memories of this armour.

MediumArmorCommonSmugglers.name: Smuggler’s Lamellar Armour
MediumArmorCommonSmugglers.desc: The shiny parts of this armour have been painted over in dark colours.

MediumArmorCommonPirates.name: Pirate's Chestpiece
MediumArmorCommonPirates.desc: The chestpiece is the core component of this armour, which pirates assemble bit by bit as they plunder.

MediumArmorCommonPit1.name: Pit Layered Armour
MediumArmorCommonPit1.desc: Versatile and affordable, layered armour is far and away the most popular form of protection in the Black Market pits.

MediumArmorCommonPit2.name: Pit Gambeson
MediumArmorCommonPit2.desc: After disappearing for many years, the gambeson is finally making its big comeback in the pits of the Five Kingdoms. Fighters appreciate the comfort of its wolfskin lining.

MediumArmorCommonSkelmars.name: Skelmar Layered Armour
MediumArmorCommonSkelmars.desc: The Skelmar have developed a habit of tying metal plates to their chain mail. The result may not be especially elegant, but it makes the armour significantly tougher.

MediumArmorUncoSkelmars.name: World's Edge Layered Armour
MediumArmorUncoSkelmars.desc: They say that each piece of metal on this layered armour represents one enemy killed, which is, of course, complete nonsense. Although…

MediumArmorRareSkelmars.name: Ulfark's Layered Armour
MediumArmorRareSkelmars.desc: The chain mail was carefully adjusted to fit its previous owner, and each link is sparkling clean. Some servant or slave must have dedicated their entire life to maintaining this armour.

MediumArmorUncoGeneric.name: Valuable Gambeson
MediumArmorUncoGeneric.desc: This gambeson is partitioned so that all its padding won't be removed by a single thrust of a sword.

MediumArmorAUncoCraftT1.name: Padded Brigandine [L2]
MediumArmorAUncoCraftT1.desc: This brigandine provides a good compromise between protection and freedom of movement.

MediumArmorBUncoCraftT1.name: Skelmar Brigandine [L6]
MediumArmorBUncoCraftT1.desc: The Skelmar have developed a habit of tying metal plates to their chain mail. The result may not be especially elegant, but it makes the armour significantly tougher.

MediumArmorCUncoCraftT1.name: Layered Brigandine [L4]
MediumArmorCUncoCraftT1.desc: The shiny parts of this armour have been painted over in dark colours.

MediumArmorAUncoCraftT2.name: Ghost Brigandine [L6]
MediumArmorAUncoCraftT2.desc: This resistant yet light piece of armour is a testament to the artisan's skill.

MediumArmorBUncoCraftT2.name: Alazarian Brigandine [L10]
MediumArmorBUncoCraftT2.desc: With some effort, a soldier can turn their standard-issue gambeson into a coat fit for a parade.

MediumArmorCUncoCraftT2.name: Piratical Brigandine [L8]
MediumArmorCUncoCraftT2.desc: Losing your helmsman puts the whole crew in danger, which is why pirates traditionally give them the best pieces of armour.

MediumArmorAUncoCraftT3.name: Golden Brigandine [L12]
MediumArmorAUncoCraftT3.desc: This crude-looking brigandine is actually one of the best pieces of armour that can be forged in the Five Kingdoms.

MediumArmorBUncoCraftT3.name: Akhedian Brigandine [L14]
MediumArmorBUncoCraftT3.desc: Belerian officers are easily recognisable by the colours of their armour, never tarnished by sun or sea.

MediumArmorCUncoCraftT3.name: Vairmeil Brigandine [L16]
MediumArmorCUncoCraftT3.desc: Comfortably bundled up in this gambeson, you’ll feel like you can handle anything. Except maybe a heat wave.

MediumArmorRareCraftT5.name: Vairmeil Gambeson(L:15)
MediumArmorRareCraftT5.desc: Comfortably bundled up in this gambeson, you’ll feel like you can handle anything. Except maybe a heat wave.

MediumArmorArena.name: Arena Layered Armour
MediumArmorArena.desc: Only a master blacksmith could craft a hauberk capable of withstanding so many battles.

MediumArmorUncoGuard.name: Lieutenant's Gambeson
MediumArmorUncoGuard.desc: Crafted from quality fabric, this gambeson remains very effective.

MediumArmorUncoAlazar.name: Valuable Alazarian Gambeson
MediumArmorUncoAlazar.desc: With some effort, a soldier can turn their standard-issue gambeson into a coat fit for a parade.

MediumArmorUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Layered Armour
MediumArmorUncoOutlaws.desc: Many farmers are still haunted by the memory of this armour.

MediumArmorUncoSmugglers.name: Smuggler's Layered Armour
MediumArmorUncoSmugglers.desc: The shiny parts of this armour have been painted over in dark colours.

MediumArmorUncoLegion.name: Elite Legion Hamata
MediumArmorUncoLegion.desc: This well-maintained, pristine hamata is a testament to Legion discipline.

MediumArmorCommonLegion.name: Legion Hamata
MediumArmorCommonLegion.desc: This well-maintained, pristine hamata is a testament to Legion discipline.

MediumArmorUncoInquisition.name: Honorable Inquisition Hamata
MediumArmorUncoInquisition.desc: Sometimes, heretics resist arrest. Fortunately, this mail armour is made for such incidents.

MediumArmorUncoDeserters.name: Veteran's Brigandine
MediumArmorUncoDeserters.desc: This brigandine armour smells of smoke and sweat. Soap wouldn't suffice to get the stench out.

MediumArmorUncoBelerion.name: Solar Chain Mail
MediumArmorUncoBelerion.desc: Belerian officers are easily recognisable by the colours of their armour, never tarnished by sun or sea.

MediumArmorUncoPirates.name: Helmsman's Chestpiece
MediumArmorUncoPirates.desc: Losing your helmsman puts the whole crew in danger, which is why pirates traditionally give them the best pieces of armour.

MediumArmorUncoRoyalKnights.name: Fine Gambeson
MediumArmorUncoRoyalKnights.desc: Each Knight's gambeson seems to have more embroidery and ironwork than the last.

GoldMinerUU.name: Helmsman's Chestpiece
GoldMinerUU.desc: Losing your helmsman puts the whole crew in danger, which is why pirates traditionally give them the best pieces of armour.

SeaLordsReputatioL.name: Pirate's Outfit
SeaLordsReputatioL.desc: Pirates aren't particularly well-known for their sense of style. Even so, this light armour was crafted quite tastefully.

MediumArmorRareGeneric.name: Reinforced Gambeson
MediumArmorRareGeneric.desc: Along with the fabric and padding, boiled leather adds extra reinforcement to this practically flawless gambeson.

MediumArmorRareAlazar.name: Colossus' Gambeson
MediumArmorRareAlazar.desc: In Alazar, it is customary to wear a layer of warm undergarments as well as chain mail under a gambeson.

MediumArmorRareLegion.name: Commander's Hamata
MediumArmorRareLegion.desc: Just below colonels in the hierarchy, commanders of the Edoranian Legion can pride themselves on wearing one of the best pieces of armour in the Five Kingdoms.

MediumArmorRareCompanions.name: Warlord's Spaulder
MediumArmorRareCompanions.desc: Despite offering their services to the highest bidder, the Brotherhood proudly displays their origins on this spaulder.

MediumArmorRareFugitiveGuard.name: Fugitive's Gambeson
MediumArmorRareFugitiveGuard.desc: A gambeson decorated in the Guard's colours.

MediumArmorRareFugitiveLegion.name: Fugitive's Hamata
MediumArmorRareFugitiveLegion.desc: A hamata decorated in the Legion's colours.

MediumArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.name: Fugitive's Spaulder
MediumArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.desc: A spaulder decorated in the Brotherhood's colours.

MediumArmorRareFugitiveInquisition.name: Fugitive's Hamata
MediumArmorRareFugitiveInquisition.desc: A hamata decorated in the Inquisition's colours.

MediumArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.name: Fugitive's Gambeson
MediumArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.desc: A gambeson decorated in Alazarian colours.

MediumArmorRareOutlaws.name: Criminal's Layered Armour
MediumArmorRareOutlaws.desc: Good luck pretending you have honest intentions when wearing this armour.

MediumArmorRareSmugglers.name: Counterfeiter's Layered Armour
MediumArmorRareSmugglers.desc: This armour seems to have been used by many different smugglers.

MediumArmorRareTrackers.name: Pursuer's Spaulder
MediumArmorRareTrackers.desc: This armour is meant to have a single owner that it will follow to their funeral pyre.

MediumArmorRareRoyalKnights.name: Gallant Knight's Gambeson
MediumArmorRareRoyalKnights.desc: This gambeson required the collaboration of six different craftsmen.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampionHarag.name: Bionn's Spaulder
MediumArmorLegendaryChampionHarag.desc: Once the blood and guts accumulated over 20 years have been washed off, this spaulder is perfectly wearable.

MediumArmorRareFiefInstructor.name: Master-at-Arms Armour
MediumArmorRareFiefInstructor.desc: This armour's understated design illustrates the humility that befits the Five Kingdoms' best swordsmen.

MediumArmorUncoTrainer.name: Instructor's Jacket
MediumArmorUncoTrainer.desc: The simplicity of this armour's design reflects the humility of the Five Kingdoms' finest swordsmen.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion.name: Matthias' Layered Armour
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion.desc: This metal abomination has a piece of armour for each of Matthias Lund's victims.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion2.name: Alexa's Hamata
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion2.desc: This hamata belongs to a Legion colonel, and is probably one of the most valuable and prestigious pieces of armour ever made.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion6.name: Fenris' Layered Armour
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion6.desc: Fenris Dredd carefully removed all the leather straps and cords from this piece of armour and replaced them with woven fabric and rush. The final item is surprisingly strong.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion7.name: Trivetta's Gambeson
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion7.desc: This padded jacket was sewn to be recognisable from the farthest seat in the stands of Hoevendorp's Arena.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion8.name: Kogo's Brigandine
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion8.desc: Despite its faded colours and damaged seams, this brigandine has been lovingly maintained. It must have sentimental value for Kogo.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion9.name: Toro's Brigandine
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion9.desc: Albeit patched up and washed out, this brigandine has done its job for years, as Toro, who seems very attached to it, has maintained it well.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampionArenaA1.name: Lisbeth's Waistcoat
MediumArmorLegendaryChampionArenaA1.desc: This waistcoat was fashioned out of bear leather and adorned with white wolf fur, an unusual combination that probably contributed to Lisbeth's prestige.

MediumArmorLegendaryArenaIR1.name: Fighter's Spaulder
MediumArmorLegendaryArenaIR1.desc: The Brotherhood adapted this spaulder to meet arena standards.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion11.name: Eokeld's Armour
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion11.desc: Eokeld seems to have converted to the cult of Mihr at the same time he took up Alazarian powder.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion19.name: Kraven's Layered Armour
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion19.desc: Caked with dirt and smeared with blood, this armour lost much of its lustre during Kraven's flight.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampionArenaA2.name: Alfrid's Gambeson
MediumArmorLegendaryChampionArenaA2.desc: Alfrid had this armour modelled on the gambesons worn by Alazarian soldiers, but with a touch of his personal style.

MediumArmorLegendaryChampion23.name: Adelbarth's Gambeson
MediumArmorLegendaryChampion23.desc: Under the threadbare fabric with stuffing poking out and the rust that covers the chain mail tunic, you can still tell this gambeson once belonged to a prince.

LightArmorCommonGeneric.name: Jacket
LightArmorCommonGeneric.desc: Despite its thick fabric, this jacket does nothing to protect from the cold or the rain.

LightArmorUncoGeneric.name: Valuable Jacket
LightArmorUncoGeneric.desc: Made from quality leather and fabric, this doublet features a tasteful blend of colours.

LightArmorRareGeneric.name: Master's Jacket
LightArmorRareGeneric.desc: This jacket was hand-crafted by a Belerion artisan. The weaving technique resembles that used for boat sails, making this armour quite resistant to wear and inclement weather.

LightArmorCommonOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Tabard
LightArmorCommonOutlaws.desc: This tabard doesn't give much protection, but never fails to impress the common folk.

LightArmorCommonSmugglers.name: Smuggler's Tabard
LightArmorCommonSmugglers.desc: A simple, flexible tabard that's perfect for advancing undetected through enemy territory.

LightArmorCommonLegion.name: Legion Tunic
LightArmorCommonLegion.desc: Every Legion soldier has worn this tunic at least once in their life.

LightArmorUncoLegion.name: Officer's Tunic
LightArmorUncoLegion.desc: The brooch that fastens the cape on this armour is worth as much on its own as several months' wages for a low-level legionary.

LightArmorCommonTrackers.name: Tracker's Cloak
LightArmorCommonTrackers.desc: The wolf pelt is equally effective at camouflaging the wearer and keeping them warm.

LightArmorCommonAlazar.name: Alazarian Waistcoat
LightArmorCommonAlazar.desc: Fighting and patrolling in a blizzard don't preclude elegance.

LightArmorCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Doublet
LightArmorCommonBelerion.desc: This padded jacket protects the wearer from sea spray and sunburn, and has the added advantage of sinking less quickly than other forms of armour.

LightArmorUncoBelerion.name: Solar Doublet
LightArmorUncoBelerion.desc: With this doublet on, you'll feel ready to face all the perils of the sea.

LightArmorCommonPirates.name: Pirate's Outfit
LightArmorCommonPirates.desc: Pirates aren't particularly well-known for their sense of style. Even so, this light armour was crafted quite tastefully.

LightArmorCommonPit1.name: Pit Cloak
LightArmorCommonPit1.desc: The fur pelts adorning certain cloaks are the product of poaching, and are currently being sought by the Harag Guard.

LightArmorCommonPit2.name: Pit Waistcoat
LightArmorCommonPit2.desc: While some fighters try to hide their identities, others opt for a waistcoat in hopes of drawing a potential patron's attention.

LightArmorCommonRoyalKnights.name: Knight's Waistcoat
LightArmorCommonRoyalKnights.desc: Some would say that the fabric on this waistcoat is too valuable to wear into combat. But that's a commoner's attitude.

LightArmorUncoSkelmars.name: World's Edge Tunic
LightArmorUncoSkelmars.desc: The padding in this garment serves to protect the wearer from the glacial cold of the World's Edge as much as from enemy attacks.

LightArmorAUncoCraftT1.name: Padded Jacket [L2]
LightArmorAUncoCraftT1.desc: A well-crafted jacket, reinforced with leather in its most vital parts.

LightArmorBUncoCraftT1.name: Skelmar Jacket [L6]
LightArmorBUncoCraftT1.desc: The padding in this garment serves to protect the wearer from the glacial cold of the World's Edge as much as from enemy attacks.

LightArmorCUncoCraftT1.name: Outlaw's Jacket [L4]
LightArmorCUncoCraftT1.desc: This tabard doesn't give much protection, but never fails to impress the common folk.

LightArmorAUncoCraftT2.name: Ghost Jacket [L6]
LightArmorAUncoCraftT2.desc: Ghost leather feels soft, but tends to give its wearer nightmares.

LightArmorBUncoCraftT2.name: Alazarian Jacket [L10]
LightArmorBUncoCraftT2.desc: This piece of clothing is perfect for patrolling the cold and windy cities of Alazar.

LightArmorCUncoCraftT2.name: Piratical Jacket [L8]
LightArmorCUncoCraftT2.desc: The saurian-tooth necklace is authentic, which adds substantial prestige to this somewhat untidy-looking outfit.

LightArmorAUncoCraftT3.name: Golden Jacket [L12]
LightArmorAUncoCraftT3.desc: One could think this is just an ordinary waistcoat, were it not reinforced with the best alloy in the Five Kingdoms.

LightArmorBUncoCraftT3.name: Akhedian Jacket [L14]
LightArmorBUncoCraftT3.desc: With this doublet on, you'll feel ready to face all the perils of the sea.

LightArmorCUncoCraftT3.name: Vairmeil Jacket [L16]
LightArmorCUncoCraftT3.desc: It’s common to recolour a part of one’s armour, whether to fool enemies or conceal oneself.

LightArmorRareCraftT5.name: Vairmeil Doublet
LightArmorRareCraftT5.desc: It’s common to recolour a part of one’s armour, whether to fool enemies or conceal oneself.

LightArmorUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Ornate Tabard
LightArmorUncoOutlaws.desc: This tabard was decorated to excess by its previous owner.

LightArmorUncoGuard.name: Guard's Red Doublet
LightArmorUncoGuard.desc: Although this doublet is light, it is also subtly reinforced at the seams.

LightArmorCommonGuard.name: Guard's Doublet
LightArmorCommonGuard.desc: Although this doublet is light, it is also subtly reinforced at the seams.

LightArmorUncoAlazar.name: Alazarian Padded Waistcoat
LightArmorUncoAlazar.desc: This piece of clothing is perfect for patrolling the cold and windy cities of Alazar.

LightArmorUncoCompanions.name: Archer's Waistcoat
LightArmorUncoCompanions.desc: There's a pocket hidden inside this waistcoat for keeping one's earnings.

LightArmorUncoInquisition.name: Honorable Inquisition Tunic
LightArmorUncoInquisition.desc: Who needs battleplate when you're blessed by the All-Seeing Eye?

LightArmorCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Tunic
LightArmorCommonInquisition.desc: Who needs battleplate when you're blessed by the All-Seeing Eye?

LightArmorUncoTrackers.name: Hunter's Cloak
LightArmorUncoTrackers.desc: The fur on this cloak is stunning - whoever has maintained it knew what they were doing.

LightArmorArena.name: Arena Tabard
LightArmorArena.desc: This tabard's fabric is of such quality that you can barely see it was mended several times.

LightArmorRareOutlaws.name: Ringleader's Tabard
LightArmorRareOutlaws.desc: This tabard was sewn by a tailor, which is rare for a brigand's attire.

LightArmorRareSmugglers.name: Tailored Tabard
LightArmorRareSmugglers.desc: An exceptionally gifted tailor has adjusted this tabard to fit its owner perfectly.

LightArmorRareGuard.name: Captain's Doublet
LightArmorRareGuard.desc: A doublet made of multiple layers of fabric that are surprisingly strong.

LightArmorRareAlazar.name: Alazarian Captain's Waistcoat
LightArmorRareAlazar.desc: Alazarian captains wear with pride the waistcoats they order not from their own kingdom, but from the famed tailors of Gosenberg.

LightArmorRareTrackers.name: Trapper's Cloak
LightArmorRareTrackers.desc: The fur on this cloak must come from a magnificent beast and is more than adequate for a Master Trapper.

LightArmorRareBelerion.name: Quartermaster's Doublet
LightArmorRareBelerion.desc: The quartermaster's doublet has been modified to make it easier to wield a bow.

LightArmorUncoPirates.name: Hodgepodge Outfit
LightArmorUncoPirates.desc: The saurian-tooth necklace is authentic, which adds substantial prestige to this somewhat untidy-looking outfit.

LightArmorRarePirates.name: Rover's Outfit
LightArmorRarePirates.desc: The rover's outfit is made of higher-quality garments than those worn by mere pirates.

LightArmorRareFugitiveGuard.name: Fugitive's Doublet
LightArmorRareFugitiveGuard.desc: A doublet decorated in the Guard's colours.

LightArmorRareFugitiveLegion.name: Fugitive's Tunic
LightArmorRareFugitiveLegion.desc: A tunic decorated in the Legion's colours.

LightArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.name: Fugitive's Waistcoat
LightArmorRareFugitiveCompanions.desc: A waistcoat decorated in the Brotherhood's colours.

LightArmorRareFugitiveInquisition.name: Fugitive's Tunic
LightArmorRareFugitiveInquisition.desc: A tunic decorated in the Inquisition's colours.

LightArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.name: Fugitive's Waistcoat
LightArmorRareFugitiveAlazarSoldiers.desc: A waistcoat decorated in Alazarian colours.

LightArmorRareDeserters.name: Looter's Jacket
LightArmorRareDeserters.desc: Deftly patched up, this jacket is still as sturdy as it was in its heyday.

LightArmorRareRoyalKnights.name: Gentleman's Waistcoat
LightArmorRareRoyalKnights.desc: Trimmed in gold rather than being dyed yellow – just the sort of detail that's typical of waistcoats worn by Alazarian gentlemen.

LightArmorUncoDeserters.name: Deserters' Jacket
LightArmorUncoDeserters.desc: Deftly patched up, this jacket is still as sturdy as it was in its heyday.

LightArmorLegendaryChampion1.name: Smot's Tabard
LightArmorLegendaryChampion1.desc: This tabard is covered in a greenish substance.

LightArmorLegendaryChampion2.name: Kaghal's Cloak
LightArmorLegendaryChampion2.desc: Time has erased this cloak's colours and eaten its original seams. That said, Kaghal's deftness has allowed this piece of light armour to survive until now.

LightArmorRareInquisition.name: Messenger's Tunic
LightArmorRareInquisition.desc: Despite looking quite heavy, this coat offers great mobility.

LightArmorLegendaryChampion10.name: Kristoff Kruppe's Tabard
LightArmorLegendaryChampion10.desc: Despite its mysterious and sombre look, this tabard is very comfortable when you have to sleep on a ship's deck.

LightArmorLegendaryChampionArenaH1.name: Nairolf's Cloak
LightArmorLegendaryChampionArenaH1.desc: The bear this pelt comes from is none other than Nairolf's previous companion, whom he didn't want to part with.

LightArmorLegendaryArenaIR1.name: Fighter's Waistcoat
LightArmorLegendaryArenaIR1.desc: This Waistcoat has been reinforced to meet arena standards.

LightArmorLegendaryChampionE2.name: Attia's Battleplate
LightArmorLegendaryChampionE2.desc: A very thick set of armour, decorated with a certain flair.

LightArmorLegendaryChampion21.name: Valandi's Tunic
LightArmorLegendaryChampion21.desc: Dyed to stand out from the crowd and emphasise its wearer's status as jarl.

BaseArmorStart1.name: Farmer's Rags
BaseArmorStart1.desc: Old, practical clothing covered in mud stains.

BaseArmorStart2.name: Angler's Clothes
BaseArmorStart2.desc: Often used in inclement weather, these rags smell faintly of fish.

BaseArmorCommonCraft.name: Simple Clothes [L2]
BaseArmorCommonCraft.desc: Crude clothing that offers some protection from the cold.

BaseArmorPilferer.name: Alazarian Waistcoat
BaseArmorPilferer.desc: This waistcoat belonged to someone important in Alazar. But due... to some circumstances, it changed the owner.

BaseArmorAClothesCraftT1.name: Farmer's Clothes [L2]
BaseArmorAClothesCraftT1.desc: This outfit is more practical than comfortable.

BaseArmorBClothesCraftT1.name: Rancher's Clothes [L4]
BaseArmorBClothesCraftT1.desc: A crude outfit for toiling in the fields.

BaseArmorCClothesCraftT1.name: Woodsman's Clothes
BaseArmorCClothesCraftT1.desc: Such clothes allow not to overheat during harvesting in Belerion.

BaseArmorCClothesCraftT1.name: Peasant's Clothes [L6]
BaseArmorCClothesCraftT1.desc: Good clothing that offers more than just protection from the cold.

BaseArmorBClothesCraftT2.name: Peddler's Clothes [L8]
BaseArmorBClothesCraftT2.desc: With an elegant cut and made from strong material, this outfit is perfect for wandering through the busy markets of the Five Kingdoms.

BaseArmorAClothesCraftT2.name: Artisan's Clothes [L6]
BaseArmorAClothesCraftT2.desc: Only the wealthiest peasants and artisans wear this Akhedian-style outfit.

BaseArmorCClothesCraftT2.name: Scholar's Clothes [L10]
BaseArmorCClothesCraftT2.desc: Just wearing this outfit is enough to feel smarter than whoever you're talking to.

BaseArmorAClothesCraftT3.name: Citizen's Clothes [L12]
BaseArmorAClothesCraftT3.desc: Gosenberg tailors were keen to create an outfit so expensive that the poorest of their fellow citizens could never afford it.

BaseArmorBClothesCraftT3.name: Elegant Clothes [L14]
BaseArmorBClothesCraftT3.desc: The many strings tying this garment together make it easy to take off, but hard to put back on.

BaseArmorCClothesCraftT3.name: Merchant's Clothes [L16]
BaseArmorCClothesCraftT3.desc: A hard-wearing but elegant outfit, perfect for travelling trade routes.

BaseArmorAClothesCraftT4.name: Judge's Clothes
BaseArmorAClothesCraftT4.desc: Wearing such clothes is the Harag judges’ privilege.

BaseArmorBClothesCraftT4.name: Broker's Clothes
BaseArmorBClothesCraftT4.desc: This outfit is a perfect blend of good taste and fine cloth.

BaseArmorCClothesCraftT4.name: Noble's Clothes
BaseArmorCClothesCraftT4.desc: The sumptuous material is enough to make the wearer of this outfit feel like a high lord.

BaseArmorStart.name: Pilgrim's Clothes
BaseArmorStart.desc: Light clothing that's perfect for those who travel a lot.

BaseArmorSwordsman.name: Swordsman's Clothes
BaseArmorSwordsman.desc: This clothing is quite suitable for moving with a sword, but provides almost no protection.

BaseArmorCommonBelerion1.name: Ihrian Clothes
BaseArmorCommonBelerion1.desc: Light clothing that's perfect for moving around comfortably on a ship.

BaseArmorCommonBelerion2.name: Ihrian Outfit
BaseArmorCommonBelerion2.desc: Adventurers in the archipelago often favour this tough, inexpensive outfit.

BaseArmorFarmer.name: Rancher Outfit
BaseArmorFarmer.desc: A crude outfit for toiling in the fields.

PeasantTunic.name: Farmer Clothes
PeasantTunic.desc: This outfit is more practical than comfortable.

PeasantClothes.name: Peasant Breeches
PeasantClothes.desc: A garment handed down the generations until it turns to dust.

PeasantClothes2.name: Peasant's Outfit
PeasantClothes2.desc: This outfit is worn by many a peasant in the Belerion Archipelago.

PeasantClothes3.name: Peasant's Jacket
PeasantClothes3.desc: The heavy jacket provides reliable protection from insect bites.

PeasantClothes4.name: Peasant's Outfit
PeasantClothes4.desc: Only the wealthiest peasants and artisans wear this Akhedian-style outfit.

PeasantClothes5.name: Peasant's Outfit
PeasantClothes5.desc: A peasant's outfit that was kept by the Belerians.

BaseArmorMerchant.name: Merchant Outfit
BaseArmorMerchant.desc: Commoner clothes that have been mended.

ApothecaryBelerionClothes.name: Apothecary's Outfit
ApothecaryBelerionClothes.desc: The scarf worn by apothecaries symbolises the order they belong to.

BlacksmithClothes.name: Blacksmith Outfit
BlacksmithClothes.desc: The perfect outfit if you're handling molten iron.

BlacksmithBelerionClothes.name: Blacksmith Outfit
BlacksmithBelerionClothes.desc: The leather chestpiece offers protection from flying sparks.

TraderTunic.name: Merchant Attire
TraderTunic.desc: With an elegant cut and made from strong material, this outfit is perfect for wandering through the busy markets of the Five Kingdoms.

TavernKeeperClothes.name: Innkeeper Outfit
TavernKeeperClothes.desc: Nothing stylish about these alcohol- and fat-soaked clothes.

TavernKeeperBelerionClothes.name: Innkeeper Outfit
TavernKeeperBelerionClothes.desc: It is not so much the clothes that make the innkeeper, but rather the smell of grilled meat and stale beer.

NobleClothes.name: Noble's Attire
NobleClothes.desc: The sumptuous material is enough to make the wearer of this outfit feel like a high lord.

BaronClothes.name: Baron's Outfit
BaronClothes.desc: No outfit this elegant has ever looked this sinister. Or is it the other way around?

DihyaClothes1.name: Dihya's Garment
DihyaClothes1.desc: The dihyas' traditional garb varies slightly to reflect the different peoples they lead.

DihyaClothes2.name: Dihya's Garment
DihyaClothes2.desc: The dihyas' traditional garb varies slightly to reflect the different peoples they lead.

DihyaClothes3.name: Dihya's Garment
DihyaClothes3.desc: The dihyas' traditional garb varies slightly to reflect the different peoples they lead.

PriestClothes.name: Priest's Vestments
PriestClothes.desc: Cut from the humblest of materials, this dress is one of the most prestigious outfits in the Five Kingdoms.

PriestReward.name: Vestments of Saint Lenaid
PriestReward.desc: Cut from the humblest of materials, this dress is one of the most prestigious outfits in the Five Kingdoms.

PriestHessuraClothes.name: Priest's Vestments
PriestHessuraClothes.desc: Only the priests of the god Hessura have the honour of wearing these vestments.

PriestMihrClothes.name: Priest's Vestments
PriestMihrClothes.desc: The colours of these vestments are indubitably those of the goddess Mirh.

JudgeClothes.name: Judge's Attire
JudgeClothes.desc: Wearing a ghost monster's fur is the Harag judges’ privilege.

JudgeReward.name: Harag Attire
JudgeReward.desc: Wearing a ghost monster's fur is the Harag judges’ privilege.

RagsClothes.name: Rags
RagsClothes.desc: These clothes are little more than rags.

TumblerClothes.name: Theatrical Costume
TumblerClothes.desc: A sight to behold, this colourful minstrel costume is worn by many an artist, from bear tamers to actors.

PuzzleManClothes.name: The Great Solveriser's Attire
PuzzleManClothes.desc: This ornate outfit is most appealing when worn by the great Solvius himself.

ScholarClothes.name: Scholar's Garb
ScholarClothes.desc: Just wearing this outfit is enough to feel smarter than whoever you're talking to.

ScholarBelerionClothes.name: Scholar's Outfit
ScholarBelerionClothes.desc: So common at the Great Library that you'd think it was a uniform, this Scholar's outfit is only for those who have dedicated their lives to the pursuit of knowledge.

NobleNegociant.name: Broker Outfit
NobleNegociant.desc: This outfit is a perfect blend of good taste and fine cloth.

Townspeople.name: Citizen Outfit
Townspeople.desc: Gosenberg tailors were keen to create an outfit so expensive that the poorest of their fellow citizens could never afford it.

TownspeopleBelerionClothes.name: Elegant Garment
TownspeopleBelerionClothes.desc: Only the most well-to-do classes of the Ihrian population wear this garment composed of expertly pleated folds and high-quality fabric.

TraderTunic2.name: Merchant Outfit
TraderTunic2.desc: A hard-wearing but elegant outfit, perfect for travelling trade routes.

Prostitute.name: Prostitute Attire
Prostitute.desc: The many strings tying this garment together make it easy to take off, but hard to put back on.

Sportswear.name: Sports Attire
Sportswear.desc: Still caked with mud and blood, and slightly damp on the inside, this outfit is nevertheless vital to any Rouste player.

SportswearGosenberg.name: Sports Attire
SportswearGosenberg.desc: Still caked with mud and blood, and slightly damp on the inside, this outfit is nevertheless vital to any Rouste player.

PurifierClothes.name: Purifier's Outfit
PurifierClothes.desc: This intricate piece of clothing is like a beacon in the night for sick people in distress.

FiefIntendantClothes.name: Steward Vothier's Outfit
FiefIntendantClothes.desc: This somewhat worn steward's outfit was clearly handed down from a father to his son.

FiefExecutionerClothes.name: Executioner's Uniform
FiefExecutionerClothes.desc: Wearing this uniform makes it easier for executioners to separate themselves from their cruel acts.

FiefProfessorClothes.name: Professor Adella's Outfit
FiefProfessorClothes.desc: This kind of outfit can only be worn by a Scholar who has sworn off field research forever.

FiefTaxCollectorClothes.name: Alderman's Outfit
FiefTaxCollectorClothes.desc: This outfit is worth an absolute fortune!

FiefBarberClothes.name: Barber's Apron
FiefBarberClothes.desc: To judge by the wide range of tools on the belt of this apron, barbers don't always limit themselves to hair-related issues.

FiefGroomClothes.name: Stable Girl's Outfit
FiefGroomClothes.desc: The citizens of Gosenberg would rather die than wear something like this.

CardinalClothes.name: Mystagogue's Cassock
CardinalClothes.desc: Mystagogues are scholar-priests who are readily distinguished from the rest of the common clergy by their elegant cassocks.

PopeClothes.name: Hierophant's Chasuble
PopeClothes.desc: While the first Hierophant Guillhem wore only a pilgrim's mantle, his successors have preferred to deck themselves out in more comfortable and prestigious garments.

GeneralClothes.name: Ceremonial Attire
GeneralClothes.desc: The General's waistcoat was tailored in Gosenberg from Belerian silk using techniques from the Ihrian tradition. The detail work uses gold and silver from the mines of Alazar, and the belt is from a bear killed by a master Tracker from Harag. There is no more expensive outfit in all the Five Kingdoms.

DeanClothes.name: Dean's Mantle
DeanClothes.desc: This type of garment can only be worn by a scholar who has retired from fieldwork.

Townspeople2.name: City Dweller's Garment
Townspeople2.desc: The brilliant white colour of the fabric is no accident, for it clearly shows that the person wearing it won't be working in the fields any time soon.

Townspeople3.name: Villein's Attire
Townspeople3.desc: This practical yet elegant garment impresses customers without restricting the wearer's movements. It is commonly worn by the craftsmen and merchants of Isandrin.

HeavyHelmetCommonDeserters.name: Deserter's Bascinet
HeavyHelmetCommonDeserters.desc: This bascinet still offers some protection despite being slightly dented.

HeavyHelmetRareDeserters.name: Corporal's Bascinet
HeavyHelmetRareDeserters.desc: The owner polishes the helm often - you would never guess it belongs to a criminal.

HeavyHelmetCommonGuard.name: Guard Helm
HeavyHelmetCommonGuard.desc: This is the Guard's favourite helmet, mostly because it's cheap.

HeavyHelmetUncoGuard.name: Knight's Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoGuard.desc: The solid design protects against almost any danger.

HeavyHelmetCommonSkelmars.name: Skelmar Hjálmr
HeavyHelmetCommonSkelmars.desc: The decorations on this hjálmr evoke the horns of some fantastical creature.

HeavyHelmetRareSkelmars.name: Haersir's Hjálmr
HeavyHelmetRareSkelmars.desc: The eyepieces on this helmet can easily block the wearer's vision. It's essential to have them fitted properly.

HeavyHelmetCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Helm
HeavyHelmetCommonBelerion.desc: Before the Ihrians left their frozen continent, this helm was lined with fur to keep the wearer's ears warm.

HeavyHelmetUncoBelerion.name: Ihrian Sturdy Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoBelerion.desc: Before the Ihrians left their frozen continent, this helm was lined with fur to keep the wearer's ears warm.

HeavyHelmetRareBelerion.name: Admiral's Helm
HeavyHelmetRareBelerion.desc: This helmet was recently polished and given a new plume, to thoroughly impressive results.

HeavyHelmetUncoPirates.name: Pirate's Galea
HeavyHelmetUncoPirates.desc: This galea is a highly effective method of intimidation.

HeavyHelmetRarePirates.name: Privateer's Galea
HeavyHelmetRarePirates.desc: The galeas worn by privateers are highly detailed, and have more teeth than most others.

HeavyHelmetRareGuard.name: Defender's Helm
HeavyHelmetRareGuard.desc: At first glance, it looks like any other helmet worn by the Guard, but its padding makes it much more comfortable.

HeavyHelmetUncoCompanions.name: Stylish Sallet
HeavyHelmetUncoCompanions.desc: Members of the Brotherhood love wearing this sallet, even when they're not fighting. Its magnificent plume probably has something to do with it.

HeavyHelmetRareCompanion.name: Peacebearer's Sallet
HeavyHelmetRareCompanion.desc: Peacebearers are known to regularly replace – at their own expense – the plumes adorning their sallets.

HeavyHelmetCommonTrackers.name: Trackers' Ursine Helm
HeavyHelmetCommonTrackers.desc: The first ursine helms date back to the Edoranian War. Intimidating and providing camouflage, they left their mark on the Trackers' reputation.

HeavyHelmetUncoTrackers.name: Trackers' Ursine Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoTrackers.desc: The first ursine helms date back to the Edoranian War. Intimidating and providing camouflage, they left their mark on the Trackers' reputation.

HeavyHelmetUncoBeast.name: Tracker's Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoBeast.desc: The Tracker's Helm far precedes the ursine helm, and while the latter is generally more popular, the Harag elite has remained loyal to this variant.

HeavyHelmetCommonOutlaws.name: Rustler's Helm
HeavyHelmetCommonOutlaws.desc: This helm's visor is hard to open, probably because it hasn't been maintained properly.

HeavyHelmetUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoOutlaws.desc: Bandits stick spikes onto their helms to appear more fearsome.

HeavyHelmetUncoSmugglers.name: Smuggler's Helm
HeavyHelmetUncoSmugglers.desc: Falling into the sea with this helm on is inevitably fatal.

HeavyHelmetCommonSmugglers.name: Rustler's Helmet
HeavyHelmetCommonSmugglers.desc: It is better to cover the face when you are in a shady business.

HeavyHelmetCommonLegion.name: Legion Galea
HeavyHelmetCommonLegion.desc: The mask of this galea is supposed to look like General Edor. Before he took the throne, this helmet was modelled after Saint Septimus, the First Emperor.

HeavyHelmetUncoLegion.name: Officer's Galea
HeavyHelmetUncoLegion.desc: Officers wear galeae that are heavier, but also more comfortable than those used by soldiers.

HeavyHelmetRareLegion.name: Elite Legion Galea
HeavyHelmetRareLegion.desc: Officers in the Legion are easily recognised by the tattered crest on their galea.

HeavyHelmetCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Galea
HeavyHelmetCommonInquisition.desc: Originally, the Legion and the Inquisition used to wear the same galea, but they evolved differently over time.

HeavyHelmetUncoInquisition.name: Inquisition Elite Galea
HeavyHelmetUncoInquisition.desc: Originally, the Legion and the Inquisition used to wear the same galea, but they evolved differently over time.

HeavyHelmetRareInquisition.name: Paladin's Galea
HeavyHelmetRareInquisition.desc: It is customary for paladins to reinforce their galea with rimesteel.

HeavyHelmetCommonAlazar.name: Alazarian Armet
HeavyHelmetCommonAlazar.desc: A standard Alazarian armet has no plume. Soldiers started adding them to emulate the Gosenberg Brotherhood.

HeavyHelmetUncoAlazar.name: Valuable Alazarian Armet
HeavyHelmetUncoAlazar.desc: The ornaments adorning this armet were crafted by a goldsmith.

HeavyHelmetRareAlazar.name: Rare Alazarian Armet
HeavyHelmetRareAlazar.desc: The ornaments adorning this armet were crafted by a goldsmith.

HeavyHelmetCommonRoyalKnights.name: Knight's Galea
HeavyHelmetCommonRoyalKnights.desc: The demonic smile that adorns this galea is not unlike the Beast's.

HeavyHelmetUncoRoyalKnights.name: Fine Galea
HeavyHelmetUncoRoyalKnights.desc: Pragmatically minded officers have often sought to replace these galeas with more modern helms, but the Knights' taste for spectacle has always won out.

HeavyHelmetCommonPit1.name: Pit Galea
HeavyHelmetCommonPit1.desc: There's no disputing it: the war paint on this galea is meant to intimidate.

HeavyHelmetCommonPit2.name: Pit Helm
HeavyHelmetCommonPit2.desc: This helm is a favourite among fighters who wish to keep their identity a secret.

HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT1.name: Iron Helm [L2]
HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT1.desc: Despite being restrictive and unrefined, the bascinet remains reliable in battle.

HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT1.name: Skelmar Helm [L6]
HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT1.desc: The decorations on this hjálmr evoke the horns of some fantastical creature.

HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT1.name: Outlaw's Helm [L4]
HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT1.desc: Bandits stick spikes onto their helms to appear more fearsome.

HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT2.name: Ghost Helm [L6]
HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT2.desc: This ursine helm was said to give nightmares to the Legion.

HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT2.name: Alazarian Helm [L10]
HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT2.desc: The ornaments adorning this armet were crafted by a goldsmith.

HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT2.name: Piratical Helm [L8]
HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT2.desc: This galea is a highly effective method of intimidation.

HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT3.name: Golden Helm [L12]
HeavyHelmetAUncoCraftT3.desc: Is there anything more beautiful than a golden sallet adorned with a majestic plume?

HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT3.name: Akhedian Helm [L14]
HeavyHelmetBUncoCraftT3.desc: Is there anything more beautiful than a golden sallet adorned with a majestic plume?

HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT3.name: Vairmeil Helm [L16]
HeavyHelmetCUncoCraftT3.desc: Purists will recognise the model from which the Brotherhood took inspiration when designing their own heavy helmet. Much simpler in design, it’s perfect for warriors who favour comfort over appearances.

HeavyHelmetRareCraftT5.name: Vairmeil Sallet(L:15)
HeavyHelmetRareCraftT5.desc: Purists will recognise the model from which the Brotherhood took inspiration when designing their own heavy helmet. Much simpler in design, it’s perfect for warriors who favour comfort over appearances.

HeavyHelmetUncoCaptain.name: Vairmeil Sallet
HeavyHelmetUncoCaptain.desc: True connoisseurs will recognise this as the model that inspired the Brotherhood's own heavy helmet design. Its much simpler look is perfect for warriors who favour comfort over style.

HeavyHelmetUncoMilitia.name: Militia Sallet
HeavyHelmetUncoMilitia.desc: This simple sallet is a far cry from the more extravagant designs worn by the Brotherhood, but it protects the wearer's head well enough.

HeavyHelmetArena.name: Arena Helm
HeavyHelmetArena.desc: To drum up business, arena owners display the helms of their best fighters in nearby taverns.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampionArenaE1.name: Kriskhed's Bascinet
HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampionArenaE1.desc: This bascinet was made to catch the eye.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryPathMight.name: Helm of Legends
HeavyHelmetLegendaryPathMight.desc: Only the champions of the Arena of Legends may wear this dazzlingly beautiful helm.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryArenaIR1.name: Commander's Sallet
HeavyHelmetLegendaryArenaIR1.desc: Members of the Brotherhood know their commander's sallet better than her face.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryPit1.name: Mythical Sallet
HeavyHelmetLegendaryPit1.desc: This sallet is said to have belonged to Silbius the Wall, an infamous Bandit who stormed the Grinmeer Jail all by himself to free his accomplices.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampion20.name: High Jarl's Hjálmr
HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampion20.desc: Few have ever seen High Jarl Sven without his helmet. Even his top lieutenants aren't sure what he really looks like.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryBeast.name: Hunt Helm
HeavyHelmetLegendaryBeast.desc: This helm has a reputation for standing up to any form of damage. But it's easy to forget just how much pressure the Beast's jaws can exert.

HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampion23.name: Adelbarth's Helm
HeavyHelmetLegendaryChampion23.desc: Unlike most noblemen's helmets, this one has actually been used in combat.

MediumHelmetCommonDeserters.name: Deserter's Barbute
MediumHelmetCommonDeserters.desc: Barbutes used by Deserters are cheap and easy to maintain.

MediumHelmetCommonSkelmars.name: Skelmar Intercisa
MediumHelmetCommonSkelmars.desc: The crest of this intercisa can do serious damage in close combat.

MediumHelmetUncoSkelmars.name: World's Edge Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoSkelmars.desc: A bit dented but still in one piece, this intercisa was forged by a blacksmith who knew his trade well.

MediumHelmetRareSkelmars.name: Ulfark's Intercisa
MediumHelmetRareSkelmars.desc: Made from a Belerian intercisa, this helmet combines Skelmar and Ihrian expertise.

MediumHelmetUncoDeserters.name: Veteran's Barbute
MediumHelmetUncoDeserters.desc: Most barbutes are rather ill-fitting, but this one belonged to a veteran who padded it to make it more comfortable.

MediumHelmetCommonGuard.name: Guard Spangenhelm
MediumHelmetCommonGuard.desc: The shape of this helmet would give anyone a stern look.

MediumHelmetCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Cabasset
MediumHelmetCommonBelerion.desc: This open, flared helmet is worn with a camail to protect the neck and lower face.

MediumHelmetUncoBelerion.name: Solar Cabasset
MediumHelmetUncoBelerion.desc: The Belerian Guard ask the priests of Hessura to bless their helmets.

MediumHelmetCommonPirates.name: Pirate's Intercisa
MediumHelmetCommonPirates.desc: This piece of armour is of Belerian design, and was worn by the Belerion Archipelago's first pirates.

MediumHelmetUncoPirates.name: Reinforced Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoPirates.desc: Pirates like to personalise their helmets by adding seabird feathers.

SeaLordsReputatioS.name: Ihrian Scimitar
SeaLordsReputatioS.desc: Difficult to wield because of its large blade, the weapon can be used by few among the pirates.

SeaLordsReputatioU.name: Reinforced Intercisa
SeaLordsReputatioU.desc: Pirates like to personalise their helmets by adding seabird feathers.

MediumHelmetUncoGuard.name: Lieutenant's Spangenhelm
MediumHelmetUncoGuard.desc: Lieutenants wear spangenhelms forged by master craftsmen.

MediumHelmetRareFugitiveGuard.name: Fugitive's Spangenhelm
MediumHelmetRareFugitiveGuard.desc: A typical spangenhelm of the Guard.

MediumHelmetCommonCompanions.name: Brotherhood's Kettle Hat
MediumHelmetCommonCompanions.desc: A kettle hat protects the wearer's eyes from the rain and the sun.

MediumHelmetUncoCompanions.name: Brotherhood's Kettle Hat
MediumHelmetUncoCompanions.desc: A Brotherhood Kettle Hat is traditionally given to a member of the Brotherhood on their fifth anniversary with the group.

MediumHelmetRareCompanions.name: Warrior's Kettle Hat
MediumHelmetRareCompanions.desc: This helmet's owner had to take on several missions to be able to afford it.

MediumHelmetCommonTrackers.name: Trackers' Crocswine Helm
MediumHelmetCommonTrackers.desc: A thick layer of crocswine fur covers an aventail that is just as thick.

MediumHelmetUncoTrackers.name: Prestigious Crocswine Helm
MediumHelmetUncoTrackers.desc: This helm can't be made from just any old crocswine. It has to have devoured at least two hunters before being killed in single combat.

MediumHelmetRareTrackers.name: Pursuer's Crocswine Helm
MediumHelmetRareTrackers.desc: Pursuers make their own crocswine helms using fur from an animal they killed themselves.

MediumHelmetCommonBeast.name: Tracker's Intercisa
MediumHelmetCommonBeast.desc: The little bones that decorate this helmet are intended as charms to protect the wearer's mind from the terror that comes of facing the Beast.

MediumHelmetUncoBeast.name: Prestigious Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoBeast.desc: You can tell an experienced Tracker by the quality of their intercisa. This one highlights its wearer's skill and power.

MediumHelmetRareBeast.name: Pursuer's Intercisa
MediumHelmetRareBeast.desc: It's not this helmet's beauty that makes it so expensive, but its exceptional toughness.

MediumHelmetCommonOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Barbute
MediumHelmetCommonOutlaws.desc: The spikes on this barbute aren’t merely decorative: a solid head butt with this helmet on can make all the difference when fighting the Guard.

MediumHelmetUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Barbute
MediumHelmetUncoOutlaws.desc: The spikes on this barbute are not only for show: a good helmeted headbutt can make all the difference against the Guard.

MediumHelmetCommonSmugglers.name: Smuggler’s Barbute
MediumHelmetCommonSmugglers.desc: The previous owner of this barbute painted it in the Smugglers’ colours.

MediumHelmetUncoSmugglers.name: Smuggler's Barbute
MediumHelmetUncoSmugglers.desc: The previous owner of this barbute repainted it in the Smugglers' colours.

MediumHelmetRareOutlaws.name: Criminal's Barbute
MediumHelmetRareOutlaws.desc: The original aventail was replaced with a new, much more elaborate one.

MediumHelmetRareSmugglers.name: Counterfeiter's Barbute
MediumHelmetRareSmugglers.desc: It gets hot fast with this barbute on.

MediumHelmetUncoLegion.name: Elite Legion Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoLegion.desc: This golden intercisa seems made of Akhedian steel, but it's only covered in paint.

MediumHelmetUncoLegionUp.name: Elite Legion Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoLegionUp.desc: This golden intercisa seems made of Akhedian steel, but it's only covered in paint.

MediumHelmetCommonLegion.name: Legion Intercisa
MediumHelmetCommonLegion.desc: This golden intercisa seems made of akhedian steel, but it's only covered in paint.

MediumHelmetRareLegion.name: Commander's Intercisa
MediumHelmetRareLegion.desc: This helmet is lined with wolf fur to keep the officer's ears warm.

MediumHelmetCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Intercisa
MediumHelmetCommonInquisition.desc: Simple and light, this helmet is perfect to hunt heathens.

MediumHelmetUncoInquisition.name: Honorable Inquisition Intercisa
MediumHelmetUncoInquisition.desc: This intercisa can strike terror into the hearts of infidels.

MediumHelmetCommonAlazar.name: Alazarian Morion
MediumHelmetCommonAlazar.desc: It is a question of honour for Alazar to forge these morions as a single piece in order to make them sturdier.

MediumHelmetUncoAlazar.name: Valuable Alazarian Morion
MediumHelmetUncoAlazar.desc: This morion is decorated with very ornate embossed patterns.

MediumHelmetRareAlazar.name: Colossus' Morion
MediumHelmetRareAlazar.desc: Colossi now prefer the more refined morion to the cabasset they used to wear.

MediumHelmetUncoRoyalKnights.name: Fine Morion
MediumHelmetUncoRoyalKnights.desc: The Knights often complain that the visor on this morion “gets in their eyes too much”.

MediumHelmetRareRoyalKnights.name: Gallant Knight's Morion
MediumHelmetRareRoyalKnights.desc: No gallant knight of Alazar would dare claim this helmet is poorly designed. If their aim is bad, it's surely the enemy's fault.

MediumHelmetUncoTrainer.name: Instructor's Beret
MediumHelmetUncoTrainer.desc: This light helmet only protects swordsmen who are nimble enough to avoid blows.

MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT1.name: Iron Barbute [L2]
MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT1.desc: This modest and unassuming helmet is a mercenary's perfect ally.

MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT1.name: Skelmar Barbute [L6]
MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT1.desc: The crest of this intercisa can do serious damage in close combat.

MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT1.name: Outlaw's Barbute [L4]
MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT1.desc: The spikes on this barbute are not only for show: a good helmeted headbutt can make all the difference against the Guard.

MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT2.name: Ghost Barbute [L6]
MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT2.desc: This helmet's creator used a crocswine helm as a model, but fashioned it from a phantom boar's remains. A true masterstroke.

MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT2.name: Alazar Barbute [L10]
MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT2.desc: This morion is decorated with very ornate embossed patterns.

MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT2.name: Piratical Barbute [L8]
MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT2.desc: Pirates like to personalise their helmets by adding seabird feathers.

MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT3.name: Golden Barbute [L12]
MediumHelmetAUncoCraftT3.desc: Why settle for a plain helmet when you can have a golden one?

MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT3.name: Akhedian Barbute [L14]
MediumHelmetBUncoCraftT3.desc: The Belerian Guard ask the priests of Hessura to bless their helmets.

MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT3.name: Vairmeil Barbute [L16]
MediumHelmetCUncoCraftT3.desc: Don’t judge a book by its cover: this barbute is as comfortable as a nightcap.

MediumHelmetRareCraftT5.name: Vairmeil Barbute(L:15)
MediumHelmetRareCraftT5.desc: Don’t judge a book by its cover: this barbute is as comfortable as a nightcap.

MediumHelmetArena.name: Arena Barbute
MediumHelmetArena.desc: This barbute's aventail is made to fit any wearer.

MediumHelmetCommonPit1.name: Pit Barbute
MediumHelmetCommonPit1.desc: Expensive to buy but easy to maintain and repair, a barbute is best thought of as a long-term investment.

MediumHelmetCommonPit2.name: Pit Morion
MediumHelmetCommonPit2.desc: The three claws painted on this morion are the mark of the Black Market. Most goons and fighters are unaware of their true meaning.

MediumHelmetLegendaryBeast.name: Hunt Intercisa
MediumHelmetLegendaryBeast.desc: This intercisa is worn only by the bravest of the brave. Wearing such a helmet is a genuine honour and a mark of admiration.

MediumHelmetTradePath.name: Broker's Morion
MediumHelmetTradePath.desc: Now a mere decorative object, this morion would have been worn by Brokers had they deigned to fight General Edor.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionArenaA1.name: Lisbeth's Hat
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionArenaA1.desc: Lisbeth decorated her beret with a customised brooch.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion9.name: Toro's Coif
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion9.desc: Toro maintained his coif with the same care he did his armour.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion8.name: Kogo's Coif
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion8.desc: This coif looks like those worn by peasants, a remnant of Kogo's past life.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion6.name: Fenris' Barbute
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion6.desc: Fenris snatched this barbute from a bandit who was threatening to capture him.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion.name: Matthias's Barbute
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion.desc: Matthias Lund was probably not this old barbute's first owner.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion2.name: Alexa's Intercisa
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion2.desc: A Legion Colonel's intercisa is instantly recognisable.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionHarag.name: Bionn's Crocswine Helm
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionHarag.desc: This disgusting crocswine helm is dripping with slobber and blood.

MediumHelmetLegendaryArenaIR1.name: Fighter's Kettle Hat
MediumHelmetLegendaryArenaIR1.desc: This Kettle Hat has been modified to meet arena standards.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion11.name: Eokeld's Helmet
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion11.desc: Despite his best efforts, Eokeld was unable to remove Hessura's symbol from his helmet.

OriH.name: Oris' Helmet
OriH.desc: Oris managed to reinforce the helmet for extra protection.

OriR.name: Oris' Helmet - Billet
OriR.desc: The workpiece required to craft the special helmet.

MediumHelmetLegendarySealord.name: Lord of the Seas Crown
MediumHelmetLegendarySealord.desc: Only the greatest Lord of the Seas has the right to wear this crown.

MediumHelmetLegendaryPit1.name: Titan's Barbute
MediumHelmetLegendaryPit1.desc: Dungal the Titan deserted the Legion during the war between Edoran and Harag. It's said that his prodigious strength came from his barbute.

MediumHelmetLegendaryPit2.name: Traitor's Barbute
MediumHelmetLegendaryPit2.desc: This helmet takes its name from its former owner, the outlaw known as Brutille, famed for betraying nearly all of her accomplices before one of them cut her throat in her sleep.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion19.name: Kraven's Intercisa
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampion19.desc: Kraven may have simply grabbed the first helmet he could find when he fled. This one seems a bit small for him.

MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionA2.name: Alfrid's Morion
MediumHelmetLegendaryChampionA2.desc: Though he sometimes dreams of a new helmet, Alfrid is content to keep the one he's always had and continue donating part of his wages to Sommer's Refuge.

MediumHelmetLegendaryGeneral.name: General's Helm
MediumHelmetLegendaryGeneral.desc: Rather than a simple crown, the Generals of Edoran prefer to wear a helmet, a symbol of their military authority. This one was cast from General Maxime's skull.

LightHelmetRareDeserters.name: Looter's Hat
LightHelmetRareDeserters.desc: A felt hat for the most stylish looters.

LightHelmetUncoDeserters.name: Deserters' Hat
LightHelmetUncoDeserters.desc: A felt hat for the most stylish deserters.

LightHelmetUncoGuard.name: Guard's Bycocket
LightHelmetUncoGuard.desc: The plume's size is subject to strict regulations.

LightHelmetCommonGuard.name: Guard's Bycocket
LightHelmetCommonGuard.desc: The plume's size is subject to strict regulations.

LightHelmetRareGuard.name: Captain's Bycocket
LightHelmetRareGuard.desc: This hat protects the wearer from the wind, not so much from blows.

LightHelmetUncoCompanions.name: Archer's Beret
LightHelmetUncoCompanions.desc: The plume is held in place by a wheel-shaped brooch, the symbol of Gosenberg.

LightHelmetCommonTrackers.name: Trackers' Headband
LightHelmetCommonTrackers.desc: This headband is fastened with claws and fangs.

LightHelmetCommonBelerion.name: Ihrian Cap
LightHelmetCommonBelerion.desc: Its colour is meant to stand out against the waves.

LightHelmetUncoBelerion.name: Solar Cap
LightHelmetUncoBelerion.desc: This cap has been blessed many times over in a temple to Hessura. According to Ihrian tradition, those blessings will protect the wearer from evil spirits.

LightHelmetUncoPirates.name: Helmsman's Turban
LightHelmetUncoPirates.desc: Once it's been folded, knotted and wrapped with precision and skill, it's best not to try undoing this turban.

LightHelmetRareBelerion1.name: Quartermaster's Cap
LightHelmetRareBelerion1.desc: The owner's name is embroidered on the inside.

LightHelmetCommonPirates.name: Pirate's Turban
LightHelmetCommonPirates.desc: There are two ways to tie a turban correctly: the Belerian way and the Ihrian way.

LightHelmetRarePirates.name: Rover's Turban
LightHelmetRarePirates.desc: The buckle that holds the turban in place was forged specially for its owner.

LightHelmetUncoTrackers.name: Hunter's Headband
LightHelmetUncoTrackers.desc: Hunters wear headbands to hold their hair back and to prevent sweat from dripping into their eyes.

LightHelmetRareTrackers.name: Trapper's Headband
LightHelmetRareTrackers.desc: This headband's light and dark hues help hunters camouflage themselves.

LightHelmetCommonBeast.name: Tracker's Cap
LightHelmetCommonBeast.desc: Made of wool or fur, depending on the clan it's from, this cap keeps the cold away during the long hunt for the Beast.

LightHelmetUncoBeast.name: Hunter's Cap
LightHelmetUncoBeast.desc: The owner of this cap took excellent care of it: the dye has barely faded at all.

LightHelmetRareBeast.name: Trapper's Cap
LightHelmetRareBeast.desc: There's an excellent chance that the creature that provided this fine cap was caught by its original wearer – still the best way to ensure an ideal fit.

LightHelmetCommonOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Coif
LightHelmetCommonOutlaws.desc: Bandits add a layer of leather onto the fabric.

LightHelmetUncoOutlaws.name: Outlaw's Ornate Coif
LightHelmetUncoOutlaws.desc: Martial patterns were engraved into this coif's leather by an obviously inexperienced hand.

LightHelmetRareOutlaws.name: Ringleader's Coif
LightHelmetRareOutlaws.desc: This coif is covered with a layer of boiled leather, turning a simple hat into a proper helmet.

LightHelmetRareSmugglers.name: Embroidered Coif
LightHelmetRareSmugglers.desc: This coif has been embroidered with various patterns to make it look a bit better.

LightHelmetCommonLegion.name: Legion Bycocket
LightHelmetCommonLegion.desc: A bycocket dyed in bright vermilion.

LightHelmetUncoLegion.name: Officer's Bycocket
LightHelmetUncoLegion.desc: By protecting the wearer's eyes from the sun, this bycocket gives archers and crossbowmen an undeniable advantage.

LightHelmetUncoInquisition.name: Honorable Inquisition Headdress
LightHelmetUncoInquisition.desc: Rather cumbersome in battle, this tall headdress can be very compelling when it comes to frightening heathens.

LightHelmetCommonInquisition.name: Inquisition Headdress
LightHelmetCommonInquisition.desc: Rather cumbersome in battle, this tall headdress can be very compelling when it comes to frightening heathens.

LightHelmetRareInquisition.name: Messenger's Headdress
